review_text: Terrific, tremendous food. Warm, welcoming service. Affordable, approachable wines. Clean, cozy environment... All three of us loved everything we ate (five dishes) and everything we drank (two bottles) -- it all comes across throughly-thought yet definitely not overwrought, never intimidating or imposing -- and we cannot wait to return.

Great first meal at Olmsted! The service was outstanding; they were very kind to us and squeezed us in without a reservation (but we did show up at 5:30 on the dot). The food was terrific- my three-year-old even ate the crispy asparagus and the scallops... What better review do you need? Very nice wine menu. Lovely setting. I hope they have a great opening week!

We drove in from Connecticut because we had heard such great things in advance their opening. At first you are intrigued by the living wall that spans the length of the restaurant. 

After a warm welcome we were escorted past the rustic bar to the amazing edible garden out back.  While it is obvious that there is serious farming going on there are also touches of whimsy. A Koi pond  (a claw foot bath tub) and a guard dog (sculpted from nuts and bolts).

We spent a lovely hour over wonderful wines and tasty snacks. Then unhurried we ambled into the dining room. Every table was in use and there was great music in the background, however we could still hold a conversation without straining. 

Be sure to bring a couple of friends. We shared just about everything on the  menu. And whether beef, fish, foul or vegetable each dish offered unique and subtle flavors and was cooked to perfection and elegantly presented.

Even the art work in the bathroom showed that while Chef Greg and Farmer Ian are serious about this endeavor they are having fun and so will you.

Great atmosphere, great service, great food and a terrific value. We will be back.

A welcome addition to Vanderbilt Avenue! I snagged a reservation online a few days in advance, thinking it would be a nice place to celebrate my last day of vacation before starting a new job.

Service was warm, relaxed, and gracious. The whole space is light and beautiful, especially the wall of live plants and the lush garden in the back. Nice selection of wines by the glass in the $10 range; can't wait until they have the all-clear to serve cocktails.

We started with the fried fiddlehead ferns and the oysters with the garden mignonette, both of which were delicious but not especially memorable. The ferns were crispy and grassy but gone in a minute. The mignonette was very flavorful and a bit spicy, so I had to concentrate to also taste the oyster, which was definitely fresh.

Our waiter recommended the radish top gazpacho, so we tried that and the chawanmushi, which was savory and light in texture. The crispy shallots on top provided good textural contrast. The gazpacho was bright green and vegetal and paired nicely with the sweeter lemon balm foam. My husband loved the generous amount of trout roe in the dish; I particularly loved the cubed pickled radish - overall really bright, springtime in a bowl. I haven't yet mentioned that everything is plated thoughtfully and beautifully, either on white china, or in a wooden or ceramic bowl, and includes something fresh/leafy/herby/flowery that was grown out back.

The large plates were our favorites, and the real reason we'll be coming back. The scallops were out-of-control good: delicious dry rub, grilled, perfect texture, and loved the creamy polenta and green garlic underneath. I hope these stay on the menu for a while because I know I'll be thinking about them. I was pleasantly surprised that the guinea hen was a twofer with the breast as one dish and the confit leg and morels as another. Very generous.

The women sitting next to us ordered completely different dishes and seemed like they really loved everything they ate, so I suspect you can't go wrong here. We were stealing glances at each other's dishes the whole time. This is fine dining AND farm-to-table AND a comfy neighborhood spot done very well and made really accessible. It's the sort of place to bring friends and family from out of town, do double dates (and order the whole menu!), and go for spontaneous celebration. Can't wait to go back.

This is a superb undertaking. Imaginative cooking,beautifully executed and a very good value. Not cheap, but worth it.in every way. We had superb service by an eager magement and skilled staff. It would really be hard to imagine a better dining experience--and we have had some of the best  in all corners of the globed And this is in Prospect Heights  Brooklyn! Get there while you can still get a reservation, because once word gets around. You probably won't be a to get a table
 It's really that good an experience.

First time there and had dinner & some bubbly at the bar after a crummy day at the office.  Restaurant has nice decor and ambiance, and my Bartender was very enthused and service-oriented.

The food is tasty.  

I had no service-related issues during my dinner at the bar.  The two issues I did have (one legitimate, the other small) concerning the food I tried was:

 - Price vs. Portion-size:  It's not that the food is overly expensive perse (if I remember correctly, most of the entrees are roughly $20 which I believe is mid-to-high range for the neighborhood), it's just the amount of food you get for that price.  Again, the food is tasty but it is absurd to me that you would need to order 2 small plate dishes & two entrees just to feel full.   (this is a semi-common problem I've found with a certain type of restaurant -- "Atrium" in dUMBO (which, randomly, also features a growing wall which is why I thought of it) has a similar issue; tasty food & good variety but overpriced for the portion size)

  - Apps:  This is small, but some of the app's and entrees are made to be eaten with your fingers (like the broccoli and skewered scallops), although based on the type of dish it was and/or the way they were prepared I think that silverware should be standard for them.  You'll get silverware if you ask (and my Bartender even offered), but it threw me off slightly.

I would go back there to eat again to see if my experience improves.

The food is delicious, the space is great, and the backyard is lovely. Everything else, however, was a mess. 

We showed up 5 minutes early for our reservation, so were told to wait outside in the backyard and have a drink. It took over 20 minutes for the waitress (who was very nice) to come over and take our order. We finished our first glass and at this point it was 45 minutes past our reservation time. We inquired about our table when she asked if we wanted another drink and were finally seated ten minutes later (mind you, we could see there were empty tables indoors). There was no apology/explanation for being late for our reservation. We then waited another 20 minutes for someone to take our order. I understand growing pains of a new restaurant so we were still not too bothered by this. Then, however, I experienced the rudest waiter I have ever met. My friend inquired if there were any vegetarian specials, and he told her to "just read the menu" in a disdainful tone. Thanks, we did that- oftentimes there are off menu specials. We ordered a couple of starters to split (delicious broccoli rabe and fiddlehead ferns) and asked for cutlery from a passing waitress. Our waiter then came over to our table and told us "the dishes are meant to be eaten with your hands, but if we REALLY wanted plates we could have them. Were we SURE we wanted them?". Again, yes. We asked for them. Not only do I not want to eat broccoli rabe with my hands, but I also don't want an attitude filled waiter telling me I'm doing it wrong. This type of behavior continued throughout our meal, and it basically ruined the entire experience for us. I was shocked by how rudely we were treated. Unfortunate, because the food was incredible, but the overall experience at the restaurant was appalling.

Great new restaurant! Loved all the appetizers - from the fried ferns to the gazpacho to the charchuterie pretzels to the oysters. So fun to eat these out back in the garden with a glass of crisp white wine and cold beer. Then, off to the inside for our main courses. Tried the scallops and the steak dishes, and both were amazing! So stuffed, but still ate the chocolate mousse and strawberry sorbet. Best we've ever had! Will definitely be back.

Really loved our meal here.  The garden in back is adorable, with clever little tables for your drinks and snacks.  I just wish we had arrived a little earlier than our reservation so that we had more time to enjoy the garden!  Yes, the portions could be considered on the smaller size, but I felt that the quality and presentation of the food (all of which was cooked to perfection) more than warranted the price.

I am sorry- I don't get it. We had an ok experience. Host at the door was rude, and didn't seem to know what she was doing. Service was nice, but not polished, certainly not as aspirational as the food. Food was good. Most dishes we had were just good- nothing reinventing the wheel. The Guinea hen was very good. I like the wine list being priced in the comfort zone, mostly 40-60, and the list has many good selections. I feel like the biggest problem with this place is it seems like no one is driving the boat in service. I watched a food runner come within inches of hitting a guy in the face with a plate, watched the host not really understand whether or not she could seat someone, no one really managed how the bar was sat- it was just sloppy. I hope they pull it together. I would hate to see yet another restaurant close on Vandy.

Three stars for the wonderful, warm service, great atmosphere, and flavorful, interesting food.

Two stars off because the portions are almost comically anemic. I understand they're cutting corners to keep their prices at the "neighborhood spot" level despite the high level of the cooking, but paying $7 for a handful of "Crawfish Boil Crackers" (literally just some crackers) or $11 for the Charcuterie Pretzels (four short pretzel sticks, each wrapped with a shard of meat) doesn't feel right.

I was with a party of four, and among us we had four entrees, three "snacks," and two "plates." We all left hungry.

My wife and I loved everything about Olmsted, from the friendly hostess, manager and wait staff to the lovely garden withs quails in a cage, to the glorious food. The fried fiddleheads were so tasty, the oysters magnotte magnificent, the hen profound and the beef perfect. Can't wait to go back there!

Creative, garden and market driven. Beautifully presented in a nice space. 
Food pros: fiddlehead ferns, broccoli rabe, sockeye salmon, leeks
Food misses: beet salad, gazpacho
Neutral on Hake, carrot crepe  and chawanmushi

Food portions are rather small, so either order a lot or don't go hungry!

Still early but the biggest issue was kitchen speed. Firstly table wasn't ready for 15 minutes when we arrived and then food was painfully slow, trickling out. Service was quite refined and sympathetic. 

Will give it another shot in a few months when things are ironed out. 

Should have been and could have been five stars...not there as of now.

Beautiful space, tasty food, chill staff - overall a really worthwhile dining experience for my wife's bday. The carrot pancake was bomb, steak terrific, broccoli rab grilled with a creamy-nutty tapenade. We had drinks outside in the garden first. Just two suggestions: the wine selection is so-so, and the music a bit too loud and incongruous with the rest of the vibe. Might consider some spicier, richer wines. But really enjoyed the place, am sure it'll be a huge success and deservedly so. And you won't end up with a huge bill.

Great addition on Vanderbilt!
Excellent food, service, decor and atmosphere. Plus they have a gorgeous outdoor space, which is perfect for cocktails.

Ate at Olmsted last night. Upscale dining in casual atmosphere and reasonable prices. Food was unusual and delicious. The menu is arranged from smallest portions to biggest. The green gazpacho was so delicious but not enough! The carrot and clam crepe sounds really weird, I was surprised how amazing it tasted - favorite of the night. Roasted Hen was nice size portion served in 2 parts with stuffed breast meat and a bowl of dark meat confit with mushrooms.  Only miss were the scallops which were described as having a dry rub - just a spicy blackened rub that completely overpowered the scallops. (But the corn polenta a green garlic served with it made the dish worth getting.) Bonus is Ample Hills Creamery is right down the block!

Not sure if this is a big deal or not but the other night we were seated next to the kitchen were we got to see the amazing and unique plates being prepared, which was the problem. The process seemed normal until the plates were passed to a decorator who was garnishing the plates with their amazing sauces and unique herbs. We thought it was weird that he was cleaning the spoon after every time he used it by licking it and putting it in a tin. We thought this was ok and even funny until we realized that he was reaching into the same tin and grabbing the already licked spoon to plate the next dish. We saw him lick and use the same spoon for every dish he had to plate. I would just like to say the food was amazing but they should have stricter rules and double dipping in the kitchen.

We had such a lovely dinner here last week!  The food was truly delicious - everything was extremely well prepared and tasty.  The snacks, though on point, are definitely not the best value for the money (we had two of them and they disappeared in about 2 seconds) but the entrees were very hearty.  Great ambiance, great service, excellent wine, etc.  A wonderful addition to the neighborhood and miles better than its predecessor Cooklyn.

Wow! As a vegetarian and a Bay Area native, I was blown away by all aspects of this restaurant. Dining during the last hour of service was relaxing and perfectly paced. I was excited about the new cocktail menu and received great recommendations from the bartender. The fiddlehead ferns are a must -plated beautifully and full of inspired flavor.  Calling them Olmstead's spin on a fried pickle doesn't do them justice. Though I was feeling close to full after the fiddleheads the fava beans, I decided to go for the English Pea Falafel as well and I wasn't disappointed. In fact, it was the best vegetarian entree I have had in a long time. With not much of a sweat tooth, I skipped dessert and happily completed my meal with the Rhubarb cocktail. The service was on point and the decor worth visiting for in itself. I will certainly be back the next time I visit Brooklyn!

This place is delicious. The service was top notch. Will definitely return. 

We walked in tonight and got two seats at the bar. Place was full up for the night with reservations and for good reason. The bartender who served us was awesome. We joked all night, he made great drinks - and was willing to indulge us with some off menu libations, and his recommendations were spot on. We ordered the crawfish boil crackers and the fried fiddlehead ferns to start, the carrot crepe in the middle, and the Guinea hen and scallops for the mains. Everything but the crackers was recommended. 

Before we knew it a complementary order of their delicious meat wrapped pretzel puffs appeared - something recommended but we passed on and after one bite we immediately realized the error our ways. The crawfish boil crackers were the most interesting thing we ate - think an amazing crawfish boil in a spicy chip. The fried fiddleheads were good too but hard to compete with the other two. 

The carrot crepe was the surprise of the night. I wasn't expecting much but the flavors were spot on and the crepe, clams, and sunflower seeds had really fun textures. 

Mains were both really good but for me the Guinea hen took the cake. It's served with this amazing confit that I almost licked out of the bowl. 

Since we sat at the bar, we didn't really see how service went, but our food and the food around us came out quickly, piping hot, and exactly how we ordered it. 

We're definitely going back with a reservation to sit on their back patio.

9:15 reservation, showed up at 9:10, not seated until 9:45. Why?  We overheard the hostess say that she had seated a bunch of walk-in tables at 8:30.  Excellent waiter, some very good dishes and some not so good dishes but not worth the obnoxious attitude with so many better places around.  https://m.youtube.com/watch?v=A7uvttu8ct0

Nice addition to the neighborhood scene, but not necessary as there are plenty upscale, seasonal fwd spots. which... is how i felt about the entire dinner. 

service was apathetic & very "we just opened and you all are banging down our doors for a reservation" kind of vibe. also, "you're not going to order multiple drinks?!" 

fried fiddlehead ferns & snap pea sushi - cool in execution and in design, but one dimensional in flavor. snap pea had too much of the preserved lemon 
chawanmushi was delicious but a little heavy on the truffle by the time you had the last bite. 
we also ordered mains, but i completely have forgotten what they were.

While the food was very good at Olmsted, the staff must feel that graciousness and warmth are vestiges of a bygone era.  Opened by an alumnus of Chicago's Alinea, if the staff displayed this kind of "tude" in Chicago, Mike Ditka would come in and kick their a__!

However, I was advised by younger friends that they would prefer to be served robotically, since that will allow them to remain on their phones texting and gaming.  What a world?  It's not my kind of world anymore.

The menu reads very interesting, with starters, plates and entrees grouped to allow both sharing and individual plating.  As with my experience at Alinea, there were hits and misses.  However, unlike Alinea, there were more hits at a much better price point.  The Pollack was delicious as was the Guinea Hen.  The salmon was wonderful.  Most everything else I would describe as "interesting."

Pacing throughout our meal was horrific.  Dishes would arrive sporadically, with long waits in between.  Our appetites would wane in expectation. I do not know if the kitchen was off, but I would suspect it was the fault of the service. We constantly had to flag them down and remind them of both drink and food orders.  Curt, with an attitude expressing "how lucky we were to have them waiting on us," service placed the customer last.  Why this is considered "cool" is beyond me, but I have encountered this affect in Brooklyn restaurants.  One member of our party thought it may be ageism, but I doubt it.  Snobbery has no age limit.

Olmsted needs good management to train staff to treat diners in the correct manner.  However, maybe this aloof snobbery is considered correct service in Brooklyn. If so, I hate it and will always avoid restaurants that consider themselves "cooler than thou."

I have had two amazing dinners here, and Olmsted went directly to the top of my list of favorite Brooklyn spots. We ate at the bar both times, which is not a chore, since you get a good view of either the kitchen or the bar. The bartenders are friendly and kind and mix excellent cocktails. There's a decent wine list and the beautiful garden out the back is a lovely place to enjoy a glass of wine. The food though! I managed to try most of the dishes on the current menu over the two visits and every dish was creative, well-executed and downright tasty. I will be back as often as I can make that happen.

Found the service to be warm and friendly. The food to be creative and also delicious, and the wine list to be simple, well curated and well priced. I'm not really sure what else people are looking for in a restaurant. After we were done eating we were comparing Olmsted to other places in the city, not other places in Brooklyn. Thumbs up.

I will never eat here, so this review is for the obnoxious hostess. I was going to meet a friend here for dinner. It was the Tuesday night after a long holiday weekend and I showed up at 6:40 to a mosly empty place. The hostess said to me, immediately, that they were fully booked for the night. I found that impossible to believe. Such attitude. She told me we could eat at the bar. Not interested. These pretentious places need to get a grip.

First, it's closed on Mondays, my bad.  Second, the food is great !!! Third, prices are moderate.  Finally , try the watermelon sushi!; carrot crepe; scallop dish... And OMG ... Choco mousse!!! This place has a backyard working garden making "food to table " visually verifiable!!!! They also serve great drinks: a nice wine list ...it's not a roomy place , you can feel cramped and thus the noise level can reach an annoying "black board" crank.
The Chef is a genius. Amazing experience. Sublime food, easy going place. The service was spectacular. Nice and friendly. We work in the industry and this restaurant is now our favorite place.

Vanderbilt is a burgeoning food mecca. Olmsted brings more locavore food with a veg garden in rear and experimental veg focused food. The wine list is very thoughtful and comprehensive.
The spaces on Vanderbilt all look the same- long and narrow on both sides of the street- it's pretty generic inside. Garden in rear has benches unlike the cozy seating down the Ave. at Faun. It is a good spot to share and we did.
Ate:
Green gazpacho
Scallops with grilled corn puree
Sweet pea falafel plate
Drank:
L'indigene Sufureax from the Rhone valley
The gazpacho made with radish tops served with trout roe was interesting- it tasted very green, but not especially  seasoned, the lemon swish added flavor, but not enough. My scallops were slightly spicy and would balance well against the corn except the corn had zero grilled flavor and was slightly mealy. The charred corn I had the other night at Cafeteria really made the dish- just saying' The falafel fared better- inventive and the sweet pea fresh hot bread was oh so good. The unfiltered Rhone Valley wine was outstanding. Brooklyn with it's heavy chef's cred is forging and foraging, but out of the three I've eaten in recently(Gristmill, Olmsted & Faun)  Olmsted needs additional refining of the  flavor of dishes.

Honestly I want to give this place 1 star but I'm giving an additional star because the bartender tried to make up for the extremely rude hostess! I wanted to try this neighborhood spot as I love supporting my neighborhood..I didn't have reservation was just coming in for a drink and of the bat the hostess tells me there is a 2hrs wait to sit at the bar, really, since when do you need a reservation for that?? Ok, I'll stand as I wanted a quick drink maybe something to nosh on! 5min or so a guy comes in who had no reservation but asked if he can sit at the bar the hostesses  tells him "oh, it's first come first serve to sit at the bar!" Hmm okay so I guess she clearly makes rules as she goes! There was a seat available and I asked if I can sit there she asks me how many people? "Girl, are you that confused because I literally asked you for one seat at the bar when I walked in 15min ago?!" I explained to her that I'm a little confused as to why she originally told me its 2hrs wait, she tells oh I thought you said you were waiting for someone? Ok, you clearly don't listen! She then tells me in order for me to sit at the bar I must order food??? WTF!!? Really?? Since when do you "have to" order food to sit at a bar?? I've lived in this neighborhood for almost 17yrs and I found her behavior to be the upmost rude and slightly racist!! If that's how your business runs than put a sign but don't tell certain people certain things and others something else. Ugh!!! Annoyed

I give 4 for the environment and the nice service ( new management) and the flowers on the wall, and friendly staff.
The food is over priced (depends how rich you are), and the bar tender's fav which was the watermelons sushi  was fucking 15$!!!!!

Any way, I love this restaurant/bar, because it's genuine and claimed to be natural.

Dear manager:  get rid of the Chechen cage, it's creepy!!! I know, it's  way too natural!!

Thoroughly enjoyed this place -- great food, service, and ambiance (the backyard garden with seating is a nice bonus). 

We had a phenomenal steak that was a special of the day, the scallops, carrot crepe with clams, and the gazpacho. All were incredibly delicious. The gazpacho was too heavy on the roe for me but my date loved it. 

The portions are small, so be prepared. This isn't a place you come to leave feeling stuffed. Come to enjoy some really fresh, exciting and interesting dishes (without completely breaking the bank). Your taste buds will thank you.

Just came back from my third visit to Olmsted. Once shortly after it opened, once for drinks and snacks in the amazing garden (those quails are CUTE), and again for a full dinner.

Love that I can order completely different dishes each time with the changing of what's at its peak, the only thing I HAVE to order every time is the Carrot Crepe. The sweet carrots + the sweet clams, the best.

Prices are great, 2 snacks, 2 small plates, 2 entrees has been the go-to for two people ( plus a cocktail each and the lavender frozen yogurt)

My favorite addition to the neighborhood since moving here, and up there with the best of restaurants in Manhattan and BK. Definitely up there with the inventive yet not overpriced favorites of mine (Contra, etc)

My only wish is that there was an easier way for us locals ( I live down the block) to get a table sans reservation, I have my next reservation lined up but sometimes I wish I could pop in with a friend or two on a whim without being turned away. Either way, I'm glad a restaurant on our block is this massively successful and I am excited to return over and over.

I dined at Olmsted last night and wow, what a treat! First of all, the staff is so incredibly cordial that you almost can't believe people can genuinely be that nice! We had an early reservation on a Friday night and when we showed up on time we noticed how cute the back garden was.  We asked the host if we could possibly have a drink outside first. I prepared myself for the old "well we need your table back at such and such time, blah, blah,blah" and what I got was " of course! We also think it's special to have dessert out there" Now reservations at this place are almost impossible to come by but I never once got the feeling that they were rushing us out in any way. The cocktail list is amazing. I had the the Rosemary to start, mezcal, aperol, chipotle, lemon and black lava salt and it was perfect. We ordered the charcuterie pretzel puffs to munch on and I could have eaten about 10 more. The waiter outside was so genuinely warm that I just was all fuzzy and relaxed, again,  the service here is impeccable. When we did meander back inside we had a table up front by the window. This place is very small inside and it was packed but I never felt cramped. This is what we had for dinner. The carrot crepe with clams and sunflower. I would never order this combination if I hadn't read how good it is and all I can say is, order it. It was heavenly!!! Next dry rub scallops with corn and chanterelles. Another winner. The scallops are served in the corn husks and the corn on a separate plate. Luckily the corn plate was in front of me and I came awfully close to picking it up and licking the remaining bits. English pea falafel was next and although it was served with some very interesting accoutrements, it was probably my least favorite. The whipped peas and cardamom labneh it was served with were excellent I just found the falafel a touch dry. We decided to take our dessert, see inventive cocktail list, back outside to finish the night with the tarragon which was amazingly refreshing. The wine list is short and sweet with most bottles under $50, exactly how it should be. I already tried to make another reservation to revisit but alas, nothing available. I will hit open table on a daily basis until I find an opening, Olmsted is that good.

Olmsted is a nice, welcoming place with some nits.  I love the concept and the vibe.  The staff is cordial and knowledgeable.  I sat in the back garden with a couple of drinks waiting for my walk-in spot at the bar.  I spent way more than I expected as a single person at the bar and frankly, I didn't feel like it was all worth it.

Specifically, the pretzels wrapped in prosciutto were a big let-down.  I'm not a big fan of pretzels in general but I thought that in a place like this, I would get something fresh, hot and interesting; but no.  Little pretzel sticks with small pieces of ham wrapped around them.  This should almost be bar food, not an eight dollar appetizer.  The carrot crepe?  Yeah, that was kind of interesting but not enough to pull me out of the hole of the first item.

What was good, and real good, was the guinea hen and confit.  If I had to do it over again, I would go back and have one of the large mains and a single drink and walk out after around $40, very happy, not almost four times that and perplexed.  I do like the place but the menu, I feel, needs expert navigating.

Overall, a very good neighborhood dining experience. 
 
Pros: friendly service, nice garden setting for a pre-dinner drink, seasonal ingredients, the carrot crepe (which I think is deservedly mentioned by nearly every other reviewer..), the duck breast & ballotine was delicious.

Cons: watermelon sushi is an awesome concept, but the preserved lemon was too bitter and overpowered the dish, the scallops were flavorful, but sandy, and the lack of starches on the full size plates means you need to order more than you think to be full by the end of the meal.

Give it a try if you're in Prospect Heights.

Olmsted is my favorite new restaurant of 2016. Everything we had here was sensational, staff was incredibly friendly, and they cater well to vegetarians.

They got us the Gobi Cauliflower first, which was stronger than I expected (no batter), acidic, and almost tarty. Like how it went with the cilantro.

Then they hit us with the Green Bean Frites (my favorite). Deep fried but was never heavy. Very airy and fried right so you can also have the crunch when you get past the batter part. It was salted appropriately. I had a Ratatouille moment.

Carrot crepe was very mellow. Falafel was a great surprise: freshly baked and salted pita, three dressings. The green pea paste was my friend's favorite "dressing" - had a unique, very mildly sweet flavor and went well with the falafel. Also, pea chutes.

Not a cheese person but my friend was and she liked the fondue a lot; The aromatics paired perfectly with it. Lavender-Honey Yogurt had a warm-cool vibe to it: you got to get both the cool from the bottom and warm from the top to make the most of it. Very unique.

Forgot which wine we had but it was recommended to us and had an apricot/peachy taste. Service was the best (for example, they made sure we had enough wine towards the end of the meal).

Cozy place but the wait may take awhile (worth it). Reservations highly recommended. We left a number and were called back in an hour and a half. There's some green on the wall and a garden in the back (where some of their veggies are also grown) where you can have dessert. Music had a motown vibe. Well worth the wait and was definitely one of the best dining experiences I've had in the city.

I would give my overall rating at Olmsted a 2.5/5.  The food was 5/5 but the service is definitely lacking (1/5).  We waited in the rose garden for an hour before our table opened up (as walk ins on a Saturday night) which is fine, but we were not served even water for the first 25 minutes as it seemed the waiter had forgotten to ask us if we wanted anything and I had to get his attention by asking across the garden. The people next to me just left as they had been waiting over 30 minutes for their drink. The food was very good and worth a wait, but if you want drinks before the meal id suggest going somewhere else.

Before you read this review, go make a reservation at Olmsted. I'll wait.

(You're not going to find anything later than 6 pm (unless it's after 9:30 pm), and it isn't going to be anytime in the next week or so, but the sooner you do it the sooner you'll get to eat here. And that's a wonderful thing for you, your mouth, and anyone you decide to bring with you.)

The restaurant scene in Brooklyn continues to astonish me. This certainly looks like a small, neighborhood joint, but the food is nothing short of spectacular. From start to finish, our table was exceptionally happy with all the choices we made. 

Although the wine list is quite nice, the cocktails are beautiful and not to be missed. I'm partial to The Rosemary myself, but that's probably because I'll always get any drink that sports a black lava salt rim (this is the only one I've come across so far, but I feel like I can stand by that statement).

The charcuterie pretzel puffs are charcuterie pretzel puffs (which means you should order them). They are a perfect snack. Handheld, salty, fatty, texturally interesting with a nice dipping sauce. The watermelon sushi was stunningly fresh and light and flavorful. The green bean frites predictably satisfying, and the carrot crepe as delicious as it was colorful. The duck breast was perfect, and the bit of duck mortadella on the side was a luxury. I didn't even know the accompanying fairytale eggplant was a thing, but it certainly tasted magical. 

The special of chicken liver mousse served with pickled cantaloupe was just that, special. I don't know why we aren't all pickling cantaloupe, but Greg Baxtrom seems to be ahead of us on all things food. It would've been my favorite bite of the night were it not for the dry-rubbed scallops. They came out skewered and laid on cornhusks, and we were instructed to drag them through the accompanying plate of corn, chanterelles, and the sauce of the gods. After one bite, one of my companions immediately said, "We have to order four more." After another, "This is one of the best dishes I've ever had."

And I can't disagree with him.

Was everything perfect? No. The pork collar, despite fantastic flavors, was a bit dry and tough. And my least favorite dish of the evening was the fennel chawanmushi, although I must admit I couldn't stop going back for bite after bite. Be sure you get a little bit of everything in each spoonful; the silky egg custard, the crisp artichokes, and all the rest can be a bit off-putting on their own, but if you make sure to stir it up and get the salty sauce at the bottom, it will grow on you, I guarantee it. 

To be sure, this sort of meal is not for everyone. The plates are small, and the prices for such can be larger than some might want. That said, having eaten all over this city, I've found that rarely can you find such high quality ingredients cooked with such care and skill at this price point. I feel lucky to live in a time when a restaurant of this caliber is operating on Vanderbilt, and not in some high-rise hotel in Manhattan. Take advantage.
Gorgeous garden in the back and excellent service. The food was underwhelming and overpriced, though.

Olmygoodness, that was delicious, creative, fresh, filling and so forth. Food was on point. Service was warm. Drinks were originals. And the space is well put together. Check the garden outside for a pre-dinner drink, the eat at the chef's bar (stools overlooking the kitchen); everyone cooking is happy to answer any questions (dumb or less dumb)

This restaurant will probably be a one-star michelin restaurant. The food is very creative and the ingredient are incredibly tasteful. There is no set menu, it is better to order 10-12 dishes and share them. Few killers: the cauliflower, the carrot crepe with littleneck clams, the squid salad, the pork with raclette cheese. Not only the cuisine is inventive, the presentation is unusual. The restaurant has a laid back atmosphere, the decor goes well with the "farm to table" concept. The only flaw is the service. Waiters and waitress are all very nice, welcoming and smiling, however they seem disorganized. This is probably because the restaurant is still new and the waiters not experienced enough. Although they were late on their service, they remained very accomodating. If they improve the service fluidity, they will reach the one star michelin level easily.

Have to say they have upped their game!   Though the service could improve a little the food is truly delectable. .... Combination of flavor is well thought out. I had the oysters and dry rubbed scallops. Both of which hit the pallet in the most delicate way! The price point is also perfect (especially compared to faun down the road). Drinks wise - also a good place to have a cocktail.. I had them make me my own special cocktail which they did to a tee but then perfected with their own suggestion... Good place and glad it is a solid choice in the hood!

Had a great night at Olmsted. Got there early and ate at the bar, seems like you def need a reservation. The food was really good. Had the patè to start which was excellent. The pumpkin crepe was delicious as well. Not as expensive as I thought it would be. But I guess I was hungry bc when I got home that night I ate 6 slices of pizza(I was drunk)

I cannot say better things about this restaurant other than it is truly for those who loves quality ingredients, and sees food as an art. Everything is 5 stars - food, service, and atmosphere. From the moment we walked in, we were never short of 5+ service from the hostess, to our waiter, to the random people hanging around. The restaurant itself is beautiful - its a true definition of "farm to table". Walls were decorated with greenery, and although small, the space was very inviting. There's a bar area to watch the chefs create their masterpieces of food. We came for drinks, teams, and small bites. We ordered the oysters, cauliflower, and watermelon sushi, a bottle of wine, cocktails, and finally ended the night with tea and the honey lavender dessert. My favs were the cauliflower (great spice and fried perfectly) and the dessert. The cocktails are strong, and the teas are good but truly meant for tea fanatics. Expect to spend a while here, because you will not want to leave until you not only try everything, but also  the people itself make not want to step out and deal with the other half of NY. Highly recommended for food lovers - don't forget to say hi to the quails out back!
LOVED everything about this place -- the garden in the back, the service, the food and prices! The carrot crepe is a must and the pork neck was fantastic too! My favorite restaurant in Brooklyn!

Come on folks! The food is good but 15+people sitting outside and 3 + tables empty the whole hour that we were all sitting in uncomfortable seats in a garden that is waiting zone, not eating friendly!
I tried to eat something out there and was so uncomfortable, it would be so easy to make the garden a comfortable extension with more food options and you would make more money!
Why? 
The duck pate and the fried fava beans I ate plus the glass of wine were all delicious 
But I will not suffer the uncomfortable space again
And I live in the hood 
Least you could have some bar stools for walk ins
The glamour will not last, think ahead
Because we would hate to lose you so early in the game
God knows we need a place like you in the neighborhood

Olmsted reminded me of many restaurants I've eaten in.

A small restaurant that draws a young crowd.  There's a bar the length of the restaurant and loud music is played so the restaurant is quite noisy.  There's a pleasant garden in the back for drinks or snacks.   The service was fine.

There's a very limited menu and it changes -- some of the courses I was looking forward to weren't offered.  The carrot crepe is better than it sounds but a bit too buttery.  The squid salad just tasted of vinegar.   Duck was excellent.  

Almost no desert choices -- frozen yogurt and honey whipped cream was nice.   Bread was fine but you had to request it.

Prices are online, we paid about $80 for 2 before drinks.

Olmsted is a very good spot, but all the professional reviews praising it for reasonable prices are a bit misleading. Yes, dishes are all under $25, but even couples with light appetites should expect a $200 tab with tax, tip and wine. Bump that up to $250 for hungrier folks.

Anyway, the eats!

--Oysters: good heavens whatever they did to these was gonzo delicious.

--Carrot crepe: amazing clams but overall not quite up to the hype. would be better as several small ravioli than a single mega-ravioli that's a little hard to eat.

--Chawanmushi: served not quite hot enough but still mad salty and delectable.

--Tempura scallops: expertly fried but dish overall a bit one-note.

--Pork collar with raclette and charred broccoli: a winner, served with an enchanting sauce.

I went to this restaurant on tuesday night. There was waiting for 40minutes but they have a garden in the back so we can order drinks and snack before we get the table. It was worth for waiting.

Service 
their service was AWESOME!! Especially my waitress JOY!!
She cares a lot every time we get the foods and drinks even though they were very busy.
Thank you joy!!!we were full of joy.

Food
Everything was good especially duck breast. 
I was shocked cuz duck was so tender also cooked very well!!

DEFINITELY come back to try other foods!

I really enjoyed the two meals at Olmsted.  The carrot crepe and some of the other appetizers are total 5 star knockouts, and the bar program is very good too--I asked for an off menu watermelon margarita (I was just really craving it) and they made a delightful one! 

All that said, I might consider 4 stars because 1, it is a small and somewhat cramped space besides the awesome backyard, and 2 the portions on some of the entrees and cocktails are a bit small.  That said, the food is very creative and delicious, and I highly recommend giving Olmsted a try.

I've had three meals now at Olmsted. The first two were fantastic, and the third was only okay, but the cocktails, charm, and backyard still make this restaurant a solid five stars for me. I'll keep my review to the food items that seem to still be available, though there were many other favorites, particularly the Watermelon Sushi and the Duck!

Food:

Romano Bean Frites: 3.5/5 
These were very tasty, but not particularly memorable. Paired well with cocktails. 

Gobi Pakora Cauliflower: 3/5
I found the sauce on this to be a bit too "goopy" 

Cheese Fondue for Two: 5/5
I absolutely loved this dish. A small wheel of cheese (think the size of the brie you would get in the super market) has the top rind cut off and is melted, and is served with burnt rosemary, and bread cubes, pickled radishes, and apples for dipping. I really enjoyed the variety of dipping options, particularly the pickled radishes which provide a fantastic bite of acidity. 

Carrot Crepe: 4.5/5
This dish seems to have become the "must order" of the menu, though I didn't try it out until my most recent visit. The crepe and clams are both perfectly cooked, and the dish itself is unlike anything I've had before. 

Summer Truffle Chawanmushi: 5/5
Chawanmushi is a steamed egg dish with broth that is wonderfully flavorful and delicate. Would highly recommend. I believe they've now changed the dish for the season. 

Heirloom Tomato Schnitzel: 3.5/5
A great option if you have vegetarians in your group, or just want some more veggies! I loved the concept, but the tomato itself was a bit bland. Perhaps the tomato we got was a bit underripe. 

Grilled Pork Collar: 5/5
Some of the best cooked pork we'd ever had in NYC. 

Frozen Yogurt with Lavendar Honey: 5/5
What a beautiful and simple desert. They've whipped the honey in such a way that it has become white and glossy, visually almost indistinguishable from the frozen yogurt. It is delightful texturally, and sort of toys with your mind as part of it is icy cold and they other is room temperature and sweet, but difficult to distinguish before eating a bite. 

Old School Chocolate Mousse: 4.5/5
I'm not the biggest chocolate mousse fan, and I wouldn't call this particularly inventive or groundbreaking, but it is an absolutely perfect chocolate mousse, and that is hard to find. 

Drinks:
4.5/5

I've tried a couple of the cocktails and by far my favorite cocktail is the Tarragon with Gin, Yuzu, Lime, and Soda. I think it may be my favorite cocktail of the year. Extremely refreshing and the yuzu pairs really delicately with the tarragon. It's the sort of drink you wish you had a pitcher of to drink on a veranda. 

Their wine list is affordable and approachable.

A real standout from this restaurant is their tea program. They have hot and cold teas from a variety of countries. Would highly recommend ending your meal with a cup. 

Ambiance:
5/5

If you arrive early, you'll be given the chance to wait in the beautiful little garden in the back and order appetizers and drinks. I would highly recommend this! It's wonderful being outside, surrounded by little lights and herbs sipping on cocktails under the stars. It's probably getting a little chilly now, but I will definitely be back as soon as it gets warm again. 

Service:
4/5
Service is generally attentive and warm. The waiters were always willing to further explain the dishes or drinks. 

Overall, Olmsted is one of my favorite new restaurants, and I look forward to returning again soon!

Bad experience with front people two nights in a row. Their success went to their head and they are letting inexperienced people ruining their business. 
They lied to us two nights in a row, took my cell # and never called. 
This is Brooklyn not NYC  and the front people attitude is not going to work for too long!!!
Im not going back there again. Period .

I wanted to quickly get this out there as the menu changes often.  We tried many items on the menu on 10/24/16 and had a great time! Not everything on the menu was a hit, but the overall experience was great and I highly recommend you eat there.  

NOTE: Garden closes at 10pm.  If you want smores get there early! We missed out! :( 

Here is a review of the food in order of our meal: 
Morgan's Meats 6/5
This was a duck liver mouse the day we went and I thought it was amazing! The mouse, honey, and pickled vegetables on a crostini was a perfect bit.  I snacked on it through out the meal as I didn't want to ruin my appetite for the full dinner, but I couldn't get enough of it. 

Tuna Tacos 1/5
Not really a fan.  They were very small, the tortillas were soggy, and not much flavor.  We did put the filling on the crostini from another dish and it was a little better.  

Carrot Crepe 4/5
This was good, flavorful and innovative.  

Kale & Crab Wontons 2/5
When you compare to your standard crab rangoons, they just didn't compare.  Healthier yes, but the crispness and flavor of these weren't there.  

Tempura Scallops 4/5
My husband loved these, I personally felt why would you ever batter and fry a scallop as they are delicious the way they are.  

Salmon & Brussel Sprouts 6/5
Perfectly cooked salmon, great flavor in the brussel sprouts and sitting in a delicious citrus cream sauce. 

Frozen Yogurt 4/5
Very surprising, you couldn't stop eating.  

Chocolate Mouse 4/5
Flavor was there, but I like my mouse a bit more whipped.  It was pretty hard to scoop.  

Drinks 5/5
Bartenders were great and drinks were very delicious.

Olmsted definitely lives up to the recent hype it has received. The space is stylishly Brooklyn, especially the backyard garden where I had a lovely cocktail among the sprouting baby kale. The food is delicious and creative: I especially liked the carrot crepe and the tempura scallops.  Service is warm and attentive, without being overbearing. And the price, although not inexpensive, is reasonable given the quality of the food: Apps were in the low teens and entrees in the low 20s, which is less than comparable restaurants in the area. All in all, Olmsted is a top-notch restaurant that is affordable enough so you can go even when it's not a special occasion.

Would describe my experience at Olmstead more as an adventure than a dinner.  

We started in the garden with a pre-dinner cocktail.  I had the Sage Lassi (Pisco, Lime, Cocchi Apertivo, Yogurt) and found it refreshing and creamy.  I felt compelled to take advantage of the Pisco offering and was not disappointed.  The garden was beautiful with benches lining the perimeter surrounding a garden of house grown kale (used in the Garden Kale Crab Rangoon).  There was even a quail coop with two quails inside.  

We made our way back inside for our meal.  Our waiter was spot on throughout the evening.  He was eager to describe each dish and freely offered to translate some of the more sophisticated culinary terms of art that puzzled me and my guests.  He was very friendly and offered helpful suggestions both for cocktails and food.  
We ordered numerous snacks, small and large plates, tasting notes below:
Morgan's Meats - seasonal and varies, we had duck pate with toast and vinegar soaked green beans.  Pate was rich and decadent.  Good portion size with the crackers and green beans.  Decadent. 
Gobi Pakora Cauliflower - Delicious sprinkling of sweet Indian style barbecue seasoning but the portion was very small.  Great for a snack. Light. 
Garden Kale Crab Rangoon - Felt compelled to order this because it contained Olmstead's garden grown kale.  The Rangoon had a strong but fresh crab flavor and the kale paired well with it.  Enjoyable.  
Carrot Crepe - Warm carrot crepe served over Little Neck Clams.  Beautifully displayed and each bite bursts with flavor.  Creative.  
Heirloom Tomato Schnitzel - We ordered this as we were fascinated by the description and this dish did not disappoint.  This was an excellent take on Schnitzel with the breaded tomato holding up substantially as if it was meat.  It is served with ricotta cheese, peppers, and a green sauce (similar to pesto).  It is worth putting all three on before eating this item as they enhance the flavor immensely.  Perfectly executed. 
Grilled Pork Collar - The Pork was served with cheese shavings on top.  The meat was juicy and matched perfectly with the grilled broccoli.  They should be eaten together. Succulent. 
Duck Breast and Scotched Fig - The duck was also very moist (I don't mind using this word) and if you are a fan of truffle this item is for you.  Great sauce and jalapeno on top was a nice touch. The Scotched Fig was not nearly as sweet as I had feared and rested atop some vinegar soaked cabbage.  Could have been its own dish, it was that good.  Plentiful. 

Our waiter then reserved us a spot in the garden so we could eat our desert outside.  We ordered the S'mores, because...you have to.  Walking outside after our meal it felt like we traveled 2 hours north to a cabin in upstate New York.  The blankets, the coal flames, the S'mores, the peaceful and quite Brooklyn evening, it was all a perfect escape from the tumult of NYC.  I highly recommend capping your night off with the S'more experience and trying one of the heated beverages.  I had the Hot Toddy and my guests had the Mulled Cider.  You can't go wrong with either and they are served in a thermos to preserve their warmth and add to the authenticity of the camping creation.  

Overall we absolutely loved our experience at Olmstead and I can't wait to return to try a different seasonal offering.

After reading the glowing NYT review (which gave this establishment 2 stars), I was looking forward to coming here, but it was difficult getting a table.
After a month wait, I was finally able to dine here, and left very impressed.

Highlight dishes: Carrot crepe, maitake chawanmuchi, tempura fried scallops, roasted pork collar, and the duck breast & scotched fig.

The desserts, frozen yogurt w/ lavendar honey & caramel apple doughnuts, were excellent.

Notice many ppl ordering the Morgan's meats & Garden kale crab rangoon. So try them.

Great place for sharing, so try to order many dishes (limited menu, so possible to order everything w/ a group of 4 or 5 ppl).

Highest compliments to Executive Chef Greg Baxtrom.

Recommend having your desserts in the heated garden.

Would love to come back soon, but looking like another month wait. :(

Excellent service.

Highly recommend.

: 9 calendars

It's not every day you sit in a garden in Brooklyn sipping Champagne and watching your dinner grow ( kale), while couples roast s'mores over a roasting mini fire. Luckily for us we got to.  

I made our reservations for the only available spot for a Thursday Night, 10:30 pm.  We arrived early hoping to sit at the bar.  Luck for us and the restaurant the bar was totally full.  The gracious maitre d lead us to the intoxicating back garden where we were greeted by cozy benches with heat lamps and blankets.  We took in the beauty of the garden while drinking wine and discussing the state of the world and our love of tiny foods.  Time snuck away,  before we were aware it was time for our reservations.   

We discussed the sensible amount of food to get and consequently we had to eat almost everything on the menu.

We started with Morgan's Meats ( A revolving selection of local farm raised humanly treated meats.)  Duck liver pate with fresh Hudson Valley Honey on top.  It's paired with pickled dilly beans and crostinis.  I've never met a crostini I didn't want to instinctively cover in dip and pop into my face hole.
We had oyster al get in my mouth and crab rang so good right now.  They were gone as soon as the attentive waiter could get his skilled hands out of the line of fire.

We had so many courses I can't recall them all but let me tell you the Brook Trout took my mind out of my head and put it in a sublime dimension only water chestnuts and fresh cheese can conjure.  

I'm sad to say by the end of our meal we opted to drink out desserts.

All in all!  Olmsted went above and beyond expectations.  I'm see you next time Kid!

Amazing! We finally went for dinner last night after making a rez back in August (!) and it was well worth the wait. The restaurant itself is intimate and charming, with a lot of beautiful details like earthenware made by a local NYC artist and herbs left to dry on garlands above the kitchen bar. The real gem is the backyard garden, complete with veggies that find themselves into the dishes (currently kale that goes into the crab rangoons, which were my favorite dish of the evening after dessert), heatlamps, hotplates for making s'mores, and a couple of live birds (quails?) who I presume are doing double duty as mascots and egg-providers. 
For dinner (inside), we started with the tiny tartare tacos (fish tender to perfection from being marinated in tequila), Morgan's meats (morgan made duck liver mousse with honey last night--we licked the plate), crab rangoons, and the carrot crepe. Everything was served playfully and creatively, and the dishes were inventive and fun, but still very accessible and unpretentious (a tough balance, esp in Brooklyn). We had the pork collar and trout for dinner--both delicious and filling--and finished off the meal with chocolate mousse. We also had several drinks, but my recommendations are the Posset (so weird, so delicious), and the Rosemary (#elevatedbasic). 
Go here. The food is delicious, the ambiance is awesome, and it's worth the wait to grab a reservation!

This place is a joke. 

My partner and I went there not long after it opened because it received a few good write-ups. In hindsight, we were able to find no reason whatsoever for the hubbub over this mediocre spot.

The portions are laughably small, especially considering the prices. The food itself is below average for the neighborhood, which already boasts quite a few great spots. The atmosphere simply tries too hard.

Do yourself a favor and skip Olmstead. You will likely pay less and eat better just about anywhere else in the area.

Wow did I love this place. From food to drinks. Snacks to dessert, everything presented is well executed and is done so with a uniqueness that leaves you spending the entire time thinking "wow, what am I eat/drinking, and how did they get it to taste this way?"  My favorite was the cauliflower. Must order. Also had the carrot crepe w/ clams and lamb entree. Both were exceptional. Dessert was recommended and it was frozen yogurt. If you are like me you are thinking "frozen yogurt? That's boring!" Not here, my friend....not here. It was amazing and complex textures made it possibly one of the most unforgettable dishes of the meal. 

And the cocktails? Second to none. Try the red grape. Really fascinating and complex flavors
World-class elevated farm-to-table cuisine available in Prospect Heights.  What's not to love?

Have you ever read "The Emperor's New Clothes"???? Maybe people can not admit that this place is insane, it is not a restaurant that serves food, just an idea that they do, hence the story. Atmosphere was nice, food not so great or not existent!!!!!! the crawfish chips were like pork rinds with old bay seasoning,and there were 6 chips in the order. We tried all of the small plates, only the cauliflower was decent. Mains were so small and unsatisfying, pasta dish wasn't pasta but a raw, spiralized root with sauce. everyone was disappointed. The scallops were shark tips and not scallops at all.  not worth the $400 tab. There was no food!!!!!! just remnants of what we thought food was.
The food was very strange, we all left starving also. Dessert was good, we had apple donuts.

Chef Greg is a creative culinary genius!!! 

Love his food so much!!! 

Everything he puts on the menu is absolutely amazing....! 

Just do what we did! Order everything!!!
Beautiful plating, delicious food, and quality ingredients. After a delicious entree and wine we had dessert in the garden. Worth the $$$

Food, service, ambiance were all very good.  Was a bit disappointed by the fried monkfish, which was literally a few fried crumbs.  The backyard is nice for warm pre-dinner drinks, even in the cold, since they have heating lamps above all the seating.

I dined at this beautiful Brooklyn resturant over the weekend, the atmosphere was fantastic, the prices were on the higher side but expected. The menu was very limited, not much in the way of discription, we needed to ask the server to describe nearly every dish. Which took away from our visit with our friends. Also after going over basically the entire menu,we forgot the first descriptions. My sugestion would be to put a little more effort into your menu. I'm thinking your entent was to come off minamal and sleek, but not practical !!  My server a young lady greeted us, got our first round of drinks, they were craft beers & wine very nice. My first warning was when our server asked us how hungry we were? What? Who does that.... She enformed us that our snacks were on the smaller side then as the menu goes on the portions get larger. So with this we ordered three appetizers, then four entrées. Our first corse was so small that we all just looked at one another and laughted!!! Not realizing that the entrées were not going to be much better. Each meal fit in the palm of our hand!!! For meals costing over twenty dollars this is not acceptable. The portions were so small that I really thought this can't be real. No bread or salad was offered to possibly deflect the rediciouls portions. When I dine out it is an experience I enjoy and an willing to pay for, however to walk out of a resturant still hungry is not expected or enjoyable!!! I am a server by trade I would be embarrassed to serve anyone these meals!!!   my hope in writing this review is to educate this eatery that simply being a hip place is not enough, its an eatery people want to eat a meal!!! Not be ensulted by extremely small portions and high prices!!   NOT COOL!!!!!!!!

My fave find of the year!  From
Start to finish, all the dishes wowed me and my husband.  We had the liver moose with honey and sour cabbage, chawanmuishi, squash soup, trout and lamb dishes.  We couldn't decide which ones we enjoyed the most.  Everything was creative and absolutely delicious.  We also shared donuts and chocolate moose dessert.  Both were terrific ends to the evening.   Will be looking for an excuse to come back soon!

Neighborhoodly restaurant in a way that's laid back and understated, with a kitchen that is making incredible food (and a waiting area that is seriously backyard dreams). Everything sounds decent on paper, but the real thing is so surprisingly good - so creative, delicious and delightful. It's exciting to take a guess at what's going to arrive at your table.

The menu is constantly changing and reinventing itself (even the cocktails), and honestly I've never had a bad bite. The famous carrot crepe is a perfect example of the type of food you can expect - gorgeous to look at, delicious, and not quite like anything else. Another favorite was lamb porchetta, which was so tender and sat in a delicious sauce, under a blanket of fig leather (mind-blowing). Rutabaga "Tagliatelle" was made with such a buttery sauce that I completely forgot I was eating root vegetables rather than pasta (which probably would've made the dish too heavy). If they have a version of their chawanmushi, definitely get that as well. 

There's nothing quick about a meal here, but it's better that way. The food arrives when it's ready, no structured courses. So get ready for a long, lingering meal that's casual yet sophisticated. We opted to sit in their beautiful backyard for dessert, benches amongst plenty of greenery, complete with space heaters and cozy blankets. Sample the chocolate mousse and frozen yogurt with whipped honey (both are amazing), roast marshmallows for some seriously upgraded s'mores, pour steamed milk from the thermos to make a mug of hot cocoa (rum optional but highly recommended) -- there is nothing more perfect to end the evening.

Had the trout with creamed brussel sprouts and roasted onion and absolutely loved it. Terrific cocktails, and I also recommend the crawfish boil crackers and squash soup. The chocolate mousse (which comes with a full separate bowl of crème fraîche) was heavy and super-rich--a little too much for someone looking for a bit of light sweetness to finish off the meal, maybe. But I do plan to go back for cocktails and DIY s'mores in the lovely garden sometime.

I have been twice now, usually come in early and go to the bar. Small space, nice design, small open kitchen and back back yard. Was too cold to go in the back yard, but it looked nice, will try it out in the spring! Food & Cocktails are what I like best, inventive food, small but very nice menu. I suggest ordering a few things from each section of the menu and sharing, that is the best way to go, great flavor profiles and sold execution. Will be back!
Fantastic! Too bad reservations are soo hard to get! Love that garden for lethal cocktails.

Got here when kitchen was officially closed but had the chance to try the dessert and get a drink at the bar. Try the frozen yogurt with lavender honey!!! Classic chocolate mousse was good, too. Port wine with it makes it better though :) 
Staff is very friendly, music is good - old school. Backyard is open even in the winter. Plants hanging on the wall in the closed space, gives it a great ambience. Will definitely come back for proper dinner!

BRO!...naw. BRAH!!! BRAH!!! I gotta go full meathead FRAT brah on THIS review!!! It's THAT INTENSLY GOOD!

This isn't your, let's pop into Olmsted because we've been eating Thai food for the last 4 days kind of joint. You have two options to get in: 1. Make reservations way in advance like Richie Rich(I don't know why that reference has ANYTHING to do with him, I just wanted to say Richie Rich Brah.) 2. Go RIGHT as they open at 5:30(there will already be a line) and snag one of the bar seats. You can go about 8 people deep at the bar, but after that, you are dry toast SOL. My Bro's and I did the 5:30 first snag option, and it worked out gloriously. No room to spare with these meaty guns in tow.(ew)

Bartender-SOLID. Got the Lavender Bourbon...that's right! I'm in touch with my feminine side Bro, chicks DIG it. AND I totally dig this drink! It is like getting slapped in the face with a Oak cask barrel made out of flowers! 

FOOD. DUUUUDE. THE. FOOD.

Check this, my Bra-hams and I went share plates all around. We wanted to try as much of the menu as our wallets would allow, and totally LOVE sharing some Grub with my Boys! Skipped the Snacks menu....we hungry oxen, and can't be nibbling a crawfish crackers. Opted for the MALE Mullett Tartare. Boom! Tartare meets almost ceviche meets hell yes. Grilled Scallops, very tasty, all enjoyed, not the best dish, but probably better than scallops at just about anywhere else. Rutabaga Tagliatelle. Ruta what?! Tagliate...how you say it? FUCK IT. GET IN MY FACE YOU DELICIOUS BASTARD! Wait, this isn't a noodle!? Its a veggie? Best damn veggie of my life! And that sauce was creamy yet mild and perfect. Oh, I'm sorry, we made an extra on accident, have ANOTHER PLATE! SCORE! GET IN MY FACE...AGAIN!Batting 1000! Then the final course.......Guinea Hen Roasted & Confit. They Enola Gaye flew that plate over to us and dropped the FUCKIN BOMB on us! What magical beast is this "HEN"
 you speak of?! This is not of this world! This was brought forth by the powers of ZEUS and all that is mighty! HEN must be their abbreviate for HEAVEN. It was moistened by the tears of GOD. It made us all cry for joy. And I'm not ashamed to CRY BRAH. I'm more beast than man and this dish made me quiver at my sheer existence in this mortal world.

Sorry not sorry I had to TOTALLY BRO out this review, and if you read this entire review I apologize but you are also welcome because I just told you where to go to have the BEST MEAL I HAD IN 2016. NOW GO you stupid mortal! (slaps phone out of your hand)

Solid solid solid. 

Expect to pay $$$ but you're paying for the whole shebang experience. It hits the right note on all aspects - great date, awesome food, beautiful decor, potent yet balanced drinks.

Scallops and guinea hen were the absolute standouts - incredible.
Carrot crepe was awesome as well, and deserves all the accolades that it's gotten.
Lamb porchetta was good, but would not get again if I were to return.
Smores included a very cute experience in the back with heated lamps and DIY coals in tin.
Lavender Honey yogurt was solid and greek yogurt lovers would love this one.

Overall, would return to sit at bar to sip on the lassi cocktail and munch on scallops and chicken dish (y)

Rolled up to the door and it was packed with folks out the door, and but our whole party was present so we waited less than a minute before being seated at a great round table near the open kitchen. Loved the flatware and tableware.  Food was amazing, carrot crepes not to be missed.  Terrific wine and liquor list. Attentive but unobtrusive service.  Will be back!

Though this is no easy table to get, Olmsted is worth the hassle.  The dishes were tasty, creative, and flavorful.  Even the two desserts we ordered were a success (don't be tuned off by the yogurt .  It is quite good.).  The in our party enjoyed the trout, the carrots, duck, and "pasta" dishes.  The plates are small, even the entre size, but they are sufficient.

A lot of hype on this place, and it lived up to it. We got (in order of how much I liked it):

- Morgan's meats
- Male mullet tartare
- Sweet potato & uni pierogies
- Crawfish boil crackers
- Carrot crepe
- Rutabaga "tagliatelle"

My wife would have them ordered differently -- she was a little freaked out by the texture of the meats, and she absolutely loved the pierogies (that was easily her #1). 

That said, we loved almost everything. We started with the crawfish crackers (recommended by the Michelin inspector's Twitter account the day before...), which were excellent. The meats were weird but incredible -- I forgot to ask exactly what it was, but it was essentially gelled meats in some kind of honey (I think?) that you smear on toast. Really amazing. The tartare was a close second for me. I really liked the pierogies as well, but not quite as much as my wife -- she said it was one of her favorite things she had eaten in a while, and she kept talking about them the day after. 

We both really liked the carrot crepe, but thought it was somewhat overrated -- the clams and the crepe itself were great, but not as mindblowing as some of the other dishes we got. We also were really excited for the tagliatelle (which was from from rutabaga, not actual pasta), but I don't think we'd get it again -- the lamb and hen looked incredible, and I think we'd sub those in as our main(s) next time.

This place is clearly still in its hype phase -- we made a reservation almost a month out and the best we could get was 9:45 on a Thursday -- but I get it, and I hope it's around for a long time. Can't wait to go back and try things once the menu turns over again. (The menu we had looked pretty different than the menu from the summer.)

Have lived in Brooklyn for 13 years and seen plenty of 'new Brooklyn' restaurants come and go. Olmsted is easily at the top of this trend.  Great room, garden, friendly service and delicious, inventive food. The guinea hen was the real standout for me.   Delicious

Came here for a late dinner on a weekday. The place was still packed at 10pm! The ambience is warm and inviting, and I loved the wall of plants on one side. The service was prompt and welcoming. Cocktails were sensational; my favorite was the Turmeric. We shared a lot of different dishes among the table. Standouts were the uni pierogies, rutabaga tagliatelle, and trout. We also tried one of every dessert. All delicious! I'd definitely come back for another pleasant evening.

Olmsted was one of the most talked about Brooklyn restaurants of 2016, and I can see why.

Their concept itself is great. Their goal is to serve high brow food at... mid brow prices (is that even a term?). Presentation takes a minor backseat to taste, and they'll go ahead and buy that bruised vegetable and pass the savings onto you. Also helps that the place is pretty dimly lit!

And of course, the head chef has a pedigree that needs no introduction.

That said, get here EARLY. Three of us stopped in right when they opened at 5pm and there was already a line of people waiting. I'm still a relatively young guy, but I'll eat dinner at early bird special times if the meal's this damn good.

We sat at the bar, ordered some inventive cocktails (the Soba and Lavender were both good).

Then we ordered a bunch of dishes for sharing.

Started out with the Gobi Pakora cauliflower. It's hard to mess up roasted cauliflower, so expectations weren't that high. But the flavors were excellent. I'm also always a sucker for pickled red onions.

Our second dish was the mullet tartare, served with what was essentially fancy chips. Served with cranberry chimichurri on top and a white sauce on the side (don't remember what it was... yogurt? creme fraiche?). It was very similar to ceviche.

Our first main was the rutabaga tagliatelle with truffles. This was a favorite. It was closer to pappardelle in terms of width, cut a little short, but oh so rich. The brown butter sauce was so thick, and I've said it before and I'll say it again - truffles is just cheating.

So it was at this point where there was lull in service (SUPER tiny kitchen behind the bar). The bartender said he would check on our next dish, and instead they brought us out another rutabaga tagliatelle by accident. Bartender told us to roll with it, and hell, I never turn down free food.

Our penultimate dish was the grilled scallops - skewered, with apple and peanuts on the side. Pretty good scallops, but I've had better elsewhere. Interesting preparation, but I'd skip this one the next time.

And finally, the piece de resistance was the Guinea hen two ways (roasted & confit). It was just... perfect. Tender, juicy, rich. The breast was served with ramp sauce and roasted sunchoke. The confit was just wonderful. More ramp foam, and morels.

The space is actually pretty big, of like I mentioned before, it's very popular. So make a reservation well in advance, or show up for first-come-first-served bar seating. They also have a backyard, which is super cool.

I loved the food, I loved the cocktails, I loved their philosophy.

Olmsted is an absolute must for food lovers!

I can see where they were trying to go with the creativity, and I admire that, but the flavors still have to hold up and they just didn't. Morgans meats weren't bad but nothing extraordinary. The Carrot crepe looks pretty but is definitely overhyped (my claims were very salty and the flavors weren't overall that harmonious). The roasted guinea hen had almost no flavor although the confit dish was quite tasty.

Perfect food. Amazing service! Everyone was so friendly and inviting. Our table wasn't quite ready, so we had some whiskey out in the back patio. Their little birds were running around in a heated enclosure. It was chilly so they brought us blankets and offered us smores. Will be back for that for sure!

The actual meal was wonderful. All the courses were timed well. We had a front row seat to the kitchen. The kitchen staff were so nice and chatted with us throughout service. Our waitress was sweet, but not intrusive. 

The food was so beautifully plated. Simple and lovely. Filled with color. The carrot crepe stood out as the best dish because of the sauce. Though the guinea hen was delicious as well. All in all. A perfect evening out! Good luck getting a reservation, though.

Only thing I would say, with such good food and cocktails, there could be a better, more interesting beer list. It's pretty safe and boring. But it's definitely not worth knocking a star.

So, after driving around for 30 minutes trying to find a restaurant open on President's Day (because apparently that is a thing...restaurants close on a fake holiday), I stumbled on Olmsted and sat at the bar. The place was packed! Every orifice, lined with people...my dining experience deserves (truly) two and a half stars BUT the food, though !!!! I had the door slammed in my face when I arrived because the gentleman was concerned about a draft and he had me wait for 10 minutes before I was permitted in. I asked for a spot at the bar and was seated right away. 

Look, the bartender was nice enough, offered a Malbec substitute that did the job but it took (at least) 90 minutes to eat what I actually ordered. I relay it this way because I was provided two delicious "this bitch is waiting too long dishes" one was a yummy cauliflower concoction and the other had carrots and sunflower seeds. 

When I got my meal, I was surprised by the portion size, it was a scallop skewer with a slaw! The food is delicious, I can't lie but I think my wait was a little ridiculous. 

And that's it folks! Olmsted can't be denied because the food is out of this world! I had the donuts for dessert (because, of course I'm having dessert and OMFG!!! The Donuts!!!!!) The bartender topped my meal off with a sour grape...it was like the yummiest thing I ever tasted. 

I think Olmsted DARED me to not love it and I failed miserably...you will too!

I've been wanting to visit Olmsted since it opened*, particularly on Monday when they're walk-in only**, and it finally worked out on President's Day 2017. The attractive space (inside & out) was designed by the same guy behind Atera, and everything we drank out of and ate off of was also beautiful. We were first on line and got the Chef's Counter, a lovely enhancement to the experience, as a couple cooks chatted us up briefly as we admired their work.
Saratoga Sparkling water $3 for a bottle
Bread (comp. if you ask, served warm with phenomenal amped-up butter) 

1st course
Monkfish $15 were so addictive

2nd course
Pierogies $13 were amazing umami bombs, albeit served a tad too hot
Carrot Crepe $15 lived up to its reputation

3rd Course
Rutabaga 'tagliatelle' $20 superbly buttery
Short rib $23 was remarkably tender, with great refried beans they torch before service

Dessert
Yogurt $8 with a healthy mega-dollop
S'mores $20 with great graham crackers from Runner&Stone and housemade vanilla marshmallows but, as cute as touch as it was, we felt a bit cheaped out with the Hershey's bar...we also felt uncomfortable (and surprised) as the only ones outside enjoying this, and felt their discomfort watching us, and clearly convincing themselves not to order it as our consumption progressed (and the coals/embers were almost useless after the 2nd sandwich)

Oolong Phoenix tea $4, excellent, though the hourglass wasn't quite long enough for us

*We first tried 9/4/16 and they didn't seem to open despite no posts on social media or their site, and they ignored a Yelp message inquiry as to why...then didn't wanna ruin my first experience with their bites at the Samsung 837 / Infatuation 2016 year-end event. There are just way too many write-ups of the place to leave a ton of links, but do your research ahead of time if you feel like it, or just leave yourself in good hands.
**Per his GrubStreet profile Chef Baxtrom's day off is Monday, but he was very much there way before service and throughout our 2.5 hours there, so that shows his dedication

Been waiting to trying this restaurant after all the hype it's been getting and finally managed to go try it and lets just say it doesn't live up to the hype in my opinion.  Me and my wife came in as a walk-in on monday and even though we got there at 5:30pm, it was already a 2 hour wait, which is understandable for a restaurant with such hype revolving around it.

After our 2 hours wait we are seated much to our excitement!  we ordered the sweet potato & uni pirogis to start the grilled scallops and lamb porchetta for our entrees and the caramel apple doughnuts for desert.  The pirogis came out prompt and hot, they were absolutely amazing, good sweet potato flavor with a hint of uni flavor, really done well.  After that we were totally excited for our entrees.  Well unfortunately it just goes down hill from here.  We waited, nearly an hour between our appetizer and entrees, that is just unacceptable.  After about 45 min of waiting our waiter brings us the carrot crepe complements of the house, which was really good also, but still not the entrees we were waiting for.  Finally after an hour our wait is over and our entrees come, only to be disappointed.  The grilled sea scallops were over cooked and over charred so they had a bitter taste to it and the lamb was just alright, nothing to write home about.  Then after our entrees were cleared down the wait begins for desert, after 10 minutes the waitress brings us chocolate mousse compliments of the house, which was good, but would've rather had the doughnuts we ordered instead.  Then another 10 minutes go by and we finally get our doughnuts and they were the absolute best part of the meal.  

While we were enjoying our dessert we also noticed a table near us that was seated well before me and my wife and when we got our dessert they were just getting their entrees, so I don't think my long wait between courses was a fluke.
