Overall the starter and desert was amazing, but the entrees were sub par with that and the long wait between courses, really can't recommend any of my friends to go here.

was super lucky to get a last minute reservation, the restaurant lives up to all the write ups. everything was delicious and I recommend only going with people ready to share food so you can try lots.  My favourite was definitely the rutabaga tagliatelle.  Already made res for April to come back with more friends to taste more of the menu then!

Wow. Just wow. Everything, and I do mean everything, was exquisite. This is the meal I'm continually searching for. We started with the cauliflower, which was easily the best cauliflower I've ever had. We moved to the duck and the carrot crepe, both of which I'd highly recommend. We finished with the rutabaga tagliatelle and the scallops and to say that I'm craving both again - minutes after finishing the meal - is an understatement. Go here. This is the best NYC has to offer. If you don't love this place, then god help you.

Summery:   Lives up to the hype.  Sixty days for a reservation... yeah, of course.  Because it's worth waiting for.  NY Times review.  Dead on.  

Here is the order:

Gobi cauliflower 
The duck w naan and pear chutney 
Carrot crepe
Sea scallops
Rutabaga tagliatelle
Frozen yogurt

Cocktail:  red grape. 

You're welcome. 

Ps - Wes our server was awesome.

I guess you just cannot ignore it - this neighborhood restaurant dual owned by chef Greg Baxtrom and farmer Ian Rothman, both had various experience trained at restaurant pearls including Alinea, Blue Hill at Stone Barns, and had met each other during the Atera period.

Instead of being over complicated, Olmsted carried a rather simple menu. With a small group, we were actually able to sample many dishes. Good thing is that each course was relatively small in size, so one would not complain about over-stuffed. While each plate was almost close to flawless, I would recommend the scallop, the uni dumpling, and the best-dessert-on-earth - that lavender frozen yogurt. This seasonal-driven, ingredient oriented menu has lots of food coming directly from their backyard garden, which was literally just several tables away from where we dined.

Established only months back last year, I already saw it grasping numerous awards - two stars from Pete Wells, the hottest restaurant ranked in Brooklyn, and potentially a Michelin star next year.

By the time we concluded our dinner, it was already close to midnight so we had to defer our garden visit to next time; yet all of us left with full satisfaction. Think Greg and his gang really nailed it, and in their own way!

Not entirely sure how I have friends who can get reservations here after all that hype from the media, which is really well deserved. I delayed writing this review but can still distinctly remember the taste of every dish we ordered. The best plates were easily the duck chakna and Dave's trout for me, but people were also loving the carrot crepe, uni pierogis and popcorn monkfish. The guinea hen was a slight disappointment given how salty it was, but the confit was still a win. Drinks have low ABV but are mostly enjoyable. Desserts seem rather unsophisticated and not my cup of tea. But overall the best meal I have had in 2017 so far.

I finally made it here to this high-demand restaurant .. enjoyed dinner:

Gobi pakora cauliflower
Morgan's meats (guinea hen liver mousse)
Sweet potato and uni pierogies
Carrot crepe
Duck chankna with pear chutney
Rutabaga tagliatelle
Guinea hen roasted and confit
Pork collar

Highlights were the carrot crepe and guinea hen (liver mousse under snacks; and the entree (roasted and confit). Very creative and flavorful execution. The pork and the duck dishes were wonderful as well but the must-haves are the former 

The Gobi pakora cauliflower was a tad oily. The pierogies were dry almost overcooked ...per the description seemed like a strange combination. I like sweet potato and I like uni but unfortunately this was a miss for me

The tagliatelle was surprisingly bland. 

The Swiss miss hot chocolate drink seemed light as was the old fashioned chocolate mousse but I enjoyed the mousse with the creme fraiche - nice way to end the meal with a fluffy creamy chocolate dessert 

Despite the couple of dishes I could've done without I really enjoyed being there and overall enjoyed the meal. Service was very good. The garden out in the back is where they grow most of their ingredients and where you can enjoy s'mores and drinks.

Took me a while to score a reservation, but overall was worth it.

We started with a cocktail, solid list.
Moved to the wine list with reasonably priced options.
For the food, it was excellent to share between the four of us. I think my favorites were:
-- rutabaga tagliatelles
-- califlower
-- carrot crepe
-- morgan's meat
-- the chocolate mousse

$100pp. A strong brooklyn option but maybe slightly overhyped.
Very small portions lacking flavor. I personally don't get what all of the hype is about.

Love love love this place. Had been meaning to visit within a few months of their first opening in the spring and eventually finally made it for my birthday in October. Fantastic service and great food. Additionally, the garden in the back only serves drinks and snacks while the bar serves the full menu. Love their simplicity and treatment of farm fresh ingredients allowed to shine. Cocktails are all great, decent wine selection, a list of additional beverages and a tea program. The desserts are also totally worth it. I revisited recently with a friend for a casual light dinner and drinks. We waited in the garden and sat at the bar and again service and food were great. Difficult to get reservations so must plan ahead.

I was lucky to get a seat here for 2 on Tuesday at 5pm. Let's start with the food as follows:

1) the truffled rutabaga that could easily fool you as a pasta if you didn't eat it yourself. I enjoyed this play and creativity and the savoriness is at 5 stars
2) Dave's trout - this is 2 stars at best. I forced ate it like foie Gras 
3) uni perrogi - too salty and I didn't get a single hint of uni in the dish whatsoever 
4) frozen yogurt with lavender honey - this dish changed my review from 2 stars to 3 stars. It's really good and I look forward to consuming their desserts next time again. 

Drinks 

1) lavender cocktail is worth going for again. It definitely opens up your olfactory senses while smelling the lavender and consuming it simultaneously. I'll def come back to sit at the bar and drink this all night 
2) soba - I'll pass on this by all means necessary 
3) decent Scotch menu (consumed springbank 10 year responsibly)

Service 

The Cook had more service than their FOH. Do I need to say more? 

Decor 

It's got a good ambience and exemplifies what Brooklyn has transformed into, especially Vanderbilt. 

Overall 

I'll be back again when time permits, but the hype might have given me higher expectations which of course lead to greater disappointments. I'll be patient in my next visit and hopefully I pick the right dishes so this review can get 5 stars instead of 3.

Halfway through a delicious meal my wife quoted a professional chef who once told her sister, "You'll NEVER cook as well as we do, because you'll never use as much BUTTER, and you'll never use as much SALT."

We had three dishes (plus incredible bread and butter, which we had to request) and all were tasty in interesting, creative ways, but they all relied pretty heavily on butter or oil. That's not really a criticism, just a warning.

The other warnings: skimpy portions. I like quality AND quantity, and I don't expect a mountain of pasta or a single appetizer portion to generously feed a table of four. I'd just like to leave and not get home and open the refrigerator to forage for more food. Our rutabaga 'tagliatelle' was phenomenal, but was a true primi size portion, rather than an entree, as it was more or less  labeled.Our $8 cauliflower app was wonderful, but had four times as much 'presentation' fodder as edible food. Our trout slathered with creamed Brussels sprouts, conversely, was naked on the plate and could've used a nice side of faro or roasted potatoes or roasted carrots or just SOMEthing. Still, an amazing dish - but it just wasn't a meal, and had we been warned, we'd have gotten a side dish or two (not that there are any, exactly, but we'd have thrown in more 'small plates.')

I'd go back in a minute. The food was great, the vibe was nice (if a little loud), the service was friendly (though could've more helpfully informed us of some things), and the prices weren't horrible for this quality of experience. I'd mainly like to see them serve just a little more food (okay, 25-50% more food, depending on the dish) and warn us in advance a little bit more about what we're getting into. 

Go check it out for yourself and see what you think!
A decent place, but I was expecting more because one of my friends told me great things about it. Ok but nothing so remarkable

I don't often venture to the outer boroughs to eat, but Olmsted was beyond worth it. The food was spectacular. Had the monkfish popcorn, duck, and pierogies to start. And scallops and the guinea hen for entrees. Every single dish was outstanding, cooked to perfection and unique flavor combos I've not had before. And the lavender bourbon cocktail may actually have been the best permutation of an old fashioned I've ever had. Can't wait to go back and hang in the garden when it's warmer.

900th review? That's cool.

Quite excellent. Olmsted came with a lot of hype attached (James Beard Award nominee for 2017), and I'd have to say it's well-deserved. It took quite a while to get an OpenTable reservation at a reasonable time, but after some patience, our visit finally happened. The decor seems very meticulously thought-out, with lots of plants and vines hanging all over the indoor space, and a really nice outdoor backyard patio, complete with blankets when it's cold out. They really thought of everything.

What we got:
- Popcorn monkfish: Tasty, but not really worth the value. The portion is really small, and the monkfish, while delicious, is cut into really small pieces and it's hard to derive any real monkfish flavor.
- Charred onion chawanmushi with smoked trout roe and maitake: really delicious, and had a nice salty taste, without being too fishy.
- Carrot crepe with littleneck clams: beautifully plated, but perhaps needed a few more clams with it.
- Guinea hen confit and roasted: Both versions were really great, and while we obviously preferred the confit, the roasted guinea hen portion did not have a dry bite throughout the dish.
- Frozen yogurt with lavender honey: quite amazing, and really hit the spot. The lavender flowers are a nice touch, and the cream with yogurt really made for a great dessert that wasn't too sweet.

Our server gave great recommendations and really knew her stuff about the wines, so that was greatly appreciated. The prices are a bit more expensive, but overall, the value is really good, given the quality of the ingredients, and the care they put into plating and execution.

Overall, not every dish was a knockout, but I would still give it 5 stars because there were some really amazing dishes, and the overall experience just left us feeling really good. Definitely a great time for a date or a small group. If you can get a seat in the backyard patio for just lounging, it seems like a really nice romantic spot. I will definitely be back to try their other offerings, and looking forward to see their seasonal dishes.

OUTSTANDING! Seldom do popular restaurants live up to the hype, but Olmsted surpassed the hype and our high hopes!

It's at the same time a wonderful neighborhood spot and a serious restaurant whose food showcases the freshest ingredients in winning creative way. The chef experiments...successfully! Turning rutabaga into "pasta", carrots into a delicious crepe that is a base for clams, Olmsted's food surprises and delights!

There were four of us for dinner this evening, which enabled us to sample more than half of the offerings. There wasn't one even slight miss. 

We shared 3 snacks - oysters with their homemade hot sauce, Gobi Pakora cauliflower, and Morgan's meats which was a delicious smooth pâté with a touch of honey on top served with red cabbage kraut and freshly toasted crostini. The last item was particularly tasty! 

We then shared 4 small plates including an Indian flavored duck sausage with red lentil naan - a brilliant combination of flavors and textures that made it a standout! The chawanmushi was silky and smoky, light but richly flavored. 

Guinea fowl prepared two ways - confit and roasted - was exceptional. The rutabaga and scallops were also hits. 

Dessert was apple "donuts" with a pot of caramel sauce. Served 5 to an order, it was the perfect sweet bite to end the evening. They have a nice selection of teas also, including three oolongs. 

Service was very friendly and helpful. We didn't feel rushed at all - the timing of the dishes was well paced. 

These Blue Hill at Stone Barns fans are looking forward to returning to Olmsted soon!

Have been trying to get a rez forever. Very good and quirky menu with a bevy of delicious flavors. Loved the unexpected Asian flair to many dishes. Everything kept us guessing and tasting, trying to uncover ingredients. We didn't regret a single dish. The crab rangoon and duck were great. I thought the carrot crepe was tasty but didn't quite live up to the hype. It was very delicate and I have a minor cold so maybe that's it. The scallops were done perfectly. The pork collar was a bit of a letdown. Nice reasonable wine selection.

The service was a slight let down. They don't have any runners so our waiter was doing triple duty and he struggled with that. Overall a very good and borderline great restaurant. 

Overall a very delicious and pleasant experience. 4/5 just because some dishes were slightly overhyped and the service was less than perfect.

I'll start by saying that I am a very casual diner and this was an extreme upgrade in experience, but a great one! I'm the 'fish and chips with a Guinness at a bench table' type, but this was way beyond that, which I did on purpose. I was testing this place out with a friend who just moved to NYC from Japan. I literally chose Olmsted because it was the newest, raved about restaurant in Prospect Heights at the time (around July 2016--I know, I'm super late with this review). However to my surprise, this place had a Japanese dish that my friend was obsessed with!

Shockingly, we got there at about 5:30/6:00pm and got seated right away, which I read doesn't usually happen. We wanted to dine at the bar so we could be close up to the large selection of booze. My friend knew his stuff so he ordered us some Japanese whiskey, which I couldn't recall the name of at this time.

Fast forwarding to our food selections, we had the (1) snap pea sushi as an appetizer, (2) radish top gazpacho (smoked trout roe), which was one heck of an experience for me, (3) NY grass fed bavette, (4) Taku River salmon (w/ crispy potatoes and poppy cream cheese) and (5) spring onion chawanmushi (Japenese savoury egg custard), which was also mind-blowing to my taste buds. We ordered all of these things because the entrees are small plates, so you need at least 3 things to feel like you had a full meal. 

My friend couldn't stop saying how amazing the chawanmushi was! He even said it's the closest to the real thing he grew up eating in Japan (hooray, Olmsted!). Little did I know that this American (new) restaurant would have a slight Japanese vibe going on because it worked out perfectly that my friend could find things on the menu that he was missing from back home.

For dessert, our waiter recommended that we go out back to their outdoor patio to enjoy the summer night, which was a good move. It was so cute out there! Nice lighting and wooden benches with pillows and a view of their garden. It was quite romantic back there (something to keep in mind for future date nights). We ended up sharing the old school chocolate mousse (w/ vanilla creme fraise), which was super delicious (I love anything chocolatey and sweet)!

The service here was excellent. I'd definitely return for dessert and drinks in the backyard in summertime.
So F-ing good. Inventive and exciting menu with palatable prices and solid service. Come early for a drink in the back garden.

Good cocktails, and the carrot crepe was our favorite dish.  We shared a bunch of the other dishes and they mostly fell flat in terms of flavor for us. We tried the duck, cod, trout, pork, yakitori, and apple donuts - mostly just ok and not memorable. Go for the cocktails and carrot crepe.

I think Olmsted may be an unintentional victim of the hype machine. It received stellar reviews in the press and apparently a James Beard semifinalist. As a result, reservations are next to impossible. The alluring back patio/garden is great, the cocktails are creative, and the service is on-point, so there's that. For me though, it comes down to what I'm eating...and for that, I was honestly disappointed and found the meal to be very average. ..not near the level I had anticpated. 

To be specific...why all the fried selections? Crawfish boil crackers? These were essentially thick, crunchy fried potato chips. Fried pickles?? My wife pointed out the dive bar in our 'hood also serves fried pickes. Popcorn monkfish? Not much different than the standard fast food popcorn shrimp served at Popeyes. Cod Fritters? Really? Fritters? See what I mean?  These weren't bad..you can fry-up anything and it'll taste good, but this type of fare was far from what I had anticpated. Granted these are snacks and starters, but given the small portions, you have but no choice to order 1 of each. 

The rest of the meal (we tried most of the menu) meandered around a few tasty items ...duck, their carrot crepe...tasty but confusing, the rutabaga 'tagliatelle'..laced with about 11 stickes of butter, and their yakitori. Nothing wrong with yakitori - small pieces of chicken breast, tenderloin or thigh grilled then skewered...just so run-of-the-mill. 

Maybe my expectations were set too high based on what I had read. ..and that's not their fault. Wish I had better things to say, but unfortunately I don't.

Delicious food, top notch drinks and great staff. Kitchen can be slow at times, but impressive what they can churn out in such a small kitchen space. Outdoor space is lovely and a great place for a drink or dessert on a pleasant night. Rutabaga pasta, carrot crepe, Morgan's Meats and many of the other small plates keep us coming back. So glad to have this gem in our neighborhood!

Mmm... Where to start? 

First of all, I was 30minutes late and they were nice enough to keep my table until I got there.

We ordered 4 dishes to share (the duck, the carotte crêpe, the yakitori & the tagliatelle). Everything was superb. Dish after dish, everything was excellent. Plated and presented so beautifully as well. I had heard good things about the place but definitely did not expect that! 
For dessert, we had the chocolate mousse and the frozen yogurt with lavender honey Italian meringue. I personally could have used a little bit more of the lavender taste but that's a love it or hate it kind of thing. 

Staff was also very friendly. I m glad this gem is in my new neighborhood! I will be coming back!

Are you people kidding me? Have any of you actually eaten at a sit down restaurant before? Were you James Beard reviewers lucid when you ate here? I've never been more disappointed with a restaurant in my entire life, and I was a New Yorker living in LA for 4 years, so that's saying a lot. It takes a ton of effort for me to come to Brooklyn, especially to try food, but I felt compelled after seeing all the stellar reviews and knowing the chef is a former Alinea alum, a place I enjoyed very much.

The place is super casual, but I wouldn't expect anything more from Brooklyn. We started off with the oysters, which are nothing special, and the popcorn monkfish, which could have been deep fried anything and it would have tasted the same. The carrot crepe that everyone raved about was underseasoned- I would have preferred to just have the cooked littleneck clams that came inside. The Yakitori was appalling- reminiscent of when I attempted to cook chicken for the first time in college on my illegal balcony grill. There are no words left for this disgusting dish. The rutabaga tagliatelle is nothing like real pasta and crunchy, though at least seasoned. 

Only redeeming qualities were the rosemary cocktail I had and the outdoor patio where you can go roast marshmallows for s'mores, though this has been done a billion times over in West Hollywood. Wish we could have eaten out here the whole time, but my view of this place can't be changed. So beyond disappointed. Back to Manhattan I go and will forever remain.

Completely agree with D s's review a couple down. Bad food. Mediocre service. Completely over-hyped and over-priced. You know when you leave a meal wanting to finish it off with a slice of pizza, then it was a bad meal.

This is a wonderful, magical experience that I won't go on too much about as I'm sure you can read others' reviews.  But I had a delightful birthday dinner at Olmsted.  It has a casual, neighborhood vibe with really delicious, delightful dishes that leave you with a smile on your face and a desire to return.  The dishes I enjoyed the most were the picked vegetables (fiddlehead ferns that day), Morgan's meats (a nice meaty pate with spicy mustard, chives and pickled cabbage), chawanmushi (intensely briney and delicious), and rutabaga tagliatelle (sooo indulgent and rich and a must order).  The duck chakna and carrot crepe were also tasty but less of a wow for me.  I know people go on and on about the carrot crepe and it was visually stunning and light and delicate and full of sweet carrot flavor but it didn't leave as much of an impression on me as other people.  My least favorite dish was the soft shell crab which was still good but I felt the charred ramps and sauce overpowered the crab.  To finish the meal, we sat in the garden which is outfitted with heat lamps and blankets and had the frozen yogurt lavender honey which was light and airy with just the right sweet floral notes.  The outdoor area is a lovely, cozy atmosphere where you can view plants that contributed to your meal and feel like you're in your own urban oasis.  The service was top notch as well.  Our waiter was extremely knowledgeable and believable in his recommendations and the wine he suggested was excellent.  The guy working the garden was the best sport.  I'm sure he gets the joke about eating the quails in the garden at least five times a night but he laughs politely and responds as if it's the first time he's asked every time so kudos to him.

Not much to add that others have already said.
Five star for Brooklyn.
Yes, reservations are a bit tricky. No real advice there apart from being a bit obsessive.
Here's what I liked:
- Small but well curated wine list and backbar.
- Fun little menu folded like a letter to the guests.
- Warm and friendly waitstaff
- Delightful presentations. I won't give descriptions as I don't want to ruin the surprise (and actual delight). A number of dishes are just very cleverly presented.
- Generally very tasty.

If I were to review only the service and the wine list, I would issue five stars. Impeccable service, excellent wine list, with many moderately priced bottles that were most unusual.

The food was frankly forgettable. It was well prepared but not distinctive. I don't get the hoopla.

A dinner for two at this place burned a hole in my wallet and cost me maybe 2 weeks worth of groceries but I would come here again in a heartbeat. 

Arrived here on a MONDAY (HELLOOO WHO GOES OUT ON A MONDAY ) at 7PM and told the next earliest seating was at 9:30PM. I was pretty hungry then and almost cried. Luckily, they give you the option to hang out in this beauuuutiful outdoor garden/bar in the back - think Christmas lights strung above you, small benches with portable heating encircling a small herb garden, and wooden crates with flowers and greenery behind every bench. We went when it was ~55 degrees outside, but the garden was pleasantly warm. They'll also give you blankets if you ask for them. In this garden, you can order wine, cocktails, hors d'oeuvres, desserts and weirdly enough, a $20 make-your-own smores kit over charcoal... (There were a lot of people making smores - they give you a lot of marshmallows but we didn't think it was worth $20 to relive childhood at a date-y restaurant but maybe its a thing). I easily could've stayed in this garden for 2 hours waiting for a seat in the actual restaurant with these amenities (snacks/drinks, etc), but we were called in for a seat within 1 hour. 

All of the dishes were beautifully presented and our waiter was super patient in explaining everything to us. The portions are tiny and each dish is pretty pricey. 

I heard the menu changes very frequently but we ordered: 
-Crab Rangoon: These crispy dumplings came in a Chinese takeout box with a sweet-sour dip on the side. Was surprisingly able to taste the crab! Wasn't our favorite thing on the menu because the dishes that followed blew this out of the water. 
-Duck Chakna: I thought chakna was always a stew, but this came as 3 things - a bowl of duck and thinly sliced red cabbage, a citrusy sauce, and 2 pieces of naan bread. We made a taco out of these three things and it was absolutely delicious - warm, refreshing and savory.  
-Pork Collar with broccoli and mustard sauce: THIS. WAS. AMAZING. If you order anything here, you should try to the pork collar. This dish took the longest to come out of the kitchen, but the pork was incredibly tender and delicious, and the mustard sauce complimented the grilled broccoli and pork so well. It was pure joy eating this. My boyfriend said the meat reminded him of waygu beef. 
-Lavender Frozen yogurt with honey (ordered in the garden): I thought this mix of sour and sweet felt super strange during first few bites but this dessert grew on me. It's also beautifully presented, with a few lavender flowers above a honey-lavender whipped cream which sits above a scoop of frozen yogurt. 

In terms of cocktails drinks, I really liked the Soba! Most of their cocktails are named after herbs - probably because of the whole farm-to-table theme they have going. Otherwise, they have a pretty limited wine list. They did have an assortment of tea to choose from though! 

The interior decor was very homey and very "green" - think plants and vines over the walls, wooden walls, slightly dimmed lighting... I enjoyed it so much I spent more than 3 hours at this restaurant on a Monday night. Maybe that's why their wait times/reservations times are so awful - you just don't want to leave!!

So I was going to wait to review this place until I actually ate dinner there, but the positive experience that I had here prompted me to share. I went there during early evening on Wednesday. I didn't have a reservation and was totally cool with the option of sitting in their lovely garden. We ordered some cocktails. We were a group of 4 and we each ordered a different one so I was able to taste each unique concoction! I loved their smoky Mezcal cocktail! Their garden featured all of their freshly grown herbs and veggies, all of which make an appearance in their farm to table dishes. They even had a little hen house. I was at ease and the world made sense again!

Make sure you get a reservation if you can! This place is really small so don't bother trying to bring a ton of friends, keep it under group of four!

My husband and I did a walk in - the wait was about an hour so we dropped our number and went to some of the bars down the street. We were starving so decided to get an app elsewhere - big mistake because everything here was so delicious!

We sat at the bar (tables are for reservations only) and our bartender / waiter was so knowledgeable and friendly! We ordered and loved most of his recommendations. Definitely get the frozen yogurt!!

We will most definitely be returning this summer and trying the backyard s'mores!

Had a really nice evening here, though I must admit I expected a little more, with all the buzz. 
Made reservations a month in advance, after I was assured they can accommodate vegan patrons. Hopped on a taxi and took the 45 minute drive from Manhattan to Brooklyn. 
Husband and I arrived a little early and were offered to wait in the lovely garden in the back of the restaurant. It was a little chilly so we opted for some tea and fried vegetables and happily excepted the warm blankets offered to us by our lovely server. This was the best part of our evening. 
The back yard is a charming little garden, music was great and overall really nice ambiance. 
After a while our table was ready and we were seated inside. We were offered excellent bread and olive oil and enjoyed it with some beautiful red wine. 
Our meal was quite nice, though no dish knocked us off our feet. We appreciated their vegan friendly attitude and for that and the lovely setting at the garden I will grant the restaurant 4 stars.

Believe the hype. It's small plates, so we tried almost everything on the menu. Everything we ordered was fresh and full of flavor. For such a popular and well-rated place, it's reasonably priced.  It can be really tough to get a reservation, but if you go on their website during the week, they seem to often have spots around 10pm for the same night.

Everything was amazing - food, drinks, dessert, service. 

It lives up to the hype and is way worth the price. My partner and I got wine, 2 small plates, 2 large plates, and dessert all for $100. Impressive.

Excellent foods. I tried every single courses in the menu, even the easy thing like fried pickle or snap pea sushi are so flavorful. Carrot crepe are phenomenal. Main course grilled scallops and trout no word to discribe. Desserts old school chocolate mousse are yummy!!!! Absolutely come back!!!!

Second time here. Do you know why it's considered one if the best restaurants in NYC? Because it is! Everything, absolutely everything is done right. Each course is so well thought out down to every single detail: the copper napkin rings, thin pottery dishes and cups, hanging plants and herbs, beautifully crafted plates. Service & staff is top notch, make you feel noticed and pampered without being overbearing. So cozy and consistently good you never want to leave. It's so rare when a place gets everything right. Cocktails and entrees are prepared with unparalleled artistry. Thank you Olmstead. Tip: having trouble with reservations, try the seats by the kitchen - best seats in the house.

Items Selected:
Rhubarb - Blanco Tequila, Lime, Bitter Orange, Salt Foam, Tonic
Crawfish Boil Crackers
Morgan's Meats - Pork Rillettes, Pickled Red Onions
Popcorn Monkfish - Aioli
Chawanmushi - Nori, Crispy Scallions
Duck Chakna - Red Lentil Naan,  Pear Chutney
Carrot Crepe - Little Neck Clams, Sunflower
Rutabaga Tagliatelle - Burgundy Black Truffle, Brown Butter
Sauteed Soft Shell Crab - Pickled Peppers, Ranch Dressing, Ramps
Horizonte - Columbia
La Joya - Ecuador
Caramel Apple Donuts - Salty Caramel Sauce
S'mores - Housemade Marshmallows, Artisan Graham Crackers, Hershey's

Owned and operated by Greg Baxtrom and Ian Rothman out in Prospect Heights, the concept at first seeming much the same as many with a Chef-driven menu based on seasonality, Olmsted differentiates itself from the pack by way of a backyard Garden and living wall from which many of its ingredients are sourced, the 50-seat space a near-impossible reservation after receiving attention as a Best New Restaurant contender at the James Beard Foundation Awards.

Named after a deceased local architect, the narrow and straight space leading to a garden where a fire-pit offering Drinks, small Bites and a special Dessert experience offers additional seating for approximately a dozen, those visiting Olmsted will be greeted promptly at the hostess podium where reservations are confirmed before being led to one of many wood tables, the noise level near the front far more quiet than at the back, in part due to the location of speakers and in part due to the fact that the bar and kitchen lie along the same wall, which thus compresses many of the tables against a brick wall lined in Plants. 

Open as a first-come-first-serve restaurant on Mondays only, the other days booked as soon as reservations open via the website, it was after getting comfortable that menus were presented along with verbalized daily specials and a clipboard Cocktail list, the prices occasionally precocious, though the presentations and flavors are frequently on par with several of New York's top fine dining establishments.

Beginning with a Cocktail and Water, the plates rustic and attractive though cups are unnecessarily small which necessitates servers leaving pitchers of water with the table, fans of innovative drinks have already made "Give Peas a Chance" a social media sensation, the Tequila-based "Rhubarb" not as photogenic but fresh and refreshing which paired well with Crawfish Boil Crackers that tasted exactly as they are named with the texture of Chicharrón while a daily dish entitled "Morgan's Meats" featured smooth shredded Pork served with Toast and Pickled Onions.

Continuing with "Snacks," Chef Baxtrom no stranger to crafting single bites with complexity and big flavor following stints at Alinea, Atera and Blue Hill at Stone Barns, Popcorn Monkfish offered a basket of lightly fried Fish alongside Radishes and a herbal Aioli while the daily special Chawanmushi executed on par with any experienced to date stateside, the Custard smooth and jiggly with the flavor of Shellfish and Mushrooms beneath fried Scallions and Nori added for texture.

Without doubt a global menu suited to concept of Vegetable-centric fare and sustainability, the newly famous orange Crepe with trimmed Clams, Sunflower Seeds and razor-thin Carrot slices as delicate and precise as anything one might see at Per Se, Baxtrom's best dish of the night came by way of the Indian-inspired Duck Chakna with confit Fowl ready to be loaded into Naan made with Red Lentils, the Soft-Shell Crab unfortunately a $22 disappointment that was overwhelmed by Peppers, the thick "Ranch" sauce sloppily placed on the plate and not really adding much to any of the other ingredients.

Appropriately impressed by the Rutabaga Tagliatelle, thin strips of the Tuber lightly steamed into al dente low-calorie Noodles and topped with sliced Black Truffles in Brown Butter, it was with two distinctly different styles of drip Coffee that a bag of Bombolini were enjoyed, the flavor not unlike that of a Cider Donut before being dipped into creamy Caramel Sauce, a fifteen minute wait quickly passed before the party of three was led out back to the Garden where sleeping Doves in cages watch diners place housemade Marshmallows on sticks before blackening them over a can of Embers and smashing them between Graham Crackers from a local Bakery plus a 50-cent Hershey Bar for twenty bucks, the cost largely related to time and taking up space rather than ingredient quality here, but worth it for the novelty and fun-factor.

Great restaurant. You must check out the back yard if you visit. It must be without question the best date spot on the planet. Just go back there and check it out.

Everthing around the food was 5 stars excellent. And half of the dishes were excellent. However, one dish was truly ruined: the shrimp were hammered. I was just in barcelona and had some of the best prawns grilled on the plancha. These were grilled and had a wonderful smoke and char but the meat was probably cooked for 2 to maybe 3 times too long? The chicken liver pate was served with 2 very sweet (no sour?) components. And the bread chips were so hard i thought I was going to go deaf. Had better chicken liver at Krupa the night before. Starting the meal with two dishes that would be subpar at any decent park slope place makes it impossible for me to give 5 stars. So sad. I could literally tell the shrimp were hammered just by picking them and feeling how hard they were.

The carrot crepe and trout were both 10s. So fresh, and interesting. Trout preparation reminded me of much more expensive meals. 

If you or I end up here again, don't order anything from the first "snacks" section.

Also, did I mention the back patio? 6 stars for the back patio area.

For a table of six, we ordered 3 appetizers, all 6 of the small plates, 4 main entree dishes, 4 desserts and all left a little hungry 

We constantly asked the server for her opinion on the amount ordered and she really should have recommended we course out our plates differently. Maybe we didn't enjoy the meal because we had a good 30 mins between every set of plates to idle and go through the wine. Feel like I would get a better meal elsewhere 

Liked the food but probably not enough to come back - would recommend the chawanmushi and the bluefish crackers

Had a very nice meal at Olmsted. Nice quality, seasonal ingredients, thoughtfully prepared and presented. Interesting cocktails that also were clearly seasonally inspired. 

I don't know if we hit them at an odd time, but we had a hard time choosing the right combination of dishes. Not a hard time because there were too many choice, but because there weren't enough that were totally of interest. The main meats on offer were a yakitori platter (3 skewers for $24 was a hefty price tag) and a cold pastrami platter (which appealed less upon arrival at the table next to us than that even sounds on paper - the whole point of pastrami is the luxurious fattiness in a warm, oozy sandwich. Cold pastrami is like a day without sunshine).

We were instructed to order 2 small, 2 medium, 2 large dishes. It was at least 1 large too many, particularly because at least 4 of the dishes were served with crackers, bread or some other bread like component, which were nice but very filling. Liked the duck mousse and the snap pea sushi, the bluecrab dip was very taste. The carrot crepe was very pretty and a surprisingly interesting plate. The two mains we had did not blow us away.  Scallops were a sadly humdrum affair with a very odd presentation. For $23, I expected better. One scallop was about 2/3 of the scallop in one piece, and the other was two poorly cut pieces. Not even 2 scallops and maybe 2 pieces of mushroom in a broth. For all the talk about making this an affordable neighborhood option, we felt a little cheated on that one.

The english pea falafel was served with a wonderful labneh, but I'd take Taim over this any day at 1/3 of the price. We also agonized a bit over even ordering something like this here, but frankly, the other options on offer just didn't appeal. We expected more.

So, that said, we will definitely consider another go at Olmsted in the future, when their seasonal menu is more in line with our expectations.  It's a very nice place where they clearly take great care with their food and the service.  We look forward to a time when the menu has better main options on offer!

Total class act.  Most memorable meal I've had in NYC in years.  Each dish was more delicious than the last, perfect presentation.  Our bartender Kelvin was a legend, serving up the interesting menu items (frozen peas suspended in an ice cube!) as well throwing together cocktails with esoteric ingredients that somehow blended perfectly (escubac!).  Everyone was kind and patient, so the meal never felt rushed along.  Left happy, full, and tipsy.

You're going to want to try as many dishes and drinks as you can.  So it's definitely priced at the special occasion level (but great value).  Very difficult to get a reservation, and we'll keep trying.

First off, this is a very trendy spot. How do I know that? Because there is a wait for reservation and you HAVE to make a reservation if you want to eat here or maybe just wait for the hype to die down?

I came here with 3 other girlfriends at 5:30pm on a weekday and it was packed! The space is small with some outdoor seating in the backyard (weather permitting). In fact, you can see the kitchen tucked in the back, that's how small this place is. But it has a very cozy vibe and it's lighting is very dimmed so not the greatest at taking pics for instagram. 

For a table of 4 girls, we ordered an appetizer to share and a main dish and drink each:
Popcorn monkfish (app) - super tasty or we were super hungry since no pics were taken which means we devoured this within 30 seconds of it arriving on our table.

Carrot crepe with littleneck clams - this seems like their signature dish since everyone orders it. I thought it tasted great but wish it had a few more clams to it. The clams were more like a garnish than an ingredient.

Grilled Scallops - 4 pieces with a bit of salad. I had to look again to make sure I ordered the entree and not an appetizer. The scallops were grilled perfectly without being chewy or rubbery but this was nothing special in my opinion. 

Rutabaga "Tagliatelle" - I thought this dish fell short for sure. It was the least favorite among the dishes we ordered because it was over salted. I do think once a dish is over salted, there's not much you can do to save it.

Guinea hen confit and roasted: This dish surprised me the most because I always feel chicken dish are ordinary and nothing special. This was flavored just right and it was not dry at all, even the roasted version. The sauce it comes with is amazing.

Overall: I think the food was really good minus 1 dish but we did leave still slightly hungry. For the price, I say it's an experience and a nice place to have dinner out if you feel like splurging. Definitely not your everyday dinner spot for sure.

I had been wanting to try Olmsted since Pete Wells raved about them nearly a year ago. Reservations have to be made wayyyyy in advance, but I was somehow able to score a res for 4 at 8:30 on a Sunday. Maybe the 4th of July weekend had us lucking out, since everyone was gone from the city.

Olmsted is gorgeous--plants line the walls and their outdoor garden in the back, where they get some of the produce they serve in the restaurant, also has cocktail tables outside. The crowd was bizarre--it was a mix of normal people and some of the absolute worst in Brooklyn hipster that I've seen. People kept going out to the back, and every one kept looking more and more bizarre (I'm talking about you, man in striped suspenders and a straw hat). 

ANYWAYS, that's beside the point. The waiter said a light meal was 4 items from each portion of the menu (snacks, appetizer, entree) and it wasn't common to do the entire menu. We ordered 2 snacks, 3 apps, and 3 entrees, and it was more than enough. Honestly, this made me feel like he was pushing an upsell...not a great thing for fine dining.

So, besides that, everything was immaculate. The crawfish boil crackers, seemingly made from puffed rice, were delicious. Fried pickles--all kinds of pickled vegetables--were wonderful.

The crispy fried pork belly came with a delicious, homemade buckwheat cracker on top, and it was delicious. The bluefish salad was incredible--perfectly cured, and it tasted like it was just smoked. The way the cold wafted from the salad was quite pleasing to the eye. The carrot crepe was weird, amazing, and wild. You should get it.

Entrees were the same. Delicious English pea falafel with fresh mini pitas and labne were delightful. The house-cured pastrami was truly, truly excellent, and the pieces of potato underneath were a real treat. The showstopper, though, was the trout. The emulsion with trout roe was unreal, and the trout--wrapped in chard--was flawlessly cooked and executed.

We were stuffed from that (not 4-4-4, but 2-3-3), but still shared the chocolate mousse. It was simple, classic, and delicious.

SO, why 4 stars? Well, I didn't like the upsell, and although Olmsted was delicious, I still can't come close to putting it above (or on par) with Battersby. When the menu changes, as it undoubtedly does with the season, I will definitely be back. Maybe they'll get that magical 5th star.

tl;dr: Make reservations way in advance. Absolutely delicious. Not quite as good as Battersby. Go there now.

Delicious and thoughtful food. We sat at the kitchen counter and it was amazing to see how hard the chefs worked to put together these magical and artful dishes. The owner (I think it was Greg but I could be wrong) checked every single plate that left the kitchen. The wait staff were all kind and helpful and swooped in and out with food and drink so seamlessly. Our neighborhood needed a restaurant like this and yes you need to reserve well in advance but at least they take reservations. Looking forward to going back and trying the rest of the menu.

Olmsted might just have one of the most pleasant little gardens in all of New York. The setup they have using the garden as a pseudo waiting/snack area is awesome. I could easily go through an hour wait time for a table just hanging out in the garden. It also looks like you can buy the garden ingredients to take home in a nicely branded planter. The service while we were in the garden was also fantastic and attentive.

Things shifted a bit once we got to the dining room. After being in the garden, the dining room can be a little underwhelming. That's nothing to complain about because the food is what you're there for and it is all delicious. 

My one actual complaint however was the service in the dining room. The time between dishes was really uneven and affected the overall experience. Our starters came out fairly quickly and things were rolling smoothly. Crab Rangoon and the BLT were both excellent. Then we waited about 20 minutes for the carrot crepe. The crepe was fantastic. Maybe the best thing we had all night. But it's a small and light dish which was sandwiched between two 20 minute gaps with no food. 

If they can get the timing right, the food here is maybe one of the best deals in NY compared to what you get at a tasting menu. Incredible quality ingredients and flavors. I will definitely come back!

We've been wanting to go to Olmsted for a long time, and we were definitely not disappointed. The restaurant itself and the garden are beautiful, and the entire place just feels completely comfortable. The service was friendly and helpful too.

For our party of two, we ended up ordering 2 snacks, 3 smaller plates, and 2 larger plates along with 2 desserts and it was definitely enough food. Along with the regular menu that you can find online, they also brought over a clipboard with yakitori selections and a chawanmushi special, which ended up being our favorite dish all night. The rich flavor of the dashi, the perfect texture, everything about it was fantastic.

Other highlights included the pastrami which came with sides of slaw, potato salad, and cornbread. The mustard sauce that came with the pastrami was really tasty. We also liked the English pea falafel in part because of the fluffy bread that seemed to also have peas mixed into the dough, the bluefish salad which was packed with flavor, and the carrot crepe which was so unique and well-executed along with looking like a piece of art. Both desserts we got - the yogurt with lavender honey and soft serve (vanilla lilac and sour cherry swirl) were the perfect ending to the meal.

While we had an overall wonderful experience, not every dish worked for me, although that might have more to do with personal preference. While tasty, I found the crawfish boil crackers a little too salty. My least favorite was the duck liver mousse as it was just too sweet for me, but the server said it was a really popular item so that might just be me. My cocktail seemed to be more ice than drink, which was initially nice because it was hot outside, but I wouldn't get that again. Even with all this though, I still give it 5 stars because overall it was a great dinner.

We definitely want to return to Olmsted, especially in other seasons so we can experience different things on the menu. Everything is seasonal and a lot comes from the backyard garden, so I'm hoping we get to try an entire new slate of dishes when a new season rolls around.

It's ok. A bit overrated. Decent food, creative but not that creative to justify the price. Service was excellent. Still...prices too high and portions too small and music and talking too loud. We got the carrot clam crepes (pretty good but tiny) and trout (really good but needed microsocooe to see it) and the scallops. Decent but not worth paying $15-$20 for 3 bites. They are very creative dishes, I will give them that. Creative is one thing. And "delicious to die for" is another. They get the first but not the second.

we thought there were several standout items, the drinks and desserts in particular - everything we had was quite good - but were underwhelmed by the food. we ordered nearly everything on the menu at our table. there were a few standout items, while the rest was good but not on par with the rest. 

i was pleased, don't get me wrong. i think i just expected more due to all the hype.
the service was simply flawless.

faun opened up nearby too and we were wowed by the food there more.

i would go back, perhaps we caught them at a non-stellar moment? but if you're wondering about the hype, feel free to come back to this when the hype's died down a bit. also if you're booking a resy, i would suggest booking a party of 4. they mostly have tabletops of 4. or eating at the bar first come first served.

Everything was delicious! The watermelon sushi was luscious and refreshing. The carrot crepe amazing.. Serrano wrapped trout - melt in your mouth.  Also a nice selection of wine by the glass, as well as attentive and thoughtful service. I plan to go back as soon as I can get another reservation.

I've only heard great things about this place and getting reservations is almost impossible so when I was finally able to get a table, you could only expect my excitement and anticipation to be over the roof. However, I can say I was pretty disappointed. 

Yes, clearly the quality of the ingredients is extremely high, but a lot of the dishes tasted like things I could honestly put together at home (minus the presentation skills). That's not to say it's a bad thing, but maybe it's not worth the waiting a month for a table and overpaying for the food that you could easily make in your own kitchen. Regarding price, this place is not that expensive, it's a solid $$ according to Yelp standards, however, how much you're getting for each dish almost feels like you're being ripped off-- particularly with the entrees.

We ordered the yakitori which was about $24, and only comes with three skewers of your choice. The yakitori was pretty delicious, however it's just so ridiculously overpriced for the amount you're getting. It does come with a small spicy eggplant dish and a small radish dish. The spicy eggplant tasted like it was doused in Tabasco sauce and frankly it offended me because this is kind of a classic example of a chef trying to cook Asian dishes without a full understanding of the spices and ingredients that go into them. We also ordered the roast beef carpaccio entree and honestly why would anyone ever thing to put a deli meat item on a menu at a fine dining restaurant like this? It didn't taste too bad, but it is fair to say i was extremely disappointed. 

The redeeming qualities of this place was that the kale crab Rangoon was absolutely delicious and I would probably come back for the lavender frozen yogurt alone. The Yuzu cocktail was also delicious. The service was great as well, our waiter noticed we did not finish our roast beef carpaccio and asked for feedback. He did mention it was a new dish and when I told him honestly how I felt, he thanked me for the honestly. And he even took it off the menu which was extremely kind of him because we weren't expecting it! 

I will try to give this place another shot. Before coming, I read more recent reviews stating how this season's menu is a little mediocre than past seasons, so I'll try to come back in the winter and hopefully will have a better review for you! 

We ordered the kale crab rangoon which was probably the best thing I had tasted

Had this place on my radar since they opened but found it impossible to get a reservation. After showing frustration to my boyfriend for months on wanting to go here he surprised me with reservations here for my birthday. No idea how he swung it but I don't care. The wait was well worth it. The food was beyond amazing! We were there in March but I know their menu switches up depending on the time of year and what food is in season. What sold me though was desert, we did the s'mores. They take you out to their backyard and set you up with your own little mini fire/coal tin to make s'mores while snuggling under a blanket. If anything just pop in to do that in their backyard while sipping wine if you find yourself not able to get in for dinner. However, try and make reservations to eat here, it's worth it!

So overhyped.

I've been wanting to come here forever because I'd heard good things, and their garden looked so cute and perfect for a summer evening.  We got there early so they offered for us to go to their garden for a cocktail.  We sat down..and waited...and waited...for someone to come take our order, and then waited...and waited...again to get our cocktail (I think we got there at 7:30 for an 8:00 reservation (with the knowledge that we wouldn't be seated until our reservation time, so that part was totally fine) but we didn't get our drinks until probably 8:15, at which point we were escorted to our table only a couple minutes later.  Also, I was carrying my bag and jacket, and my cocktail was in a coupe glass that was almost spilling as I was walking to the table, and the server didn't offer to carry it for me, which was a little weird but again, no big deal).

We ordered the watermelon sushi, kale crab rangoon, and carrot crepe to start.  We were going to order 2 mains, but didn't really find any of the options that enticing, so we just settled on the serrano wrapped fish.  The sushi was very refreshing, and the rangoon was good, but neither wow'ed me in the slightest.  The carrot crepe was my favorite but such a teeny tiny portion, I basically forgot what it tasted like immediately after, because it was gone in a couple bites.  The fish entree was unremarkable.

For dessert, we had the chocolate mousse (fine, not great) and the lavender yogurt.  The yogurt was a perfect summer dessert, super light and tart - like an elevated version of pinkberry.  I liked it a lot, but not enough to come back here for it given how underwhelming the rest of the meal was.

On top of it all, service was horrible.  I can kind of excuse bad service in the garden, because a) we were early and b) it's out of the way, so it's not like there's a waiter there the whole time.  But once we were seated at our table, our waitress seems so uninterested in serving us, it was bizarre.  It was impossible to get any water - we must have had 6 different people come to our table before anyone refilled our cups/pitcher - and at one point, our waitress started taking our order and then just trailed off and got distracted for a good minute before turning her attention back to us, without any acknowledgment that she'd just cut us off and ignored us.  The people who cleared our tables and brought us our food seemed friendly enough, so maybe it was just her, but she was so unprofessional that it really detracted from our dining experience.  I understand that restaurants are kind of hectic and waiters can be busy juggling a lot of tables...but she was just standing around talking to the host the whole time, not doing anything.  It was certainly off-putting, and not the level of service I expect from that caliber of restaurant.  I'm bummed because I really wanted to love this place, but I just didn't.  Oh well.

Easily the best restaurant I've ever eaten at in Brooklyn. Like the Brooklyn version of Estela. They make the best small, shareable plates I've ever had. The carrot crepe is so unique. The squash rings are so simple yet so incredible. The scallions with corn was so tasty and juicy. The sickest part was I enjoyed the dessert way more than the meal. The lavender and honey yogurt is the most refreshing dessert in New York City. The smores, though over priced, are so good. The peanut butter and jello is simple tasting but the presentation of it is great. Easily one of my favorite restaurants ever.

After waiting months for a reservation for two, we finally secured one at 10 pm on a Friday night! The garden was beautiful, and the cocktails really good. When we came inside for dinner I was impressed with the decor and food presentation. However, the food itself is over hyped. While we were impressed with a few dishes (namely the carrot crepe and watermelon sushi), the others were just ok, especially considering the price we paid for them. I would've given this place 3 1/2 stars, if Yelp allowed for half star ratings.
Spectacular, inventive food and great service in a relaxed atmosphere. Go often and enjoy. World class!!!!

Great restaurant to go to for a special occasion. Try to get there a bit early to sit in the back garden with cocktails and delicious appetizers. Small portions but very memorable dishes. I had the oysters, grilled pork belly and scallops. For dessert we had the chocolate mousse. All of these were the best dishes I have ever had.

Came here on a weekday around 6pm. Was told there was a 2 hour wait. Sure thats fine, so we head on over to the backyard garden area to wait and have some appetizers. Nice seating area- we decided to order crawfish crackers, and snap pea sushi. Crawfish crackers were delicious, flavorful and crispy. Definitely wish there were more pieces! Snap pea sushi was ehh, but refreshing. 

After a long wait, we were finally called in for seating. We ordered the carrot crepe. dry rubbed scallops, and the trout. Let me tell you, if you are hungry or impatient. This is not the place for you!! Each dish takes forever to come and the kitchen in my opinion is too small for the amount of people being served. Portion size is laughable for entrees. But really I will be basing my review on the flavor. 

Carrot crepe- Tasty rich flavor, the sauce that its served in is delicious. Serving size I would describe is like a small tapa plate. There were a few pieces of garnish on top that didn't go well with the dish.

Dry rubbed scallops- Scallops came in a single skewer (3 pieces) with a side of dipping sauce. Scallops were extremely small. They were like the size of 1 scallop cut up into 3 pieces. For $20, I would expect a little larger portion size.. However the scallops were delicious. The dipping sauce went well with it. 

Trout- This dish was super delicous!! I just wished the serving size wasn't like two bitefuls. Fish was buttery and moist. Spinach fresh, and the sauce is to die for. Took almost an hour to come though. 

Overall ok experience. Food tasted great, but portion sizes leave you wanting for more! My advise, don't come here on an empty stomach or if you are on time constraint. Expect a long wait on eveything.

Everything you've heard about Olmstead is true. After trying for a few weeks to get reservations, we decided to just aim for walk-in bar seats. We arrived around 7:30pm on a Thursday hoping for two spots at the bar, and were able to get in after about a 30 minute wait. The service was incredibly friendly, and every single thing we had was delicious - two snacks, two small plates, and one large plate was sufficient to fill us. The highlights were definitely the kale crab rangoon, the carrot crepe (which they sent to us accidentally, but told us to enjoy anyway), and the frozen yogurt. If you've been eyeing Olmstead for a while, hoping for reservations, the walk-in bar seats are a useful option.

Thank goodness we had a late afternoon pizza.  This was ridiculous.  Precious portions without very much even going on.  When yakatori is the main meal you'd better order everything on the menu first.  Left really hungry.  Service was very nice.  Definitely not worth all this hype.  The chocolate desert was delicious.  But wow, so silly.

I really do not get these reviews.  We were so glad we had a late afternoon pizza before dining here. Left there starving and had to pick up another pizza on the way home!   We've been to many 'shared plate' restaurants but this was ridiculous.  Minuscule precious portions and no punch of flavor to any of them.  We had a party of five and pretty much ordered everything on the menu. The chicken yakatori was really good but you definitely need an order to yourself. then there really is nothing left to order after you've spent so much time waiting for all these teeny little dishes which look so pretty but two bites its gone.   The chocolate mousse desert was great.  The service was fantastic.  Cute place too.  But seriously needs some help in the kitchen.
Ok --- The service and the staff  were delightful.    The food was good and we had a great time  and some great laughs making fun of the food.   [ I can't really explain that ]

The food is good. The aesthetic is charming and the attention to detail with dish ware is a lovely touch. However, the service style does not match the expectations set by the menu's complexity and price point. The service is friendly, but not terribly attentive or structured - very average. 
Dining at Olmsted, should not be discouraged. I did not received what I had expected in my overall dining experience, but I would say it's a good restaurant for the area. 
I recommend the Duck Liver Mousse! The honey on top is a great touch and the pickled melon is an excellent compliment.

Olmsted is a creative and beautiful New American restaurant in Brooklyn with a stylish dining room matched by a spectacular backyard garden. I managed to obtain a reservation for one at this highly sought after restaurant and was very impressed.

I began with raw oysters, which were covered in pickled beets, horseradish crema, and caviar. They were beautiful & quite possibly the perfect food.

Next, I had the "Green Eggs & Ham", which was trout brined like ham & diced. It was covered with green egg whites beaten until fluffy. Four brioche roasts were provided to smear trout upon. It was salty, but delicious like a hearty breakfast & a very creative plate. Today was the first day it was on the menu & a manager stopped by my chair to ask for my impressions. I thought this was a nice touch.

I finished with the dry rubbed sea scallops. They were topped with diced Serrano peppers. Cream corn sauce was for dipping. It was very spicy but delicious.

My only criticism is that Olmsted would benefit from a certified Cicerone and more extensive beer menu.

New York has endless array of outstanding restaurants, but I would love to visit Olmsted again.

After a bunch of mediocre overpriced food on our recent NY trip I wanted to end it with One Wonderful Meal and this was it!  It's hard to get a table but it was Sunday night and we were seated at the bar, with a wonderful server (and one not so charming when he took a break).  

Not only was everything we ate innovative and surprising, but it was also absolutely delightful and delicious!  And everything was served on and it the most wonderful hand made dishes, which seriously added to my experience for every minute I was there.  (If it hadn't been my last night, I would have rushed to the studio where it was made the next day!)

We had the Watermelon Sushi (only wished the slices of fish had been a bit heftier) which was a great combo I will try at home, slices of squash which were a fabulous textural and taste combination, a fantastic salmon tartare -- far from the usual take on this dish -- beautifully served in a little jar with crispy treats to spread it on, and Crab Rangoon Dumplings, yum!  My husband usually doesn't feel satisfied with a bunch of small plates, but even he was charmed and delighted with what we had here.

Looking forward to another trip to sample more at this lovely place, with a garden and little "farm" in the back yard!

Commitment is hard. You want to invest your heart and loyalty into something, but you don't know if they're going to be around. That's the deal with restaurants on Vanderbilt Avenue. 

The shelf life for a restaurant on Vanderbilt isn't long. Cooklyn, which was where Olmstead is, was such a hit. It had to last, NOPE! Vanderbilt is weird. One day it's all quiet. The next three Korean spots open within a week. 

I'm here to tell you Olmsted is here to stay. Promise! Whether or not you'll be alive the next time a reservation is available is another story. Seriously, please attempt to make one now. One might be available in six years. 

Kidding aside if you want to go sometime soon, I got two options for you. First, Mondays. Everyone's least favorite day of the week. Here, Mondays are no reservation. So you can just walk right in, and hope to snag a table. You're gonna wait, so you may want to go on the earlier side or wait till a lousy, cold, dreary day in which people don't like going out. (Survival is for the fittest) Your other option is to sit at the bar. First come, first serve. You have to get there right away though. Olmsted opens at five right now, but their hours can change, so be sure to check in with them or their website if you plan to do that. 

My first time there I got their early went for the bar seating. I personally enjoy bar seating so it was grand for me. Three of us perched up there and began our journey. The drinks here are top of the line. The cocktails are well designed and pack a good punch. I personally enjoyed the Lavender. 

We kicked our meal off with the cauliflower with pickled red onions. Excellent starter. If you can only get one small dish though, go with the mullet tartare. Simply delicious. The rutabaga tagliatelle was so good we got it twice. Well it was by mistake, but it's that good you may want to order two servings. The scallops were lovely. Not too filling but very tasty. Last we had the big hype dish. The guinea hen. This is their star, and it shines. Succulent, juicy, and tender. Paired with a sauce that compliments it perfectly. We ate every morsel. Make sure you get it. 

The space is intimate and pleasant. Beautiful store front. The service is impeccable. The bartenders and waitstaff are fantastic. All very nice and friendly. 

So if you're looking for a special place to book your special someone's next birthday, ehhh you might not be able to swing it here, maybe two birthdays from now you can get a reservation. Or just wing it on a Monday or right when they open. Either way, you have to come here.

For my money, Olmsted is the best restaurant in NY.  I'm sure you could pay $500 bucks/person for a mind-blowing omakase or tasting menu somewhere in Manhattan...but my wife and I shared six dishes and five drinks here for $140 plus tip last time.  The math is easy.  

Food-wise, the menu here has changed a bit over time, so it's hard to single out particular dishes as must have, with the exception of the carrot crepe.  I doubt they'll ever take it off the menu, and for good reason.  It tastes like the purest, butteriest carrot you've ever had, with pops of salt from the clams, and it's visually stunning when it arrives.  Other than that, I don't think you can go wrong.  We've never had a bad dish here, and they do everything well.  Standouts last time were the battered squash rings (somewhere between a healthy onion ring and an everything bagel), squash som tum (bracingly spicy), pork belly roulade (unusually soft, but still with the crispy seared flavor), and the chocolate mousse.  The "secret" yakitori menu is a new development.  I thought the flavor of the chicken thighs and the king oyster mushrooms was outstanding, but it was a very insubstantial dish for $24 -- maybe the first thing I've ever had here that wasn't great value for the money.

Drinks here are fantastic as well.  Can't go wrong with any of the cocktails (my wife's lemon balm was one of the best scotch drinks I've ever tried, and if you come in the fall/winter the warm drinks are nice), and the beer and wine are well-priced.  The rotating four taps are always interesting choices from great brewers (Kent Falls, Sloop, Troegs, etc) at $6-7 a glass.  

Yes, it's a tough reservation, but you can usually get a table at 9:00 pm or later less than a week out.  Service is always super friendly, especially at the bar.  Come early and have a drink in the backyard (it's beautiful and warm year-round), or move out there after eating for some s'mores after dinner.  Or both.  You'll probably want to stay for a while.

I'm so sad right now because I had been dying to try this place for a long time. However, I was massively underwhelmed. I will say, the cocktails are exceptional, the service was great, and the uni pierogis were frickin' incredible. Those are the reasons I gave it 3 stars. The rest of our meal was fine and unmemorable at best, and the trout was one of the most mushy and under-seasoned dishes I've seen. I'm glad I can now check this place off my list and not need to return. Unless someone wants to meet for drinks and pierogis.

The food rules. The carrot crepe and Lavander Yogurt were out of this world. 
The Duck Liver Mousse was a perfect first dish.
Cocktails were ok - nothing to die over and beer selection is Bad. No reason for a restaurant of this quality to have such bad beer. 

Food and Service were top notch though so i won't knock down a star for that. I didn't come for the beer, i came for the food and that was amazing.
Love it here! Constantly rotating dishes and great backyard, always a fun time! Crab Rangoon are a must, and Smores in the winter are a ton of fun.

Went here with a friend before heading to the Islanders game and was excited to check this place out after hearing so many great reviews.

After talking with the waiter, we decided to go with 1 snack, 2 medium plates, and 2 entrees--which was a good amount of food overall:

Popcorn monkfish (3.5 stars): I love monkfish. This dish did not disappoint, but obviously with a fish as flavorful as monkfish, I thought that some of that flavor was lost in the frying process. Still a good dish nonetheless.

Pierogies (4 stars): I can't quite put my finger on what makes this dish so pleasing to the palette, but we got them steamed and they were cooked perfectly. Each bite was flavorful--not earth shatteringly so--but very good.

Beef tartare (4.5 stars): This is apparently one of the newer items on the menu and it is bound to be a favorite. Though it has the looks of a classic tartare, the flavor with the broccoli and béarnaise sauce really provides an added layer.

Trout (4 stars): This dish was completely unique and unlike anything I've really eaten before as far as fish goes. The flavors really went well together and every bite was very fresh. That being said, the flavor was a bit limited and I wish I could taste a little bit more of the meatiness from the fish.

Lamb (4.5 stars): This is definitely some of the most tender and flavorful lamb I've had in the city. Though the dish is a bit on the small side, it packs a punch of flavor and was a great way to end the meal.

Overall, this place serves up some very good dishes and is great at creating a multi-course dining experience as they serve one plate at a time, keeping everything super fresh. The service was friendly and attentive and we were lucky enough to sit overlooking the kitchen, which was an added bonus. Definitely a solid place out in Brooklyn.

This place i so cute and fun. I recommend it to anyone. The food is playful and tasty. The starters are always delicious - it is hard to choose which ones to get. Occasionally, the scallops can be too salty but you really can't go wrong. The yogurt dessert is amazing. i wish i could have it every night after dinner

My boyfriend and I came here for our anniversary and had the most incredible meal. We sat at the bar and the bartenders were knowledgable on the menu and answered all our questions. The popcorn monkfish, cauliflower okonominyaki, and the bouillabaisse hot pot were very good. The sweet potato + uni pierogis (steamed) and Dave's trout were two of the best things I've ever eaten. After explaining my drink preferences, the bartenders recommended cucumber and rosemary cocktails. Both were incredible. We ended with the chocolate mousse, which was wonderful and rich. We can't wait to go back to Olmsted.

Return? Definitely, lived up to the hype
- Atmosphere 4: Intimate interior, cool outdoor space in the back (partial menu + drinks) 
- Service 4: Friendly, attentive
- Food 4: fiddlehead ferns (3), oysters (5), squash sum tum (5+ - delicious peanut sauce), pork belly (4+), scallops (5), yakitori (5 chkn skewer w/ veggies + mushroom sauce), choc mousse (5)
- Drinks: $11 rose, $9 tenuta mosole
- Cost: $145 w/ 4 wines before tax/tip - fed 4 people

So it seems like they worked out most of the service kinks from when they first opened and the food is still killer. Staff still has a bit of a "you're welcome" attitude but whatever. My only real problem now is the music is TERRIBLE and SO LOUD. Why do I want to listen to pop music I know the words to at my expensive dinner?! The music does not enhance the experience AT ALL. Maybe I wouldn't notice it if it weren't so so so loud? It's too loud. Guys? Turn it down please. 



I would give this place five stars for food and five for drinks and a whopping -1 for service.
They have no idea how to take a wait list and seat tables in an efficient manor. Hell, I haven't worked at a restaurant since college and I could have done a better job!
The server we had outside was snide and rude and had a lot of quips when we expressed concern that we'd be quoted 30 min and it had been an hour. 
The server inside was basically dead. They weren't excited about anything and having tasted the food there was a LOT to be excited about. 

Lastly, take care of people who live in the neighborhood and we will take care of you LONG after the droves of Manhattanites stop coming (and they will stop coming). We're good people and we wanna eat at your space. Remember us, cause we don't forget. 

1. Charcuturie pretzels good
2. Carrot crepe good
3. Guinea Hen good

Tried to go here for our anniversary which was a walk in only day... showed up 5 min after they opened and was told it would be a 2 hour wait... less than 1/4 of place had people sitting down.. tried to talk to the person at the front to only to be treated condescendingly about the situation... finally we just decided to leave... don't care how good your food is... made my wife cry... thanks for making our 1st year anniversary memorable!

Highly recommended, it is a beautiful restaurant. The food is unique and perfectly cooked. The service was little slow but beyond responsive. For a table of 2, we got 2 snacks and 3 plates. Save room for dessert as it is the best! We did dessert in the backyard and they setup a spot for us, highly recommend that you do drinks or dessert outside. They do have heat lamps. The backyard is so pretty, it really transports you and adds to the experience. 

Must get: chicken liver, all entrees are great, and honey lavender frozen yogurt.

I went for dinner for my birthday. It was quite difficult to make a reservation, but I was very excited to be able to get one and celebrate my birthday there. Restaurant is very nice, service is great. The food however...nothing special and some things actually taste bad.

- Duck Liver Mousse: There is honey on top of the mousse, which is revolting for anybody who loves pate. After I scraped the honey off, the pate is good, but nothing special. I've had better pate from several other places.
- Beer battered squash: There is this strange sweet glaze on top of the rings, which is topped by some seeds and toasted seaweed. As a result, you get this weird sweet fishy taste, which actually ruins the squash because it completely overpowers it. I scraped off the toppings, of which it was just a plain beer battered squash, which of course tastes good but is not special.
- Carrot Crepe: I actually hated this dish, because the crepe is sitting in this really strangely sweet carrot and orange sauce. In addition, I don't think that everything tastes good with the clams, and I don't think the flavors blend well together. 
- Tamarind glazed lamb: The lamb was actually good, but had such a large piece of fat (which is annoying because the piece of lamb is already small, and imagine when 1/4 of it is just pure fat). Honestly, it tasted like a good gyro from a food truck.
- Bouillabaisse hot pot: This was the special, which is mussels, scallops, and shrimp in a shellfish stock. The stock had an underdeveloped flavor and came with this weird aioli that made no sense. The best part of this was the homemade baguette it came with.
- Honey lavender frozen yogurt: So, the actual yogurt is plain greek frozen yogurt. Then there is this warm whipped meringue or something on top that is extremely sweet. The honey completely overpowers the lavender and is so sweet. I didn't even finish this because you can walk down the street and get significantly better dessert.

All in all, I don't think this place lives up to the hype. Go to Lilia instead - at least the food tastes good.

Olmsted has been lauded as the best new restaurant in NYC of the year, an honor that is well-deserved based upon the food.  We have dined here three times since it opened, most recently on Friday, 11/17.  The carrot crepe has been on the menu since the beginning, and should be on your table regardless of what else you order.  The current menu features a bouillabaisse that is finished at your table.  This has to be one of the finest dishes currently available in Brooklyn and will, hopefully, be a permanent part of the menu.  The wine list is deep and includes some unique wines priced fairly.  The sommeliere is knowledgeable and helpful.  

As others have pointed out, the reservation process is challenging.  The restaurant uses Resy and, it seems, tables book up four weeks in advance.  Because of the arrival of an unexpected, but cherished friend two days prior to our reservation, repeated attempts to add her to our reservation was made.  Unfortunately, there's no way to contact a human being at Olmsted and my emails went unanswered.  We took a chance and brought her with us at the time of our reservation.  The hostess made no effort, other than offering us a table nearly 3 hours later, to accommodate our guest at our table.  With embarrassment, she chose to take a taxi and sent her home.  We deeply regret that this occurred and it will color future visits to Olmsted.

On one occasion, we booked seats at the pass, with a view of the kitchen.  These seats are outstanding.  In addition, there is first-come, first-served seating at the bar.

Listed on the best new restaurants of 2017 by Bon Appetit, Olmstead has been at the top of my dining list for months. However, getting a reservation here is almost impossible.
