My boyfriend was finally able to snag a 5pm reservation here on a Sunday evening at the best seat in the house - the chef's bar looking into the kitchen where all the magic happens. 

The restaurant itself is beautiful and joins together the outside garden with the inside restaurant. Plants line the walls hinting at the fact that most of your food is actually harvested outside in the restaurant's well-tended garden. The restaurant, opened by Chef Braxtrom (who has experience cooking at Alinea, Per Se and Blue Hill at Stone Barns) and an exper micro-farmer, Mr. Rothaman. 

Every dish here is excellent and unique. The waitress recommended 4-6 dishes to share for 2 depending on our hunger level. We opted for 4 dishes - 2 smaller plates and 2 main courses. To start, we ordered the pierogis with uni and sweet potato and the cauliflower pancake. These were my favorite dishes by far we had all night. The pierogis were freshly made and melted in your mouth - definitely the best and most flavorful pierogis I have ever had. The cauliflower pancake was also unreal - a pancake that boasted flavors I have never tasted before. 

For the main course, my boyfriend and I shared the lamb and the fried chicken. I am not a huge fan of lamb but the lamb was tasty. However, the fried chicken dish was amazing. Portions for the main course were small though and I was really unimpressed that a main course chicken dish came with 2 measly pieces of fried chicken (for close to $30). 

That being said, I left full. The service was exceptional (our waitress constantly filled up our waters), and the food was delicious. Only complaint is that need to give you more food for the price. I understand the inventiveness and that that comes with a price, but really main courses should come with more food.

DO NOT GO IF YOU ARE A VEGAN, VEGETARIAN OR PESCATARIAN. Literally one of the worst meals we have ever received. We paid for a multiple course dinner and the vegan and vegetarian had to sit most of the courses out. Of course, we were told before making our reservation the restaurant "absolutely could" accommodate a vegan and pescaratian. The vegan was literally served a slice of potato on a plate (that was it!) and for dessert a "fruit platter" which was a bowl of sliced apples and CANNED MANDARIN ORANGES. The pescatarian didn't fare much better- a tiny piece of bland fish with mushy broccoli on top- nothing else- no sides, nothing. It was very insulting for the price. Meanwhile, the meat-eaters in our party had multiple courses and sides with their meals. Again, if you are a vegan, vegetarian or pescatarian stay far away from this place. Very disappointing. We left feeling insulted.

Rarely does a restaurant exceed expectations, but I think Olmsted was worth all the hype! I'm not sure why there are bad reviews on here, but people are entitled to having different preferences in food. My one complaint is that Olmsted is pretty expensive for the small portions, but the execution and imagination in the dishes are worth it for a special occasion.

Reservations are impossible to get-- prepare to hover on the reservation website (Resy) when they open to make reservations a month out. The service was excellent and courteous, the space was beautiful and inviting. The only thing that annoyed me about the restaurant is that in the winter, if you sit near the front door or near the back door to the garden, it's ALWAYS cold because every time the door opens, a gust of wind comes in. Anyway... that's beside the point. 

The food here is creative but balanced, which many "fancy" restaurants don't pull off successfully. I really enjoyed the exciting things the team here does with vegetables. The wine list is decent, and more than half the bottles are less than $60. For two people, we ordered two "snacks", two small plates, one entree, and dessert. It was more than enough food (we were plenty full), and we definitely could have done with one less small plate or without dessert. 

- The duck liver mousse is covered with a thin layer of honey instead of the usual aspic. I really liked the honey and savory liver mousse together. The mousse was one of my favorite things. 
- The beer battered delicata squash is delightful. It's wonderfully crisp, and the interesting seasoning on top (seeds, wild rice, seaweed?) is savory, umami, and not overpowering in the slightest and the squash still shines through. 
- The sweet potato and uni pierogies worked well with the sauerkraut on top. I personally prefer a traditional pierogi (heavy, comforting, and... cheap :)) If you do order this, it's better steamed than fried so you can taste the uni. Not sure I would order it again, but it was tasty nonetheless.
- The carrot crepe is beautiful and creative, but it's not something I'd order again. It's an interesting mixture of texture (soft and delicate crepe, chewy clams, and crunchy raw carrot ribbons) and flavors (sweet, savory, fishy), but I agree with some reviewers that it doesn't necessarily work well together. It's fun and interesting to eat, but I think the dish is just that. It's been on their menu since day 1, so it's worth a try if it's your first time here, but I wouldn't order it again. 
- Trout with creamed Brussels sprouts - Delicious. Didn't expect it to work, but the combination of everything was fantastic! I would definitely order this again. 
- I'm not a frozen yogurt/ice cream fan, but I ordered this because it's their signature dessert. It's refreshing and light. The frozen yogurt is a very smooth, slightly tart, greek frozen yogurt topped with a wonderfully warm, whipped light meringue of honey and lavender. The honey and lavender are nicely balanced, neither overpowering the other. I really enjoyed this dessert and it's a great thing to order if you want something sweet but light.

FYI - The garden is only for drinks and dessert. As of November, there is no "seating" outside for food.

Very unpretentious atmosphere. Food was amazing. Especially liked the outdoor seating in the back for drinks before dinner and s'mores out there for dessert. Can't wait to go back, they are always changing the menu. It was better than $250+ tastings I went to, I'll just leave it at that.

Olmsted is somewhere I'd been wanting to try for awhile, and I must say it lived up to the hype.  Olmsted is a completely unique restaurant, and it works great in its Brooklyn neighborhood, where it can exist on a quieter street with an amazing backyard garden.  Each dish was delicious and very impressively put together - nothing was simple - and it was a very fun dining experience.  It was a fun way to try lots of new things, and I'd like to come back as the menu is always changing.  It's definitely worth making a night of the dinner and hanging in the garden afterwards for drinks and dessert.

After a long, stressful day, there was nothing that could have been more comforting and cheery than a pleasant dinner at this neighborhood food sanctuary. Small and intimate, Olmsted represents so many of the best trends to be happening in the culinary world right now.

Service was immediately friendly, and I couldn't have been more chuffed to see smiling faces with genuine kindness. The bloke behind the bar steered me in all the right directions both on the menu and with the drinks. Both cocktails (the Rosemary and the Lavender) were exceptional and unique. I was immediately impressed on all fronts and my mood only improved when the dishes came.
  
Many of the ingredients used at Olmsted are grown in the backyard garden. The small plates are creative, balanced, and refined with an unpretentious nuance that is both comforting and pleasant to the senses. The menu is often changing but the Carrot Crepe is a mainstay for a reason. It's simply brilliant. You have to try it for yourself. I also heartily enjoyed the vibrantly seasoned scallops and, of course, the impressive frozen yogurt. The level of detail in dishes from beginning to end provides an enriching experience that also happens to be sensible to your wallet. 

I can't wait to be back in town because Olmsted is the first place I'm heading for Dinner.

This was one of the most uniquely fabulous restaurants we've been to in a long time.  The menu is innovative and puts foods together you've never in your wildest dreams considered.   The "tagliatelle is the bomb and should be your last main course!!  Highly recommend for food, drink and atmosphere.

Unreal food experience! I love eating flavor blowout food but I also like to be a tad healthy.  The eclectic offerings here, which are not long on options, are so across the world and healthy I was blown away.  Our waiter and the host were very sweet and welcoming making it a top notch night!

Beautiful room, excellent service, yummy and interesting food.  But their portion size is just laughable.  My wife and I split and appetizer, two entrees and a dessert.   (oh and the cocktails were superb).   our lamb was literally the size of two packs of gum stacked on top of one another!  so after we were done, we literally bought a slice of pizza each on the way home!  I don't mind spending big bucks at a restaurant.  In this case they should just charge more, and serve more food.  We had a good laugh about it later...it was like one of those  old movies when the blue collar guy goes to the french restaurant and they serve him one carrot on a huge plate!

I will say the food is tasty....but, if you have heard of the movie Downsizing--I think they forgot to shrink us before serving the tiny portions.  We left hungry, and had to go home and make (a real) dinner.

I was really excited about this restaurant because of the Bon Appetit review. It didn't really meet those expectations. 

The pierogies were the best dish that we had. They were well balanced and sweet. 

The chicken dish was tiny and not very impressive. For $24 it was two small fried chicken strips and a really small salad with dark meat. The salad was kind of salty and it was not enough food for that price. 

The lamb dish was kind of odd. It was two layers, a sausage layer and then pulled lamb meat. It was kind of like meatloaf and a little bit dry. The flavors were good but the texture was kind of strange. It was really small. 

Last, the best part was our waitress. She was excellent! The whole time she was attentive, knowledgeable and friendly.

The service at this restaurant is impeccable. Everyone is very friendly and knowledgeable about the food that is served. It was our first time here and we ordered three dishes to share. 

The fried squash rings were fried tempura style and coated with nori, wild rice and a green tomato paste which held it all together. They were served in this beautiful wooden bowl, which was very cute and dainty.

The second dish we tried was the cauliflower okonomiyaki. It was delicately made.

The third dish was the bouillabaisse. This was served hot pot style. The most fun part about the dish was the presentation. The broth was nice and flavorful, which was perfect for the freezing cold temperature outside. The seafood was so fresh-I especially enjoyed the scallops.

We also enjoyed soba tea, which was perfect for the weather. Lester was so nice to us and showed us great hospitality. He made us feel so welcomed. 

I would agree with other reviewers that the portions are small, but the feeling given in this place is quite remarkable and the meal is solid.

This place looks like your friendly little neighborhood spot, but it definitely lives up to its pedigree. The chawanmushi is a must try with it's perfect balance and umami. The carrot crepe little neck clams with sunflower was so good, we got two orders. The rutabaga tagliatelle had the perfect brown butter/butternut squash taste and the texture was "al dente with a crunch." A few things you can skip are: crawfish boil crackers, the lamb. If you're in Brooklyn, I think it's a must try.

Was really excited to try Olmsted after reading rave online reviews. My boyfriend made a dinner reservation about a month in advance. My verdict: good atmosphere and decent food but high price and small serving size seem are not worth the hassle of getting a reservation.

We tried oysters, cauliflower okonomiyaki (mayo, hazelnut), Dave's trout (creamed brussel sprouts, shaved hazelnut), a very seafood bare bouillabaisse, and some dish with broccoli that was so unmemorable I can't identify despite looking at the picture now.

I will say the cocktails were pretty cool. One of them used yummy frozen grapes as ice. The service was also good. Since it was my birthday, they gave us each a dessert amuse-bouche to start.

Probably won't be back for dinner but might be back in the summertime for a drink in the backyard.

I've been planing to go to Olmsted since the summer and I finally had the time to do it. And I'm very glad I did. Service was impeccable. The attention details can be noticed from the menu to the restroom. All the 5 plates I've tried are nothing less than amazing. I'm definitely going back to taste new flavors.

Have tried this neighborhood restaurant two times now, and found the food to be excellent and served with real professional aplomb by people who clearly are proud that they work there.  The menu is short and focused, so you are very much there to have the experience of this chef's cooking.  The chicken liver mousse that comes topped with a layer of honey and served with little crunchy brown toasts is really heavenly, and we had it both times.  A dish of root vegetables cut like thick ribbons of pasta, and sauced like pasta was also fabulous.  They only have three desserts, but one of them is 'smores cooked in their pretty backyard, which is really cool.

Amazing! Everything from the food to service to decor is excellent! Especially loved the wall of hanging plants and am told the back garden is beautiful but haven't been yet. 

Warmly greeted and seated right away with our reservation (made about a month in advance). Excellent cocktails (especially fond of the lavender bourbon cocktail!) and extensive wine list. Ordered the cauliflower okinomiyaki (great flavors, nice textures) and another special small plate they had that day (Japanese egg custard soup with celery root salad) which was a true winner. For entrees, had the trout - blew my mind, so delicious, melt in your mouth, and had the rutabaga tagliatelle with black truffle and brown butter - very creative and flavorful. Portions are on the small side, but for the flavor, service, and quality, I'm happy to go back.

This place was amazing -- they change the menu often so what I liked is almost certainly gone by now, but if they have a cucumber cocktail, try it! And if you are on the fence about some ingredient have faith, this is one of those places that you can trust to make magic combinations even out of things you normally don't fancy.

Great ambiance and definitely had a unique menu with lots of creative and original dishes. Came for a birthday dinner with my family and we ordered a ton of dishes to try. My problem was we were still not full by the end of the meal. For the prices, which are high, I would like to get a bit more bang for my buck. Service was excellent though.

What an amazing little nook on Vanderbilt. Amazing ambiance! Amazing service cant wait to go again.


Also, very vegan and veggie friendly

Have been trying to get a reservation here for awhile, was very much looking forward to it. In NYC it's so hard to keep all of the hype about a restaurant out of your head & just go in "neutral". So of course I had high expectations, but was mostly just looking forward to a great meal. What  I found was that it was good. Not blown away by any means, neither was my dining companion. I had the bouillabaisse and squash rings, they were both good, not amazing. I mean, this is a good neighborhood restaurant but not something to be stalking Resy @ midnight to score a reservation for.

One of the absolutely best meals I have ever had. We got a reservation 30 days before when they open them. It's located in prospect heights a becoming trendy Brooklyn neighborhood. The restaurant is the perfect size, mostly tables of two and a bar. The outside is a shared communal table around their garden but closed in winter. The waitress was nice but quiet, timing of service on and off fast and slow but the menu is SO unique and so delicious and actually filling. Every plate that came was better than the last. Our favorite was kale crab Rangoon and their oyster dish. Reasonable for the kind of food and casual vibe with plants, mismatched plates, and wood interior. Highly recommend.

Was it a bad night at the kitchen?? I read many good reviews about this place so was very excited when we were finally able to get a walk in at the bar on a Sat night after a few try. Ordered oyster, carrot crepe, kale crab, trout and pork. The only dish that we were wow'ed by was the carrot crepe. The other dishes weren't bad but lack the exquisite flavors one would expect from a chef who has worked at top high end places. Maybe he wasn't there that night?? Anyway it was disappointing.

I'm very sorry to give 2 stars but the dinner we had was not handled professional.

Unfortunately we came on a night where also the health inspector cam for a 'small' visit.

After 15min sitting & ordering the first round of drinks, he showed up! & after that everything stops! we were happy enough to get more tap water! The service tried to apologize with 1 glas of a nice riesling that the drinks will take a little bit much longer bc of the HI. Unfortunately we never got the drinks bc the bar was to afraid of the HI.
At least after 45min the kitchen decided to start cooking again, we ordered 2 snacks - the duck mousse & the Neo oysters - both very nice, duck packed with flavor but dense - oysters very fresh, nutty & refreshing. Than we start ordering almost all the plates ( except the one the staff told us not to: beets, kale salad, hot pot & the Gai Tod hat Yai ) All the food got send very quickly so that we had some hard time to keep up with the kitchen.
Everything we had was ok never something special or even up to the next new star.

I had the absolute best time here. I accidentally booked two seats for my five-year anniversary at the bar on Resy (d'oh), and to be honest was a little bummed at first that we weren't going to get an actual table. However, the bartender immediately made up for it. I'll update if I can remember his name, but he was absolutely wonderful, gave great wine recommendations, and was very attentive throughout the meal despite having, you know, a bar to take care of. He gave us champagne at the end of the meal because we'd mentioned that it was our anniversary, which was incredibly sweet, but I'd have given the service five stars regardless.

The food was also a total knock-out. The crab crackers were very good, but the kale crab rangoon was so excellent that I immediately considered another order despite having two entrees coming. The pork was tender and excellently seasoned, but the duck (prepared in two ways) was perfectly cooked and genuinely transcendent. I cannot recommend that dish highly enough.

We probably wouldn't have picked Olmsted for last night if I'd realized the only seats were at the bar, but I'm so glad we did! I know it's a little uncool to give the hundredth 5-star review to one of the only upscale spots in the neighborhood, but I literally want to go back tonight. Stellar service and food -- thanks!

The food here is excellent.
The service is great - the bartenders, servers and hostess couldn't be nicer.

However, on a recent Friday night we were served five courses in under 35 minutes. I understand the weekend rush, especially sitting at a bar, but when you're paying over $200 for a nice meal, the last thing I want is to feel like I'm being rushed out.

I spoke to the manager upon leaving and sadly he seemed to care less and said "we'll see you next time." without apology. Bummer, really wanted to love Olmsted since it had been on my list for so long. I will say eating the s'mores dessert outside was a highlight and very fun.

Pros: good wine list and wine prices. Cute water glasses

Cons: the service was nothing special; they accidentally spilled hot wax on our shoes (which was a bummer but accidents happen) but they didn't do anything to make it up to us like a free desert or comp us part of the meal. We didn't feel well taken care of at all. 

The food wasn't what everyone's been raving about! Every dish was overwhelmed by an extremely citrus-y sauce. I don't even remember what my entree was it was that unmemorable. My companion had the disappointing "duck two ways." 

I can't believe how much money we spent there, it felt like a huge waste.

The longer the wait and the higher the expectations, the greater the likelihood of being disappointed. So I was worried when I finally snagged a reservation at Olmsted. It was my number one Waitlisted Restaurant on Resy for God knows how long. Farm-to-table is my favorite kind of restaurant, the hype has been relentless and deafening, and the chef's pedigree (Alinea, Blue Hill at Storn Barns, Per Se, etc.) speaks for itself. In other words, Olmsted was created for me and me alone (obviously). So you could imagine my excitement when I got pinged for a 9:15 table on a Saturday--my reflexes have never been more swift. Now that I've come/seen/ate/conquered, I'm happy to report that I did in fact have the experience I was dreaming of, with some extra love and surprise thrown in there. The space is beautiful and earthy--the ideal Brooklyn restaurant. The execution on food here is a perfect example of why I always prefer small menus. Do a few things superbly instead of spreading efforts too broadly over too many options. The creativity, the flavors, the technique, the thoughtfulness, all of it translated in such a lovely, satisfying way. Yes, the portion sizes may have been smaller than usual, but the quality makes the price worth it. 

As I mentioned, the space is beautiful. Upon walking in, I was better able to understand why getting a reservation is particularly difficult: there aren't actually that many seats. While they now reserve bar seating as well, the space is pretty narrow and not too big overall. Even the kitchen is tiny! That said, there's a lovely garden in back you're free to sit in and apparently you can roast s'mores out there for dessert. I might need to return in the spring! 

As is the case with the food, it's pretty hard to go wrong here when it comes to beverages. While my original plan was to experiment with some natural wines, the cocktails looked too good to pass up on. If you appreciate masterful mixology, Olmsted has some talented folks behind the bar conceiving of/constructing these drinks. Similar to my favorite cocktail bar in the city, Mace, each of the cocktails here is constructed around one primary ingredient, thoughtfully complementing and highlighting it. My first drink was the Beet (Gin, Preserved Lemon, Maraschino, Juniper), which was superb. Gorgeous color, incredibly well-balanced and fresh. The bf got the Pear (Brandy, Cachaca, Lime, Escubac, Bubbles), which really did taste just like a pear. The Brandy/Cachaca combo worked beautifully with the fruit's flavors. My second drink was the Lavender (Bourbon, Herbs De Provence, PX Sherry, Black Walnut), which was delicious and unique. Really impressive.

The food, as I mentioned, was just as magical. The variety of techniques and styles employed, the creativity, the precision--it was a joy to experience. With a small menu and small plates in general, I really got to appreciate the meal on a more conceptual level than I usually do when I dine out. As a farm-to-table eatery, the menu reflects what's in season and it all comes straight from the garden. As I said, this place was made for me. Eats, below:

Duck Liver Mousse: A+
Like candy. With honey drizzled on top, this is easily the best liver mousse I've tried. Decadent perfection. I'm usually hot and cold on chicken liver mousse but there's no ambivalence about this order. Spread it on a crostini or spoon it right into your mouth. It's that good.

Kale Crab Rangoon w/ Sweet & Sour Sauce: A
Served dumpling-style in a classic, white Chinese food box, these were crispy, creamy, fresh and yummy. The least exciting of the night, but still delicious.

Red Miso Chawanmushi w/ Salsify, Smoked Egg Yolk: A+
From Chinese-inspired to Japanese-inspired. This is one of the most interesting dishes I've had to date. Flavorful, rich but still light, savory in a really unique way. 

Carrot Crepe w/ Littleneck Clams, Sunflower: A++
Melt-in-your mouth dreamy. You'll blink and this will be gone. Now, from Japanese-inspired to French-inspired. I can't keep up with you, Olmsted. Beautiful presentation, delicate but powerful. This one was magic. 

Brook Trout w/ Creamed Brussels Sprouts, Shaved Chestnuts: A++
I'm not sure if I enjoyed the fish or the accompaniments more. The Brussels/Chestnuts combo was served in its own dish and man, that could've been a standalone offering itself. Rich, warming, satisfying textures, excellent flavors. The fish was light and creamy, punctuated by more creamed Brussels on top. A fabulous way to dress up a seemingly ordinary type of fish.

Long Island Duck Grilled & Larbed w/ Watercress from the Wall: A+
No guinea hen on the menu in March but this was a pretty great runner-up. Not sure if this was Thai-style or more South American but either way, more worldly influence here. Cooked as well as I'd hope for and it's hard not to love that you can see one of its featured ingredients growing on the wall right next to you.

A meal to remember, well worth the wait.

worth the hype, the wait for the rezo and then some. the attentiveness and friendliness from the whole staff is just the right balance. i thought the carrot crepe was good but kind of freaked me out, also wasnt the biggest fan of the yogurt, but these are personal preferences and have nothing to do with quality or taste. my favorites were: the pear cocktail, crab rangoon(must and i dont even likecrab rangoon), scallops, but stand out of the night: tagliatelle. i mean WOW! thank you olmsted for an exceptional experience

From ethos to design to ambiance to the simple cleverness of each dish's conception and execution, Olmsted has earned my all time top 5.

We started with the beet cocktail and hot amaro out in the lovely heated patio with blankets. 

Our first course, served by a wonderfully warm and knowledgeable gentleman, was

The Duck Liver Mouse:
The rich, smooth duck is immediately rocketed in flavor by the sweet and savory schmaltz, which you spread onto crostini with a smashing salty crunch -- also served with pickled vegetables 

Then, we were served 

The Beef Tartar:
Essentially "steak and eggs" -- bottom layer of melting tartar, topped with a crumbled hard boiled egg layer, topped with béarnaise, and served with warm, slightly charred sourdough 

Then we had

The Beet Salad:
Long gold and purple ribbons, with shaved hazelnuts, and a pungent but complex blue cheese 

(I love that I get to keep writing "and then we were served...")

And then we we served 

The Trout:
Steaming on the plate, ready to be devoured, blanketed by an almost soufflé preparation of creamed brussels sprouts -- this is my wife's favorite fish dish of all time 

At this point we ordered another round and had 

The Pine:
Unveiled at the table to release a piney smoke, the large format is cube even had a sprig if rosemary frozen into it!

and 

The Pilsner:
Just a great choice by their beverage manager to have a pilsner that has that grassy, hoppy flavor 

And finally, our last course was 

The Pork and Broccoli Rabe:
The pork, prepared to unthinkable tenderness, was dressed with "Reading Raclette", which brought me immediate to thinking it was a cousin of teriyaki. The bitterness of the broccoli rabe balanced perfectly with the other sweet and savory flavors

For our digestifs, we had 

Amaro (type no longer recalled):
Who doesn't love an Amaro? It's like a warm, boozy Jolly Rancher 

Cup of Coffee:
Served in an adorable mug and saucer, this black coffee was served as only 4 or 5 ounces, which happened to be snuggle-able at the comforting hot temperature at which it was served.

Thank you to the host, our patio server, our table server, the bartender, the magnificent person at Expo, and the entire BOH.

I came here for brunch the first weekend they started serving brunch and it was unbelievable! I really want to go back for dinner now.

My favorite dishes were the house gravlax with scallion ricotta and bagel crackers (you'd think oh, smoked salmon for breakfast? nothing special, but this is special so good and a must order!), egg rolls (such an inventive way to have your bacon egg and cheese, but make sure to add their sweet and sour sauce), and the apple strudel sticky rolls (ask to get this for dessert). The potato latke is also so good, but slightly on the heavy side. 

The service was also wonderful, my server kept refilling my coffee and water and was very friendly. I love that these plates are all on the smaller side which means you can order a few and try a lot and not get overly full (and not overly expensive either!). 

The spanakopita shaksouka was slightly less successful, all it really tasted like was a giant bowl of spinach.

Delicious food. Great flavor. Excellent service. Well priced. Everything you want in a restaurant.

Chawanmushi. Order!

This place is fabulous.  It Delivers on the hype.  Reasonably priced too, which is cool for a fancy culinary experience.    
     Loved the watermelon sushi. Spare rib tagliatelle were incredible. Very accommodating with dietary restrictions and amazing food.  Backyard cocktail experience pre-dinner is not to be missed.
We loved the brunch at Olmsted. The egg roll, the duck duo and the sticky cinnamon roll; pretty awesome.

Amazing food! Yum yum yum!!

Went in for brunch without reservation. I called ahead but they are all booked up and mention they take walk-ins. We waited for a long time but we get to hangout in the backyard where there are heaters and blankets and enjoyed our cocktails before seated. 

I had the matcha cocktail. It was so different! I really like it. We ordered 2 plates and 2 mains as suggested but felt like it was really too much food. Next time I will only order 3 dishes. 

The bagel chips dish was delicious. They smoked their own fish I think. The spinach shukshuka was so good! Gooey and cheesy. The duck duo was refreshing with the cilantro. We also had the butternut squash bread which was the only thing I feel like that's kind of just average. (But still yummy!!) 

The whole meal was enjoyable. The great food, nice servers and to be able to see their chicken coop and green house right at the back yard really show this place took farm to table to another level. 

Will definitely visit again!!!!!

Super cute spot and amazing food. Portions are small, but you order a couple and it'll be fine. The oysters were crazy good. There's a little garden in the back which looks cute, but it was too cold. The service was very attentive even though it was a packed restaurant.

O.
M.
G.

The breakfast egg rolls.  YES. YES. YES.  Do not walk past this place without going inside and promptly ordering yourself the egg rolls and a delish brunch cocktail.  If you're inclined to stay for more... indulge yourself with the duck liver mouse spread.  BC that's ALSO soooo good. 

Do not be discouraged if you cannot get a table, as this place is SUPER popular.  There is a GARDEN!  You can order snacks and drinks... and guess what?  BOTH items are on the snack menu.   

I'll be back for full menu, but the first tease has me jonesing for a Round 2.

Hype meets reality, and Olmsted mostly performs. Immortalized by Pete Wells as the new champion of vegetable-forward, hyper-local Brooklyn cooking, Olmsted has a reputation for being both a hot ticket and a culinary experience. I can speak to the first point at least-- when my friend tried to book us a table of 4 a month out, when reservations opened, he checked too late in the day and had to actually set an alarm for the time reservations opened the next day.

When we arrived a month later for our 7:45 reservation on a cold March Sunday, the place was pretty busy, and we had to momentarily wait in the (cold, though cute) garden before getting to our seats. The decor is kind of average, with some live plants along the top of the wall.

We all started with a round of cocktails ($13 each). The drink list is interesting but not too eclectic; you might need to look up one of your ingredients, but on the large part it's easygoing, fresh spins on classic drinks. I thought my Rosemary, a bittersweet mezcal drink with a striking charcoal salt half-rim, was the best among them, though my companions were satisfied with the Pear and Fig. We all agreed the Hot Buttered Rum was tasty but a struggle to finish. I also got a glass of bubbles later (cremant de bourgogne from Bailly Lapierre) for $14, excellent.

We started with the oysters ($15), which I would recommend even to non-bivalve fiends. It was topped with the most delicious champagne mousse and packed so much flavor into one bite. Do note the green rocks below it are not, indeed, edible.

Next up was the steak tartare polonaise ($16). I was skeptical the broccoli and numerous sauces would work, but the layers of textures worked well together. The beef was good quality. Good toasty bread as well.

The carrot crepe ($16) was visually impressive, and definitely technically accomplished, but I had a hard time buying the hype on this one. The creaminess of it was lovely, but most of the flavors were similar. Companions raved, though.

Chawanmushi ($14) was a simply stunning rendition, though small. Get this. One of the few mind-blowing moments. This was followed by a seafood hotpot ($24), which was instantly forgettable.

Our other two high-priced dishes were a similar whiplash. The famous rutabaga pasta ($22) had a compellingly crisp texture but ended up having a weird empty taste and wasting the luxuriousness of the truffle. On the other hand, the duck ($24) was effortlessly perfect. Served both grilled and in a Thai larb salad, this was one of the best dishes of the night.

Service was very good. The bathroom has a wasp's nest and nice smelling candles.

Overall, it ended up being a pricy but not insane night, at $275 post tax and tip for a party of 4, though that was with 1-2 drinks a person. So that's $70 all-in per person, with about 2 dishes a person, which is fair on both the portion and the price to me. However, I would say half of the dishes were stellar and half were purely average. I can't say it falls into the upper echelon of places I've tried in New York, and it doesn't compel me to go back beyond enjoying the garden in the summer.

Just had sensational brunch - I highly recommend the Duck Duo, very flavorful, and the egg rolls. Ingredients are fresh (some grown in their kitchen garden, which you can sit it out the back), staff are very friendly and the decor and layout are great.
Amazing food and great service. Carrot crepe is a must! They gave us free drinks for "the wait" which we hadn't even noticed

Reservation is strongly recommended. We came here at 5pm (opening) hoping to get a table or at the very least a seat at the bar. No such luck! So we decided to have a drink and eat snacks in their garden where they grow herbs that they use in their dishes, so that's pretty cool. They also have  2-3 birds in a birdhouse. Nice and plump birds but we dont think they are meant for meals. LOL.  There are heating lamps and blankets on the benches so you wont get cold in the garden.  For cocktails we had the Matcha and Lavender - both excellent. The waiter warned us the Matcha was among sweetest drinks on the menu but we didn't think it was sweet. Snacks:  crawfish boil crackers - good but thought they could have given more knowing how inexpensive a bag of these are in Asian stores and then just sprinkle cajun/creole spices on then; golbi  cauliflower - excellent; duck mousse - excellent.  We put out names on the wait list for cancellations and we were lucky someone cancelled and we got a seat at the bar around 6pm. We started with the kale crab rangoon. Its nothing like the rangoon in your typical Chinese restaurant. Perfectly crispy on the outside and inside had this delicate tasting crab mix.  This was served in a Chinese takeout box which we thought was very whimsical.  We then had the carrot crepe. Wasn't sure what to expect but it was one of the best and most inventive things we ate there.  For mains we had the duck and rutabaga.  The duck comes in two parts and they recommend you eat them together. We agree!  The rutabaga was the best thing we had.  Incredible rich sauce but without the heaviness from eating it with your typical pasta.  Just incredible.  The service is excellent here.  We can't wait to come back!

What a delicious place ::drools::

I've heard of Olmsted but it didn't actually register in my head until my friend suggested we come here for dinner. We made reservations for a Wednesday evening at 5:30pm. Upon walking in, it was brightly lit with a mix of sunshine and lights. it's a semi-narrow restaurant with a backyard (where they also grow some of their herbs). We were seated at the bar, which is super pleasant because we get to see the bartenders in action. 

Our waiter/bartender was absolutely wonderful. My Hibiscus drink was light and refreshing in taste but also strong. One was surely enough for me. My friend ordered the Shandy, which was also refreshing in taste. Both drinks were in the red spectrum and of course my clumsy self got a few drops on my white pants. The waiter came to the rescue when we requested club soda to hopefully dab the drops out. He brought out a Tide-to-Go pen! and voilà, spots be gone! 

Now to the food. We ordered the oysters, shaved beet salad, and the duck. Oysters came in 2 on a plate of salt - very creamy and smooth. Best to eat it when its nice and warm. Beet salad was nicely paired with blue cheese and hazelnut. Gold and red beets were used. The pickling of the beets mixed really well with the flavors and left me wanting for more. As for the duck, came in two parts. The grilled portion was nice and tender, while the other portion of the duck provided it a nice crunchy texture.

It was a lovely evening and we concluded the night with the honey lavender frozen yogurt. The desert was sweet with edible lavender flowers atop. The lavender was a bit too subtle and difficult to pick-up unless you ate one of the flowers (more flowers, please!). The honey was much stronger but not entirely over-empowered the dessert. 

I'd definitely want to come back for the experience and more food!

Olmsted is where the hype lives up to your expectations. I've been twice now, for dinner and brunch. While you sometimes have to book a month out for a reservation, it's totally worth the wait. The actual restaurant is not huge, but the tables are spaced out well enough for it not to feel cramped. Brunch really knocked it out of the park. My boyfriend and I got 4 plates to share and it was more than enough food. We shared the Egg Rolls, Potato Latke, Spanakopita Shakshuka, and the Krapfen Rhubarb Donuts. The Egg Rolls were filled with housemade bacon, farm eggs and vermont cheddar--a combination inside an egg roll I never knew could taste so perfect. The Potato Latke was cooked to perfection and topped with lemon creme fraiche and smoked trout rod. Insane. So good. Honestly, everything we ate was insanely delicious. Whats so impressive is not only the inventiveness of the menu but the actual execution of it. The ONLY thing that I found to be a bit annoying was that a cup of coffee (which in my opinion tasted like diner coffee was $5 for a single cup which is a biiiiit much for the lackluster taste).

This place is great! The food, service, ambiance, everything. We went for brunch and ordered the Gravlax, latke, Carrot Kathi Roll, apple strudel rolls, and the egg rolls. I especially loved that when the waitress heard I didn't eat bacon, she offered to make 2 of the egg rolls with no bacon for me. The carrot mimosa is also a must have! I defiantly want to check out for diner. Reservations are a must!

My friends and I walked in for a Saturday morning brunch. The three of us arrived at 11am, which is 30 minutes before their opening at 11:30am. The line started forming around 11:15am and at 11:30am, they called the parties with reservations first followed by walk-ins. We waited for about 10 minutes in their perfectly curated garden area before getting seated. Not a bad wait at all considering the hype this place is receiving. 

The three of us shared the Butternut Squash Bread, Egg Rolls, Potato Latke, and the Duck Duo. It seemed as if the waitstaff overly encouraged us to order more food (they recommend 5-7 dishes for 2 people sharing, though we made due with 4 overall and we were all satisfied). The kitchen staff was very accommodating towards food restrictions and allergies and half an order of Egg Rolls were made without bacon and the Duck Duo was made without dairy. Everything was very tasty and the staff was generous with the coffee refills. I will say that the Duck Duo was on the salty side and I was not a fan of the heaps of sugar on the pita bread. Also, the bacon in the egg rolls seemed a bit paltry. It also felt like we waited a while to receive our food.

That said, it was a pleasant experience overall and I would come back to try their dinner menu. Olmstead clearly put a lot of thought into making guests feel comfortable in their space and making their menu unique yet comforting. I enjoyed the vibe of the restaurant and the decor and dinnerware was beautiful. 4/5 would recommend.

I was visiting NYC for the weekend and looking for someplace new to try, I happened upon Olmsted, after seeing it listed by a number of publications as a "must try" place. It was far from it. It wasn't all bad, but it  just wasn't that impressive, and the hype is confounding. First, the good: great cocktails (a little pricey, but nothing outrageous by NYC-Brooklyn standards). I tried three different cocktails - two off the the menu and one which was the bartender's creation - and they were all outstanding. A rare meal where I thought the drinks were the best part. The space is also quite lovely. It does feel like a classic "date night" spot. Second, the mediocre: the food - really underwhelming with the exception of the crawfish boil crackers. Aside from the crackers, I had the gobi pakora cauliflower, carrot crepe, and grilled scallops. The cauliflower tasted like the last remnants of something you might scrap up from an Indian lunch buffet that was about to close. The carrot crepe was tasteless, and the grilled scallops meh. Even though I hadn't really enjoyed the meal, I hoped that dessert - a lavender honey frozen yogurt would soothe some of my disappointment. It didn't. It wasn't really bad. But it wasn't really good either. This is a relatively expensive place to eat, and it is difficult to justify the cost of this meal. I am sure the ingredients were all of the highest quality (and the care taken in preparing the various plates was obvious), but this just isn't very memorable. I was staying in the Financial District and went out of my way to eat here. Not worth the effort - cannot recommend.
Worst experience ever. I called them, sent email and text messages. Nobody responded. They let me out with my family after we got a couple of minutes late. Horrible experience.

This was our 2nd time dining here but first time for brunch. We sat at the bar and started the meal with some much needed carrot mimosas. The thought of putting carrot juice in a mimosa never occurred to me but instantly, it sounded delicious and happily it was in fact, actually delicious. First course was the House Gravlax, uber-thin slices of salmon served with Scallion Ricotta and Everything Bagel Crackers. They were wonderfully light and refreshing, and a great way to start the meal. Next up was the House-made Egg rolls served in a cute Olmsted fast food container. The egg rolls are far from fast food and you know that right when you crunch into all their bacon, egg, and cheese egg goodness.  We followed that with the Rooftop Romaine which segued into the Grilled Breakfast Burger. This is what we walked into the restaurant knowing we wanted to try and it didn't disappoint. The Apple Strudel Sticky Rolls were exactly as good as those 4 perfect words sound when put together. The highlight of our brunch though, was our server, who made the best Irish coffee I've ever had in New York. What he later told us was that he lived in San Francisco and had spent some time at Buena Vista Cafe, which made the drink famous in the states in the 1950s. Long story short: we asked the right guy for an Irish Coffee. 

Overall, another great experience! Can't wait to visit again.

My wife and I had an 8 PM reservation to eat here last Tuesday, May 15 to celebrate her birthday. We received a call 1 hour before our reservation, after we had made the trip over to Prospect Heights in an intense thunderstorm, informing us there had been an accident and the restaurant was closed for the night.  No further information was provided and no accommodation was offered beyond a vague offer to come back another time, without any meaningful way to follow up on it beyond trying our luck on Resy again. We then spent the evening trying to find a table at another restaurant in the rain instead of celebrating what should have been a fun night.

What a great little spot in Brooklyn! Inventive and fresh dishes with a serious farm to table feel. Some of my favorite dishes were the beef tartare and the long island duck two ways, especially loved the beautiful outdoor garden in the backyard where we had dessert + finished our bottle of wine. Cant wait till the outdoor deck opens! Will be back.

Love this place and everything about it.  The vibe is great.  Outside space is super inviting.  Drinks were phenomal and creative.  Food is well thought, tasty and affordable.  This is the restaurant you want in your neighborrhood cant wait to go back.

Farm to Table restaurant. Quite a unique taste. That watermelon sushi was actually refreshing but different. I would say the overall experience was great. It Ii be a bit pricey but it is expected from a farm to table restaurant. Great for a date and definitely need to book early. Parking is not so bad in that area.

Expect twists and turns, like a breakfast of Carrot Kathi Rolls (Carrot Pulp Falafel, Cilantro Stem Raita) or the Duck Duo, crispy duck sausage with scrambled egg and maple flatbread. And don't leave without trying their bacon, egg, and cheese Egg Rolls, as delicious as they are adorable.

The tight and thoughtful dinner menu includes a scrumptious Duck Liver Mousse, a Beef Tartare with hard-boiled egg, Heritage Pork with Raclette, and other seasonal curve-balls. Toss in a playful cocktail menu and you've found the perfect spot for those who like a dash of quirkiness on the plate.

Sooo much hype surrounding this place. I made a Saturday brunch reservation several weeks out, and was able to secure a 2PM seating (the only one available for a month at the time I booked). 

Interior is super cute - love the tableware - with a photogenic patio out back as well.

We ordered the egg rolls, duck two ways, and burger. Egg rolls are just as cute and creatively presented as everyone says, and the burger is solid (my boyfriend loved it), but my favorite by far was the duck. Somehow the scrambled duck eggs, sausage, and maple flatbread combined to make something far greater than the sum of their parts. Savory, sweet, with a slight kick from the slaw and chili peppers that accompanied the dish. Party in my mouth, for sure. 

Not sure if it was worth the trek out to Brooklyn, but I wouldn't say no to coming here again.

I've been wanting to go to Olmstead for a while. Finally made a reservation way ahead and was excited to go. So much fun. Delicious creative dishes. Loved the kale crab Rangoon. The lobster Thermidor. Carrots with clams. Didn't like the tartare. But we had three orders of the chocolate mousse!

I love this place. The backyard is heavenly. The S'mores are delicious. And the wine sommelier there, Swann, is an absolute treasure. Levi is also a good waiter. Haven't done dinner but the nibbles and cocktails here keep me returning. It is expensive but the ambiance makes for an impressive date.

After my boyfriend tried making a reservation to Olmsted for 2 weeks straight (maybe 3 weeks), he finally got us a brunch reservation! I didn't care if it was brunch or dinner, all I knew was that it was going to be good for sure. I checked the menu again before we went and my expectations were a bit low because the menu seemed so small. 

Now that I've gone -- although their menu is short, they finesse everything. We enjoyed everything that we ordered and couldn't be more satisfied. The restaurant itself isn't that large but they have bar seating as well (i'm not sure if this is FCFS). There's is ample lighting, enough for you to share that insta picture and have everyone DMing you about the restaurant! I promise. They have an extremely cute garden space in the back where you can go there after your meal to finish your drink. They also have a shortlist for food as well (more finger foods). 

Like always, we order too much food but never regret it. We started with the gravlax and when it arrived, it looked to good to be eaten, especially since the lox was colored so beautifully. It's served with ricotta cream cheese and everything bagel chips. This was good but extremely salty but the ricotta and pickled veggies help cut through the flavor a bit. I probably wouldn't order this again when I come back. The egg roll on the other hand was the cutest dish I've seen at a restaurant. It's served in it's own custom Olmsted packaging and served with local green ketchup and sweet and sour sauce! I couldn't get over how the packaging was throughout my entire meal. Also, I was so distracted that I didn't realize the egg roll was literally an egg roll, filled with eggs bacon and cheese. Loved it!! The potato latke arrived on a skillet and was extremely crispy on the outside and a tad soft inside. My favorite part of this dish was the lemon creme fraiche because it was so refreshing but definitely needed some hot sauce/ketchup... Lastly, the duck duo completed my weekend serving of eggs. There was definitely a slight game-y taste to the dish, balanced perfectly with the extra cilantro on top. It could've used a little less cilantro, but we ended up mixing up the whole bowl and scooping it into the sweet pita. THIS PITA WAS LIFE CHANGING. I almost wanted to go ask the chef for the pita recipe... It was so soft and fluffy, almost like I was eating a pillow... The mix of sweet and salty in one bite... this sealed the meal and gave us the perfect ending to brunch!

I haven't had such a memorable brunch in a while. Usually you find the same thing across every brunch menu, but Olmsted changed the brunch game. I loved and am already trying to get another reservation ASAP. Can't wait to try the dinner menu!

My fiancé was thrilled about trying out Olmsted. We were seated on time for our reservation and greeted promptly by our server and attending staff. Upon looking at the menu I was confused on what to order. The menu is split into several courses based on size. To be quite honest, they're all small and underwhelming in flavor. Our server suggested the amount of plates for 2 people and frankly I was baffled as the plates were on average $21. We're in Prospect Heights not Midtown. Know your audience. Sadly I didn't care for much on the menu. I had 2 won tons, half a falafel and some tempura kale. This of course shared with my very hungry fiancé. We settled our check and headed to Daly Pie to redeem the evening.

If you get a reservation at Olmsted, verify that they check off your reservation when you arrive. Three hours after my visit they emailed and said they had charged me $50 no show fee. Outrageous as we were there right on time and even asked if they needed my name for the reservation, but they didn't care. Had to call 4 times before someone picked up and, in a suspicious voice, finally helped me correct the problem.

The food and service was pretty good, what you would expect for the price.

Well, Michelin has lowered its standards to the point that I don't care. 
I cannot believe a one star has such indifferent, incompetent and confused service. As a server who supported myself through school I have no words for how sloppy this place is. The bartenders seem to ignore drink orders, and it took forever to have our orders taken for food. The menu is confusing and is structured to upsell you at every point. If I go to one more restaurant that "suggests/recommends/urges" you to order nearly every damn dish to feed four I'm going to strike. The portions are miserly and overpriced, and they are not worthy of a one star in taste or structure. 
So what that there is a bird or two in the backyard?  
Seriously, Brooklyn is awash with lovely finds; Olmsted is not one.
Great food for brunch--shareable dishes and a cute garden put back where you can wait for your table. Loved the vibe and the breakfast burger is amazing!

So this was a particularly special night - my girlfriend and I got engaged earlier in the day and this was part of a surprise evening for her. So yeah, take all my gushing review with a grain of salt, but I truly had a wonderful experience. First and foremost the restaurant helped me out with getting a booking even when Saturday RESY was showing nothing 2 weeks out. 

We ran through a fair portion of the menu, each dish was more delicious than the last. Started the evening with the Lobster Thermidor, and then walked our way around some exquisite Kale Crab Rangoon followed by a filling Beef Tartar. The main event consisted of Roast and Grilled Duck as well as English Pea Falafel. The duck was favorite - the sour cherry really offset the richness of the duck, it was absolutely incredible. Our server Felice was attentive and brought such a warm and joyful smile to our experience, she's a real treat if you have the chance to meet her. Start to finish I couldn't be more happy with our time there!

So had a chance to come back to Olmsted recently. The experience warrants updated review.... This one would make Gordon Ramsay proud.

While reservations for table dining are hard to schedule on short notice, bar reservations are often available - so we went that route. We were given a choice to sit at the main bar or at open kitchen bar. Elected open kitchen bar - what an amazing experience. Highly recommend as it will make it into a dinner and a show.

Sitting at the kitchen bar we had full visibility into all dishes being prepared and plated. Was very interesting and impressed by the work that chefs put in. All three chefs were working in unison with great efficiency, yet focusing on perfection from each dish. Expediter (sous chef I guess) was great at finishing plates and providing support as she had solid control of the kitchen. Everytime a dish was plated - workplace was wiped down - cleanliness was observed. Everytime a dish was prepped - chefs tasted it to make sure there was consistency - of 20 garlic risottos I saw served - I think all 20 were tasted, which makes sense as salt, cheese, pepper, butter - were all added and cooked for each individual plate. Bottom line - kitchen ran as a well oiled machine. Chef Baxtrom popped in a few times - doing quality checks and offering guidance to line chefs. Pretty cool to observe - literally 2 feet away from where magic happens

Menu changes regularly so we lucked out with some of earliest days of July menu. Of dishes we tasted:
- Duck with spring onions - spot on - very filling and juicy, prepared mid-rare, with duck sausages and cherries on the side - 5/5
- Rabe tempura w shishito butter - quite a filling appetizer, light tempura batter, nice heat on butter - 5/5
-  Snap Pea Sushi - great fresh appetizer to start - snap peas as base instead of rice, thin fluke sashimi on top, preserved lemon w salt, in a light acidic sauce - very flavorful and tasty - 5/5
- Scallops - grilled on skewers, seasoned wonderfully with creamy corn and mushrooms - I found this to be executed perfectly - 5/5
- Lobster Thermidor - perhaps the only dish we did not carer for. It was more like crispy crackers with lobster foam for dipping. No actual lobster in the dish (besides foam) and it did not work in my view. Perhaps as an amuse bouche it could work, but not as $12 appetizer - 1/5

Sitting in front of the open kitchen, we also observed other dishes being prepared. The pork loin with leeks looked absolutely amazing. As did risotto and the carrot crepes (which we had before and are delicious).

So next time you want fine dining, perhaps consider booking a bar reservation at Olmsted and asking for kitchen bar sitting.

One of the best dining experiences I've ever had. Our son-in-law made dinner reservations weeks in advance. We got there early for a drink on the back patio, which was crowded, but we sipped amazing cocktails as we walked around the vegetable garden. The table before us took a very long time to leave, so the staff went above and beyond to keep us happy with food and treats. The food was heavenly and the service was first class, warm and friendly. I can't speak highly enough about our host, our som and our waiter (Emmanuel). I can't wait to go back.
The food at Olmsted is delicious and presented wonderfully. It is a tapas type restaurant so a party of two would need to order at least four dishes which can get pricey.

4.5 stars. Food 5 stars. Ambience 4 stars. 

The farm-to-table food is inventive here- fantastic values. We arrived at 1pm on Saturday for walk in for 2 and got seated in 30 minutes. In the meantime, we hang out at the garden in the shade having chilled drinks and had an order of kafpen. The restaurant was a bit loud. We were seated at the bar next to the grill - can get hot during the summer. It was good to sit next each other when the restaurant is loud but the counter was a bit too high for the stools. 

MUST GET:
Krafpen (Austrian donut with rhubarb jelly) - the donut falls between a donut and a brioche. A lot softer than a donut and a lot more structure than a brioche. Not too sweet. And rhubarb jelly was tart, sweet, and sour - fabulous juxtaposition to the Austrian donut. Delightful little bites. Good start to the brunch!

Carrot Kathi roll with carrot pulp falafel and cilantro stem raita - phenomenal. Soft carrot crepe with a bit of spice, yogurt, and earthy falafel inside. Brilliant and definitely worth trying. We shared it between two of us. 

SOLID:
Egg rolls - this is like a soft quiche (with egg, bacon and cheddar) wrapped in a crispy egg roll cigar. Interesting combination of flavors and texture. A bit too heavy for 2 people. Best to share among 4 people. 

SKIP:
Shaksouka- middle eastern dish. This version had less tomato. I prefer this served in a cast iron skillet like for baked eggs to keep the dish warm, with more tomato to bring out the acidity in this dish. Olmsted's version is a bit creamier (with copious ricotta) and heavier. I like the crispy ricotta salata addition on top.

This place was so so good. We got the Cobb salad, pork belly, cacio e pepe, scallops & duck breast. The duck breast, cacio e pepe, and pork belly were my favorites though everything was phenomenal. Would definitely recommend making a reservation as this place was small and incredibly busy. We saw many people turned away at the door since the restaurant was out of tables.

Could not say enough nice things about this restaurant. Although the portions are very small for the price, the food is AMAZING and worth the price if you're willing to spend. They even offered my boyfriend and I a complimentary dish of pasta which actually turned out to be the best dish of the night. We will definitely be  coming back next time we have the money to spend haha

Most of my favorite foodie restaurants with relaxed service are in BRKLYN and this is my new fave. 

The menu has three sections and the tip is to pick 2 in each section for 2 people.   We had 5 total plus dessert and that was the right amount. 

My favorite dish was the garden spaetzle cacio e pepe to which we added summer truffle on top.  

Other standouts included the heirloom tomato schnitzel which is a giant tomato cut in half and baked with breading : batter on top and the pork dish.    

For wine, I selected a Vacqueyras from Rhône Valley with a barnyardy smell.    I loved it and the wine Director was knowledgeable and friendly.  

Overall this restaurant is outstanding and I'll be back!

I'll start with the most important part: the food is excellent. The menu is small but very thoughtfully curated, so every dish is well conceived and nicely presented. The snap pea sushi, crab rangoon, duck breast, pork espangnole, oysters mignonette, and especially the carrot crepe made a really well balanced meal for two, topped off with raspberries and cream for desert. Everything was fresh and delicious. The wine list is solid as well. We will definitely return on the basis of the food alone. However, the portions are small, and the prices are high, so be warned. 

My real criticism, however, is regarding the atmosphere. They overbook, so it's really crowded, and for some reason, they play music at a deafening volume, so everybody is shouting to make themselves heard. This is not a relaxing environment, and I want a relaxing environment when I'm paying this kind of money for a meal. Next time, we're going to try a non-weekend time, maybe that will make a difference. Honestly though, does anybody go to a fancy restaurant for the music?

So disappointed. I heard about that place for so long, it was a real satisfaction to finally get 2 seats at the bar on a random walk-in while hanging out in the neighborhood. The bar staff is amazing, cool and funny and they know their menu. Going to the menu, it first appears definitely original, the name and ingredients .. but soon enough, it was a disappointment. I don't even remember one impressive dish, may be a potato thing that you could find in any brunch places. There was this duck egg with sausage, what was so original there ? .. or some fried veggies that should only belong to a 2stars deli .. Overall it was still a good experience, prices are not too crazy, location is chill, restaurant design it cool (my favorite are the restroom), but don't go there for the food, it definitely has no-thing special at all.

This was exactly what I want in a nice meal. Every dish we had was surprising and unique in its flavor combinations, and very delicious. From the watermelon sushi to the carrot crepe to the spaetzle with pea and truffle, every dish seemed to have a fun twist to it. Most of the dishes are small, so I suggest getting about two per person and sharing everything so that you all get a few bites of each. 

The service was exceptional, and the ambience very pleasant. It won't be a cheap meal; but I think the food and wine prices are both very reasonable for such a high quality meal. 5 stars.

Great meal at Olmstead. They have a great attention to the details. The staff is always passing by the table to refill water or take things away. Plating is beautiful. Decor is cute, and their backyard seems very calming. You can sit in the backyard for drinks and a limited menu I overheard. 

The duck liver mousse was delicious. Carrot crepe was interesting- the clams were cooked perfectly. Kale crab rangoon was all right. Crispy and had a good amount of crab inside. The roasted duck was delicious and the grilled duck sausage was okay. Scallop was delicious and so was the corn salsa that was paired with it. Their chocolate mousse is a must!! It might be the favorite part of the meal.

This place is bomb. I ate brunch here. And everything was on point. Flavoring was Amazing and balanced. Palamo was Defiently one of the best drinks I've ever gotten, so refreshing! Get the egg rolls without bacon. Sooo soo good!

We luckily came to Olmstead on a Monday when they do walk ins rather than reservations and had the most whimsical experience. 
Every detail is carefully assembled, from the napkin rings and menus that you're presented with to the creative, thoughtful presentation of the food and cocktails. The stars of our experience were the Shandy cocktail (DANGEROUSLY crushable) and the Caccio e Pepe (my new cheat meal). Jake, our bartender, was welcoming and offered excellent guidance for our meal. 
Oh also, the backyard is a magical fairytale wonderland where much rose will be consumed. See you on Friday for brunch!
Simple. Elegant. Unpretentious.

It's funny to think that for all my efforts looking for the greatest food in New York City, all this time I was living barely three blocks away from one of the best restaurants in Brooklyn. With nothing but a tiny sign advertising itself, I'd probably walked by the Olmstead several times without noticing it. But now I'll never be able to pass it by without staring longingly through the window. The occasion for finally trying it was my aunt and uncle visiting me for an afternoon during a flight layover. My aunt can't eat gluten, so we looked around for gluten-free options in my neighborhood and the Olmstead came up at the top of the list. Following the advice of our waitress, we picked a number of dishes and shared them family-style. First was a delicious rooftop romaine salad with crisp watermelon radishes that perfectly complimented the dish's light yet robust flavor profile. Next came a carrot kathi roll. The falafel was sharp and tangy and went nicely with the cilantro stem sauce--I normally can't eat cilantro, but the sauce was mild enough that I could get in a decent tasting. For main courses, we got their "duck duo"--a dish made of scrambled duck eggs and sausage served with gluten-free toast prepared with a prosciutto rub--and a green shaksouka crammed with sun-ripened tomatoes and parmesan. The former was, in my opinion, the highlight of the meal: the prosciutto rub was a strong yet pleasant counterpoint to the lightness of the eggs and the gaminess of the sausage. But the shaksouka was great, too. I joked to my aunt that it was the best pasta dish I'd ever tasted that didn't actually have pasta. We ended it with a giant, sturdy potato latke with sweet and tart lemon creme fraiche and smoked trout roe--this wasn't gluten-free so I shared it with my uncle. My biggest issue is the portion/price ratio. Even after dropping nearly a hundred bucks, the three of us were still hungry enough to get ice cream afterwards. But the Olmstead is definitely an essential tasting experience for the budding Brooklyn foodie.

Fantastic service, atmosphere and food. I love restaurants geared towards sharing food. Perfect for a date night. Cocktails are really great. The Lavender was perfect if you're a whisky fan. The servers really know the menu and can help you create the perfect meal. 

Duck liver moose was to die for. Best thing I've eaten in a while. The scallops and duck were also fantastic. We left feeling perfectly satisfied.

As a side note, the back patio doesn't take reservations and you can get drinks and their snacks (appetizers). Plus, the patio is so cute. It's where they grow some of their food and it feels like you're not in Brooklyn anymore.

Tonight's menu was by far the best iteration I've had here. 
Eggplant tempura came with an addicting shiso sauce. 
Duck liver mousse- always so tasty. 
Garden spatzle - so light, so delicious.
Grilled pork belly- SO tender. wtf. Came with a vinaigrette that was more of just a savory delicious sauce.
Dry rubbed scallops- also unbelievably silky and tender.
Tomato schnitzel - I have no idea what this was made of but it came with a bunch of incredible sauces and was so, so tasty.

Also, Emanuel at the bar was the nicest human ever.

Feeling disappointed...trying to make a reservation for two at Olmsted was very difficult.  After trying to make one on their website and being asked to contact them, I tried to call...the recording said to email for a faster response. It also stated that walk-in's were welcome as seats are saved at the bar for this purpose.  After a 30 minute drive from the city we were turned away at 9:30pm.  There appeared to be seats available but were told that getting in was "highly unlikely."  A better system for reservations or walk-ins is a must.  Waste of time and travel money!

Lived up to the hype for us. Restaurant has a nice ambiance and attentive staff. Food does not come out quickly so this is a good place to sit back, relax, and have a few of their top-notch cocktails. Good beverage menu for non-drinkers as well.

Carrot crepe has a warm buttery citrusy sauce which goes perfectly with the clams, it's a must-order. The crepe itself is delicious as well. I would eat this dish again and again.

Pork belly was another standout. It's thick and perfectly cooked, really meaty for pork belly. They pour a delicious sauce over it.

Olmsted has a number of breaded items and they do an amazing job frying/breading everything. The heirloom tomato schnitzel and eggplant tempura were both packed with flavor. Dipping sauces are all on point and independently great.

For dessert, the chocolate mousse is another must order, some of the best i've ever had. We also got the lavender honey frozen yogurt, which was the one let down of the meal. Beautiful presentation though. 

Will eat here again and again
The staff isn't very pleasant. My service was so bad I wouldn't even eat there but the ambiance is cute.

Best meal in Brooklyn during our week long trip to NY. Loved the watermelon sushi, kale crab rangoon, carrot crepe, scallops and more. Need to try the oysters and more main dishes next time. And even the kids menu pasta was excellent. Great service, too. Charming garden outside. Cant wait to be back.

Wow! I was not sure whether Olmstead would live up to the hype, but it sure did in my book. We went with friends visiting from PA and took the 5:30 reservation (it was that or 10:00). They have a lovely cocktail menu and managed to try 6 different drinks, all of which were quite good. The menu is broken up into starters, small plates, and slightly larger plates. Our server recommended 3 dishes per person and the whole menu was 14 dishes I think, so we agreed on 5 things we didn't want and ordered the rest of the menu and shared. We really liked everything although some dishes really stood out - the pork belly was so good we got seconds! For dessert, they usher you put to the garden to clear up table space; fortunately it was a nice evening. The chocolate mousse was to die for, the guys had the s'mores and enjoyed cooking marshmallows. I'll be back.

Great experience! Whimsical interpretations of dishes that you already know. Staff was attentive but not at all intrusive. Overall, the place had a friendly, laid  back vibe. Food was delish! Highly recommend.

Very friendly staff. Very nice ambiance.  Wonderful presentation of the dishes.Very unique flavors. We were able to get a table on a Tuesday night without  reservation.   They recommend sharing 3-4 dishes at once between 2 people. Our dishes came one by one, and the service was very slow. Since the wait between all dishes, we did not feel like we had enough for a light  dinner, and serving size appeared smaller and smaller with each dish. Leaving a restaurant a bit hundred is always a bit disappointing.  Also, although the restaurant is beautifully designed, and their dishes and cups are made of thing elegant porcelain that adds to the experience and atmosphere, the place is extremely loud. It is hard to have a conversation over diner.

Have been wanting to eat dinner here for a year now had to settle for Saturday brunch and was not disappointed. First of all I have to say the staff was exceptional. Chris working the back deck was super friendly. We were walking with an hour wait so we were able to get a spot in the garden area really chill 90's hip hop and a little bit of pop loud enough for you to hear without being obnoxious. Had a few drinks out back and two appetizers while we waited. Had a tequila drink of the patio menu, was so tasty ended up having two. The patio has a smaller menu which just made us ask why haven't we come here sooner. We split an order of the egg rolls (4 per order) and the summer squash bread. The squash bread came with harbison clotted cream and fresh jam. The clotted cream and jam stole the bread show and made it worth the $12 price. The egg rolls were delicious. Crispy and not over oily. Perfect egg with small cubes of bacon. So good could have had another order if we didn't get seated. We were called inside just about an hour later which was perfect because I was about to order more egg rolls. The inside is very nice. Beautiful bar and garden on the wall. 
We ordered the potato latke with the smoked trout roe, the carrot kathi roll and a breakfast burger. The potato was delicious crispy outside perfect inside no oily after taste here. The burger was very good cooked perfectly medium.  My favorite dish was actually the carrot kathi roll. It was so tasty. My only complaint was we were sharing and it was served in a deli style basket which made it hard to cut and share so we had to put it on a plate. The flavors and different textures in the roll were awesome. 
I can't wait to get back and try the crab regions and lavender yogurt. 
Great job everyone on the Olmsted team.

This is a nice restaurant, but nothing is that good or that interesting. I certainly don't feel a need to go back.

Everything was fine. The fried squash rings were tasty, but dry, without sauce, without much of a depth of flavor. The crab rangoon was a slightly classed up version of the dish -- real crab instead of sarimi -- but again, that's fine. If you're sensing a trend, then you basically get the thrust of my experience of Olmsted.

The most fun dish was certainly the s'mors with housemade marshmallows that diners toast themselves in the restaurant's backyard. But they're just s'mors, and they're served with a wrapped bar of Hershey's milk chocolate.

For the price and for the fuss it takes to get a reservation, one can certainly do better.
The food was very good and the service was excellent. The big downside was that the portions were a bit small for the price. Will probably return for a few light bites and cocktails.

Came here for dinner one time and it was GREAT!  The beet cocktail is to die for.  Came here for brunch, too.  They do not take reservations, but we popped in and got a 2:45pm slot. After a long long wait we finally were seated and the level of service was outstanding.  They took great care of us after waiting for a long time outside on the patio.  Even though the place doesn't allow for seating past 3:00pm they took us at 3:10pm and served us a full meal for brunch.  

Their food innovative, different, creative, and delicious.  AND located in an awesome area of Brooklyn, too. I highly suggest coming here...and if you can't get in...be warned that you are not guaranteed a table if you come back when you get the text that your table is ready (if the people before you take forever to leave).

All in all, great and thank you for management for dealing with our Brett-Kavanaugh-esque entitlement. #Yale #Legacy #ServeMeFoodASAP

Another difficult reservation to get but, I ended up scoring one on a Thursday night. Olmsted is super popular and I understand why. The food is inventive, and extremely tasty. The atmosphere is beautiful and that includes the spacious garden in the back. 

We arrived a bit early and enjoyed some time in the back garden. When our table was ready we were seated in the front and the wait staff was extremely helpful and very pleasant. 

The menu is super different and has so many interesting things to chose from.

For apps, we decided on crab and kale Rangoon with a spicy sweet and sour sauce.  They were bites of heaven. We ordered a second portion!  The price tag is expensive for 4. They are extremely tasty though! 

Our next app was broccoli rabe spatzle Mac n cheese. The crunchy rabe and creamy cheese with a bread crumb topping. A def must try. 

For an entree I had the scallops with corn, chanterelles and blueberries. It was an interesting mix of flavors. The scallops were delicious and cooked perfectly. 

Also we had the duck. Again, another amazing dish it was cooked perfectly with a beautiful sauce and fruit to accompany it.

For dessert we had to try the frozen yogurt!  Light and fresh. It was a beautiful ending to the meal. We also tried the chocolate mousse. We weren't really impressed. That was the only down fall to this meal. 

For drinks we ordered a bourbon cocktail and beer. They were both delicious. 

In closing Olmsted def stood up to what I thought it would be, AMAZING! If you can get a reservation go and enjoy! 

Street Parking wasn't difficult (326)

Mondays they don't take reservations! We arrived 10 minutes after they opened for dinner and were sent to the garden to wait to be seated.  The garden was a lovely place to start my wine flight.  The wait was only 10 minutes.  We ordered the lobster thermidor which essentially tasted like a lobster rind.  It came with an airy cheesy lobster sauce that was delicious.  The pork belly was fast but way too much fat and not enough meat.  The duck was the highlight.  Both the duck breast and the confit were great.  Finally, for dessert you go back to the garden to end the evening.  I didn't love being on top of my neighbor in the garden but the plentiful homemade marshmallows made it worth it.  Only complaint... After the s'mores I was super sticky and there is only one bathroom for the whole restaurant so I had sticky hands for a while.

I went for the Crab Rangoon with kale, but ended up staying for the tea selection and the (holy sh*t!) Krafpen with my tea.

LOVE the garden out back!

I am wild about the thoroughness here -- the sheer, well, choreography (if you will) of how dishes are both selected and prepared at Olmsted.

And the ambience itself? Inimitable.

The restaurateur here knows one thing for certain, and never forgets it: GOD IS IN THE DETAILS.

Went with my parents and boyfriend. My parents and I arrived early and they were able to seat us (it was 5:30, reservation at 5:45). My boyfriend was coming from work so he was running a few minutes late. At 5:49 the hostess told us we had to order in the next 5 minutes because of the next reservation. We had literally just had a few sips of our cocktails. Luckily bf came within a few minutes but the pressure was ON! When our waitress explained the way the menu worked (sharing) we ordered about 4 or 5 dishes to share and she said it wasn't enough. We then ordered several more. Wayyyy too much food. And we are big eaters

The fried squash and liver mousse were good. Duck was amazing. We didn't like the carrot crepe nor the scallops. 

Great atmosphere and music. I actually would recommend but just make sure not to get bullied!!!

Honestly, I was underwhelmed and disappointed. I was so excited to take my mother here when she visited me in Brooklyn because I'd heard such great things about the restaurant.
