I had to make the reservation a month in advance at like 9:30 am and even at that time there were only several time slots left, possibly because there were going to be 3 of us and that's an odd number.  When we got there, the decor was simple and the food really was delicious. I especially enjoyed the crepe, which is one of their most-known dishes. That being said, the experience was not good.  First of all, we didn't have one set waiter, which definitely led to inconsistencies. The first person who spoke to us recommended 3 dishes per person. The second person who spoke to us suggested 6-8 dishes total (for a group of 3). We ended up getting 7 dishes. It was NOT enough, even after we all ordered desert. Also, we got the first 5 dishes in the first 1.5 hours of our meal, in slow succession. After that, we waited for over 45 minutes with no food and no one coming to get another drink order even when I tried to flag someone down. At one point I did order a drink from someone and they disappeared and I had to wait another good length of time to flag someone else down for another drink. Then our last two dishes came and we ate desert in the backyard. It was pretty, and there were wool blankets outside which was cute. I really wish this had been a good experience, but I will not be going back again. We literally left the restaurant and ordered a pizza because my mom and boyfriend were still hungry. We definitely should have gotten at LEAST 3 dishes each!

Everything is on point at this place. We got purifies to start and duck confit and scallops for the main course. Everything was so delicious, I couldn't help it I had to order their frozen yogurt with Lavender and honey. That's it. I'll never be skinny if Olmsted is just 15 min walking from my house. Thank you!

I usually love farm-to-table places because the dishes are fresh. Here thats no different. The dishes were unique and fresh, but I have to say that I didn't enjoy some as much as I enjoyed others. We had the Dave's trout, which I didn't enjoy as much as I thought I was going to. 

My favorite dish here (and possibly all time in NYC) was the carrot crepe. What an unexpected, savory dish. It has got to be one of the most unique dishes I've tried in NYC and if I could I would come here every day to have this dish. I can't exaggerate enough how delicious this dish is.

Mixed feelings about this place. Great value for money but the service was a little slow and scattered in our experience. The food was stellar and the space had a very cute ambience. Will definitely come back to this place in the summer again since they have an outdoor garden we haven't experienced. The most disappointing part of the evening was having to miss dessert due to the excessively slow service as we were running late and the chef could not have it packed for us to go. Will need to revisit this one!

What a gem! 

Olmsted is hands down one of my favorite restaurants. It's the prefect date spot, the food is delicious, and it's a place you'll find yourself recommending to many friends because it's that good.

The Long Island duck grilled and larbed was tie for my favorite dish. I was also a huge fan of the carrot crepe. Don't be fooled, this carrot crepe surprised me at first bite! the little neck clams were fresh and the dish put all together has so many flavors, it's just simply amazing. I loved that all the dishes were unique and in my opinion memorable.

I absolutely loved the cocktails! Don't know what to say aside from, order one! 

I know the menu changes, so I know I'll be back and I'll be excited to try what's new.

Tips:
-MAKE A RESERVATION!! If not, get there right when they open and hope for a bar seat.
-for two is recommended ordering 4 dishes to try and share! You won't re

Amazing food. Love the inventive dishes with local and seasonal produce. I love what they are doing here and think it's a great model for conscious cooking and eating! Service was attentive and lovely. The ambiance is amazing. We had the oysters, MNC spatzle, sweet potato pierogis, carrot crepes, lobster Thermidor, plum cake, housemade ginger beer, and the Lavender cocktail. Everything was wonderful! Our server let us know a couple times that our order was on the light side. I appreciate the heads up but I didn't need to be reminded. We were full at the end! It sort of felt like we were being encouraged to order more, but it wasn't too aggressive. Overall it was a great experience!
Service was great, food was meh. So disappointed after waiting weeks to come here after all the hype. Honestly would go elsewhere for the hassle.

Took my lady there for date night food lived up to it's reputation, it was delicious!
The service was perfect, and we got lucky and were seated in front of the kitchen, and chatted with the cooks, they were super sweet! We had an awesome time!!!
My favorite restaurant in Brooklyn, perhaps in the entire NY. The food was so delicious and the staff were so friendly. The best food I've had in years I think. Keep up the amazing work! :)

It's pricey. But it's incredible. Small plates...creative infusions...the Lavender, Pine and Rosemary concoctions off the cocktail menu are inspirational. In the warmer months, the patio is pretty spectacular.

Without gushing... one of the finest meals I've purchased in a long time. Everything was well prepared and painstakingly presented such that it was a feast for the eye as well. The egg rolls and smoked salmon dishes, while seemingly simple, were outstanding in such a way that were both familiar and creative. 

It's a perfect place to take a couple of friends and share everything. If you're in Brooklyn and you're a foodie, this Michelin star restaurant isn't to be missed.

I'm being generous by giving this place a 5. Reservation is extremely hard to get and we literally checked for dates non-stop so I don't have to sit at the bar. I wouldn't mind the kitchen bar seat though to be honest and I think service would have been better.

The good - the idea, the serveware, the carrot crepe, the battered squash rings, and the duck breast. The idea of farm to table with a changing menu based on seasonally available products is great and makes the food tastier. The servewares were from a designer based in Brooklyn and they were the cutest ceramics I've seen. If she sells individual pieces, I'll be all over that. I don't like carrots and I don't like clams, but their carrot crepe was gorgeous visually and tasted amazing. The battered squash rings were my favorite dish. It's served in an interesting way and omg so tasty! It's one of those dishes you are not sure what you are eating, but it's good. Both dishes are so unique that, no one has it but them. Duck breast is awesome as well. I got pissed at Eleven Madison Park for wasting a whole damn duck just for a few pieces of duck breast meat. Resources are scarce and just because you are rich enough to pay $300+ for a meal doesn't make it okay for you to waste food like that. Olmsted definitely did not throw away the duck and this tasted just as good in my opinion. A bit less is okay if that means I don't have to feel guilty about wasting food.

The okay -hot pot and Dan dan spaetzle. We like Dan dan noodles and spaetzle, but their creative version kind of didn't work. Didn't taste bad, but I much rather they just gave me dan dan noodles straight up and my husband rather have spaetzle the tradition way. Fried spaetzle in chili oil is way too greasy and I eat greasy Chinatown Chinese food all the time. Hot pot was nothing extraordinary. I could get the same thing in many Japanese restaurants in town minus the cute sand timer. Also, the scallops were sandy.

The not so great -Service was not terrific at such a small restaurant, which is weird. It wasn't bad, but I expected more at this price point. They answered my questions when asked and picked up the table when asked, but I asked a little too much that evening. Food was also extremely slow. They made us eat a 2 hour dinner and we are 1 hour dinner people.

Would I come back? Yeah. The changing menu is way too exciting and I want to see the backyard in the summer. The good was so great that it's enough to compensate for everything else as the everything else wasn't that bad.
Great service great music food was amazing!!! Chris was my waiter and he had such great energy and suggestions for what to order!!! Love this place!!!

Great atmosphere, highly in tune waitstaff, and definitely bustling on a Saturday night. Quite a show from the bar, since you can see the entire kitchen adjacent to you. Reservations are a must, and take a number because there's a stand-by list also. We trusted recommendations from our bartender/waiter, and we were not disappointed. Their Duck Confit dish was one of the most outrageously delicious things I have ever had. Soft corn cake, slow cooked duck, and sliced breast on the side make for a ton of flavor. Watch out for that Dan Dan Spaetzle. There's a reason there are 3 red peppers next to it, so grab a beer while enjoying. Our party of two tried a little of everything, and had an undetermined amount of wine. It was under $250, and I considered it dinner and a show.

I took my gal here for her birthday and she loved it. The food was fantastic, the atmosphere was great and the service was spot on.

I'm not a foodie, I'm actually pretty picky, but I found everything to be delicious. I recommend ordering several dishes, as the portions are small.

We sat at the open kitchen which I highly suggest. It was cool to see how much care the chefs took in preparing each dish. 

The service was great. When we had questions about the food or drinks the servers were happy to stop and give an explanation.

There's a great outdoor area where you can have drinks, order apps, or make s'mores. We finished the night outside and it was very romantic. There were overhead heaters and a blanket was provided incase we were cold (it was winter). The s'mores were delicious, but bring an extra bar of chocolate.

One of the best meals I had in 2018! The food and service was amazing! I recommend sitting at the kitchen counter then moving to the garden for s'mores/hot cocktails in the heated garden during winter.

Lives up to the hype! Gotta thank my friends Grady and Jaime for making a resi and bringing us along. The review below is for a brunch back in early Nov'18 (certain menu items change depending on ingredient availability/seasonality). 

The brunch menu is not extensive but each item we had was pretty wonderful yet different. Hopefully something on there for everyone. We had the house gravlax, the potato latke, duck duo, egg rolls, and some sort of seasonal soufflé.  The egg rolls are probably what most folks try / take photos of. They're served as if they were large fries in a custom paper container with green tomato sauce on the side. They're also incredibly delicious. The house gravlax was a fun spin with the everything cracker vs bagel - also makes the dish less filling and allows you to order moar plates!! Flavors were good- but strong (scallion ricotta specifically). Duck duo and the seasonal soufflé were both also really tasty - particularly enjoyed the scrambled egg in the duck duo. Finally, the potato latke was good (how could fried potato not be) but relative to other dishes was just ok in my opinion - so despite it also being a frequently ordered item, if you're contemplating something else- maybe try the something else! All in all, worth the journey out to Brooklyn, especially on a nice day (they also have a cute garden with seating out back where you can chill and enjoy drinks).

What a lovely spot to have in our neck of the woods.  The decor is understated if well crafted (much of it from local artists), an air of sophistication while maintaining a quaintness that is more restrained.

The food is excellent, the tomato schnitzel is exquisite.  The menu reflects the seasons and I look forward to being to revisit it again soon.  They are very accommodating of dietary restrictions, being able to deftly adjust the preparation to keep the magic of the dish.

As some have noted, a bit of a shock not see a star or two, but then again, it keeps the crowds at bay (somewhat).

Just go! Having gone twice now, I find the flavors are sophisticated, the presentation is sublime, and the staff are professional and friendly. The menu changes occasionally and in the two times I've been, I just picked whatever sounded interesting to me and always enjoyed the work of art that was the dish. This place is great and a wonderful addition to Brooklyn!
Some of the other reviews here seem to be overly critical. Relax and just enjoy this creative and marvelous restaurant!

Creative Gourmet in a friendly atmosphere. Yes, you must go here and be thankful that art can sometimes be edible. Delicious from start to end standouts were, Beer Battered Squash Rings & Rutabaga Tagliatelle. The carrot Crepe with little neck clams I would pass on even though they say it is a signature dish they are known for. Friendly service makes you feel welcomed a great contrast to other restaurant experiences in the same week.

Believe the hype. If this place isn't Michelin starred in 2019, there is something wrong with the universe. 

I recommend you come here with a small group and get EVERYTHING on the menu. They make the most intelligent, inventive choices with their recipes and presentations--and the service is absolutely spectacular. The bar program is one of the best I've seen (and the only regular thing on offer, really, since the menu is seasonal. EVERY cocktail is spectacular!). 

Go early for your reservation so you can wait (with a fabulous drink!) in their backyard (complete with wool blankets and heaters in the winter). 

You may even want to get an appetizer back there, too. Both times we've gone they've had an interesting chicharron/cracker on offer as a starter. Right now (winter 2018/19) it's a Lobster "Thermidor", in which they've managed to get gorgeous lobster flavor into what looks very much like a delicate pork rind, complete with an impossibly light, airy, buttery sauce for dipping. It tastes like the traditional dish, yet eats like buttery, lobstery clouds. Earlier in the year the cracker was "gumbo", I believe, and it was similarly mind-blowingly fantastic.

This kind of culinary brilliance abounds in every dish on their menu. It's like a gastronomic art exhibit you'll want to revisit every season. 

The thing I find most incredible is their ability to refine louder flavor profiles (I'm looking at you, sichuan spaetzle & gobi manchurian) to create impossibly balanced, delicate dishes where individual flavoring components can be distinguished and fully appreciated. The food here isn't just good, it's truly art to the palate.

We've experienced the majority of Eater 38 restaurants in NYC, and quite a few more with current or former Michelin stars. Olmsted ranks above them all, hands down.

Thank goodness for reservations at this neighborhood eatery.  I arrived earlier than my party and was promptly seated.  My drink and appetizer of fried squash decorating branches of a tree set on our table  arrived at the same time as the others in my party -- what a great time had by all feasting on a delicious selection of many plates to share. I can still taste my rosemary drink with mezcal.  Yum. The servers all seemed to truly enjoy working at Olmsteads and they conveyed that sentiment at every opportunity.
The experience here is excellent. Great food and cocktails. Highly recommend for an evening out with friends.

This was the best meal my husband and I have had in quite some time.  We needed to make a change to our reservation and they were extremely accommodating.  The service , food, and decor were perfect.  I cannot wait to go back and try the rest of the menu.

This was such a wonderful brunch! From the service, to the food, to the ambiance, it was all wonderful.

We started with the lox, which was absolutely perfect! My friend hates cream cheese, and she even enjoyed having cream cheese with every bite.  

We ultimately tried about 6-7 dishes for the three of us. 

Highlight: hot toddy cocktail and Irish coffee, quite potent but so delicious! The egg rolls are also such a cute presentation and really good.

Will definitely return for the service alone!

Fantastic food! We came here for brunch and ordered the fall "pancake" which is a lovely warm fruit focaccia with hot caramel sauce. We also got the potatoe latke which was great as well. 

One note for vegans and lactose intolerant folks, pretty much everything had some dairy product in it so I wouldn't say it is vegan friendly.

Olmsted was very good. But in the battle of Vanderbilt supremacy, Faun holds the title for us. Even if Olmsted has more of the hype.

What threw us off the most was the presentation of the squash rings. We don't like a lot of gimmicks when dealing with food. And this was pretty much a gimmick. So there was that.

The other kind of weird thing was the really large duck liver mousse starter... which was really good. But way too substantial as a starter. I know, I know, complaining about too large a portion is weird. But we hate wasting food so overly large dishes create an unnecessary dilemma...

Beyond that, the rest of the food was quite good, the highlight of which was the carrot crepe dish. Just wonderful...

Perhaps we'd visit again (reservations are hard to come by at this spot) or maybe we might visit the other less hyped, but equally as good restaurants in Prospect Heights... Decisions, decisions...

This review is based on a 15 second interaction with the hostess/waitress at the front door.
My bad for not checking what time they stop serving lunch (2:45), but when I asked her if she knew any other place we could go, she tapped the phone in my hand and said "you know what this thing can do for you darling, give you lots of ideas." So I had an even better idea what to do with my phone...do not waste your time going to a place with such a rude, condescending fucking staff.

Went for dinner. I really wanted to love this restaurant, but the food was lacking a little. The service was great. I think i fell into the hype of the place and had too high of an expectation. You are recommended to order 3 dishes to share with table. I liked the bouillabaisse and the duck (its made 2 ways, only the breast was good). Food is creative, but the flavors were not there.

Really good brunch spot.  I had high expectations and they were met. We started with drinks, I had a Virgin Mary and it was amazing.  We ordered the potatoe latke, butternut squash bread, duck duo, and spinach borek. Everything was delicious.  Service was attentive and water was constantly refilled. They are fairly small plates but we were stuffed with the amount we got. Can't wait to return to try other menu items.

Quite good, but not quite great. There's a lot of hype around this place, and it just falls short of living up to it.

We went for brunch and got the egg rolls, breakfast burger, and tomato schnitzel thing. The breakfast burger was pretty good, but not that memorable. The egg rolls were a novelty, but didnt have a whole lot going on taste-wise. They'd be forgettable as well if they didn't burn the roof of my mouth, hot pocket style. The tomato schnitzel thing (cant remember the actual name) was awesome, but it unfortunately looks to no longer be on the current menu.

The ambiance of the place is great, and overall the food was pretty good, but not that memorable. But then again, maybe I just have memory issues. Never ride a razor scooter without a helmet.

3.89/5

Had a really nice meal and date night here. Sat in the window seat with my boyfriend. I'd never been here before. Their service was prompt and super friendly. My rosemary cocktail was delicious. 
We ordered six dishes. Two from each section.  

From snacks we ordered the lobster thermidor which was good but which I wish had more crackers. We also ordered the squash rings which were super delicious. One of my favorite bites of food. Definitely order those. 

From the small plates we ordered the beet salad which was honestly my favorite dish. So balanced and flavorful. We also ordered the uni and sweet potato pierogis which were a definite standout. Highly recommend ordering both these dishes. 

From large plates we ordered the trout which was interesting and definitely good but not a knock out. We ended with the Thai duck which I loved. Both preparations of the duck were super flavorful. We also tried the Rutabaga tagliatelle which was way better than I thought it would be. Super satisfying but also clean tasting. Loved the "al dente" noodles. 
Really great meal overall and reasonably priced unlike restaurants with similar aesthetics (and worse food) in Brooklyn.

The food here is both creative and quality-driven, but this doesn't necessarily equal delicious. Carrot crepe with chewy clams, mullet tartare with cranberry, beets with hazelnuts, trout hiding under a blanket of brussels sprouts. Flavor and texture combinations didn't work for my palette. Maybe the dishes should remain abstract, as they began.
Service was slow and inconsistent, despite many tables waiting for their reservations.  Overrated and underseasoned.

Olmsted is a beautiful restaurant that, overall, lives up to the hype. Food and service are both excellent. The backyard is really special. 

I went with hubs and we just ordered bunch of stuff to share. The Dan Dan spaetzel was a favorite, it really well done. Nice heat but well-balanced.  Loved the bouillabaisse hot pot and the carrot crepe which was a perfect blend of sweet freshness and umami. I can't speak to the pork dish but hubs loved it. 

We ended the meal with the s'mores, which was fun but also kind of felt like a gimmick. Delicious, because s'mores, but a thing that we could probably do without next time.

Came here for brunch last Sunday with the hubby without a reservation. The wait was an hour, so we put our names down and went home to wait for their text. We received a text stating our table was ready within the hour which I appreciated and were sat at the bar once we arrived. I happen to love sitting at the bar so this was a definite plus. 

We started with a Bloody Mary and carrot mimosa, the Bloody Mary was really good! Savory but not spicy. I had asked in advance if the mimosa ran very sweet given the elderflower liquor and was told that it was quite balanced, but I personally disagree, so I bullied hubby into switching drinks with me since he said he didn't mind it. 

As an app we shared the B.E.C. egg rolls, which came in a serving of 4 small egg rolls, they came with a nice acidic house-made green tomato ketchup. I though they were perfect size for an app and should have been listed under the small/share plates section, I would have been annoyed getting them as an entree. I got the Thai duck duo which came with delicious flatbread and my husband got the burger. The bartender described the burger as an elevated Big Mac and we thought that was a really fair description. Both were good but not outstanding. The burger was saucy and perfectly cooked, but lacked that special something to put it on a crave-able burgers list. I found the duck flavors to be very reminiscent of Thailand, but lacking in some heat so I asked for extra Thai hot peppers with my duck and the bartender brought some but also suggested I try their homemade hot sauce. Their hot sauce is delicious, super flavorful, but I didn't find it spicy, so I ended up adding the hot sauce and peppers to my duck to kick up the heat closer to Thai level. 

Service was attentive and friendly. Ultimately, we would return but order different things, we definitely didn't have anything we would crave a second time (except that hot sauce).

Really good - with a party of 6 we ordered the whole menu. Most things were awesome and everything good. The savory donuts to begin with the chicken liver pate were excellent. All the duck dishes excelled.

Been dying to go here, and finally came up with a plan since it's so difficult to get a reservation here-we went at 4:50pm figuring we could sit at the bar. We weren't the only ones with this idea-there were a few other people waiting outside without a reservation.

We sat at the bar, which actually is a really nice
Area to eat, and the bartender slash server was very attentive. 

Our favorites were the Squash Rings, the Rutabaga Tagliatelle (Delish!), and Dave's Trout. I could have lived without the Carrot Crepe and the Lobster Thermidor-didn't really knock my socks off like the first three. Dessert was great too, forgot what we had tho!

This place is upscale farm to table done right!! 

The vibe is relaxed and buzzy at the same time, but not too scene-y. A great spot to bring parents or a date, though getting a reservation is near impossible. We came on a Sunday night at 6pm and had to wait 2 hours just to get seated at the bar! 

You must try the carrot crepe - it is one of their signature dishes. The clams are a pleasant surprise! P.S. the dish looks nothing like you would expect a crepe to look (in fact way more aesthetically pleasing with carrot ribbons and flowers). 

I even liked their oysters and I typically find them slimy and gross. The squash perogis are creamy and buttery inside, balancing the crispy dough on the outside. The mushroom spatzel is tasty but nothing special. 

My favorites were the mains - we ordered the rutabaga "tagliatelle" and heritage pork. Oh my goodness the pasta was the best squash ribbons I have ever tasted. It was because of the creamy brown butter sauce, but it wasn't too heavy. The heritage pork was almost equally good - perfectly cooked and with a very generous portion of broccoli rabe. 

We didn't get to do the s'mores outside because it was snowing, but will come back when it's warmer for sure! 

Overall an amazing meal that is worth the wait!

Overall, I'm not sure that this place lived up to the hype. The food was good, but surprisingly really heavy and cream-based for a "farm to table" restaurant. We made a reservation online about a month before we came, and it seems like that's the only way to get seated during a normal dinner time without a wait.

The good: the ambiance, drinks, and presentation of the food. It's a really small restaurant and feels super cozy, but I loved how they had an open concept kitchen so you can see the chefs working on your food. The cocktail menu was super unique and as you can see from the pictures, the way that the food and drinks are displayed is very well done.

The bad: the menu selection and the restaurant's emphasis on CREAM. As someone who doesn't eat pork or shellfish, I didn't realize quite how limited my options were before I got here. The online menu doesn't include the fact that the duck and lamb dishes both have pork and I believe the duck also has a "shellfish glaze." Considering how common food restrictions are, it would have been nice to have had these ingredients listed out on the menu ahead of time.

Also, nearly everything we ordered had a cream sauce. I was really surprised because usually farm-to-table restaurants emphasize the freshness of the ingredients themselves, but it ended up feeling like a very heavy meal.

The weird: the service! Although I'm rarely ever one to complain about getting too much attention from waitstaff, we had about 4 different people ask us if we wanted more drinks and another 4 people come over to replace each sip of water we took from our glasses. We literally had one person put more water in my cup before I even drank from our last refill. While this seems like an absurdly nit-picky comment, it did make it hard to have a conversation with someone coming over and frequently interrupting us.

Came here for brunch. The Egg cheese bacon egg rolls were so so good. Loved them. The restaurant is very cute with good service. Everything else we ordered was just fine. The burger reminded me of a Big Mac and the donuts and potato latke were very average.
No expectations going, super fun staff, go with Simon. Creative menu but food just tastes good. Garden in back for drinks. Seasonal menu. Get Froyo.

Inventive beyond reproach and such a fun atmosphere, Olmsted is, above all, playful. The variety of spaces - bar, garden, dining room - are beautiful and complement each other nicely, there's a good flow to the space. It's a reliably great experience but dishes miss the mark more often than you'd like, better in theory than execution.

Service and staff absolutely amazing. Food beautiful but very sparse and overpriced. Need to have a few dishes that will meet the needs of a hungry diners; (a.k.a. men who came for dinner and had appetizers) at present not there and needs some serious thought....Cauliflower had min flavor, duck salad way too salty ( too much fish sauce) and without a doubt  the highlight of the night were Chris and Kirsten and the s'mores under the NYC skylights  - thank you for terrific evening - but went home a bit hungry - I am not going to lie

KenScale: 8.5/10

As I have been carrying on my resolutions for 2019 to revisit restaurants I had previously been to and select places that I would like to go to more regularly with my wife Jun, one of the restaurants that has been on my radar for second look was Olmsted, one of the best newcomers that opened in 2016. When Jun and I, back then not married together yet, we had a lot of things to like about the thoughtful culinary philosophy of the kitchen emphasizing the freshness of ingredients and finding ways to present small dish-centric plates at affordable prices to become a truly neighborhood destination every New Yorker would love to go every once in a while. Olmsted was almost universally praised when it opened, but as I have witnessed with other restaurants that made a splash in the beginning only to fade after several months, I wasn't sure what our second visit would look like. On a recent Sunday, after stopping by Brooklyn Museum nearby the restaurant to watch the ongoing Frida Kahlo exhibition, Jun and I went to the restaurant for an early dinner, and it was clear that Olmsted is still going very strong.

Just like our first visit, the menu at Olmsted consists almost entirely of small plates ideal for sharing and no single dish costing more than $24. This time, Jun and I made it a point to order dishes we hadn't tried previously, and had a lot to like about our choices, starting with the dip inspired by lobster thermidor that was a perfect snack to kick off the meal. I guess there was a mix-up with our sourdough and honey butter bread order as it took us nearly 20 minutes to get it; perhaps our server felt bad about it and wanted to express apology with a free plate of the now iconic carrot crepe with little neck clams and sunflower underneath that was one of our favorite dishes from the first visit. It was as beautifully plated as I had remembered, and was still an outstanding dish showing the remarkable ingenuity of the kitchen to marry garden and sea. One of my favorite dishes of the night was mushroom spätzle following the Russian tradition of stroganoff style dishes. It was earthy and delightfully creamy without overpowering my palate. If this were to be my lunch every day, I would be very delighted. The kitchen at Olmsted draws inspirations from outside the U.S. often to great effect, like the lamb chakna (a type of spicy stew from India) with red lentil naan and pear chutney on the side. You don't feel the same fiery intensity of Indian cuisine, but the way Olmsted reimagined the dish to fit its culinary philosophy was quite memorable. For larger dishes, we both enjoyed grilled scallops with winter slaw, spicy peanut and XO sauce for its playful take on Chinese flavor. The only dish that was off from our dinner was the duck, which really comes in two formats (duck breast and dark meat accompanied by watercress salad). While the duck breast's texture wasn't too bad, we wished it didn't have the sweet sauce underneath that surprisingly overpowered the meat, and the watercress salad was simply too aggressive in flavor to give us any chance to savor the dark meat. Still, we both agreed that Olmsted is a very good restaurant while enjoying another iconic dish from the restaurant, the frozen yogurt with lavender honey (if we had more room for dessert, we probably would've tried the s'mores again at the garden but we were beyond stuffed by the time we were ready for dessert).  

Getting a reservation at Olmsted is still very difficult although if you plan ahead and don't mind early dinner seating, you should be OK. The dining space was full of diners and there were still guests waiting for their turn at the garden, showing the enduring popularity of Olmsted in the Brooklyn neighborhood. There is full bar as always with inventive cocktail menus inspired by various elements of the garden. New York City now has plenty of restaurants that claim to be farm-to-table in concept, but it's hard to top Olmsted with its own garden and the consistency of the kitchen's execution using the best ingredients available. Because of the letdown from the duck, I will hold off giving the KenScale All-Star to Olmsted for now but will certainly visit the restaurant again in the near future to give it another shot.

This place is brilliant. We sat at the bar and received excellent service from the bartender both for drinks and food. Almost every dish was novel and inventive, and certainly all were tasty. The cocktails were similarly fascinating and delicious. Plus the price was reasonable. They deserve their current place on various "top NYC eatery" lists.
This place is very unique.  You can order lots of different dishes from 5-8 and enjoy the symphony of exquisite tastes.  Highly recommend this restaurant. The bigger company the better.
Loved it.  It's a great place for a date or to have good food and drinks with your friends. Lil pricey but worth every penny. You won't be disappointed

People have been raving about this place for a while, so thanks to my sister in law, I got a gift certificate to check it out. My better half and I decided to check it out for lunch. Wow am I glad we did. Yes, the food was outstanding- special shout out for the butternut squash bread with clotted cream and white peach jam.... but the best thing by far was our enthusiastic, sassy and incredibly knowledgable server Miriam. This woman was a joy to be served by and all of her recommendations were spot on. Do yourself a favor and find a way to get to this place. Yo Miriam... great Rosé and thanks for a memorable afternoon.

What a disappointment. We've eaten here at least 5 times. Showed up as a walk-in. The new hostess gave us a 45- minute wait. We showed up after an hour and waited for another 10 minutes to be sat next to the door. The hostess was fake and clearly didn't care to make our experience any better.  Will reconsider next time.

The lavender drink tastes like something you should lather on yourself rather than consume as a drink. I saw that it was bourbon based (I'm as whisky and bourbon drinker) and figured the lavender would be a nice change of pace. But it was too much. Im sticking with the hard stuff. That said the food was great. The beet salad was very tasty and refreshing,  and the rutabaga tagliatelle was  amazing! It had a pasta consistency even though it's a root. The cream and cheese was perfectly cooked with the rutabaga to give it that authentic pasta texture.

Second time I've been here, and progressing in the wrong direction unfortunately. If you're going to charge steep prices for small portions, those portions better be tasty, and they just weren't. The "snap pea sushi" was smothered in a lemon slice that overpowered everting else - what a waste of fresh fluke. The asparagus in the "fried asparagus" was so thin and overpowered by the batter that if I closed my eyes I wouldn't have known what fried item I was eating.

The staff is kind, and the ambience is great, but the menu is falling short.

Feeling ripped off after having the Mother's Day tasting menu - 125pp but got about 75pp worth of food max based on prior menus (basically got 2 apps, entree, and a shared dessert). 

Would have hoped to see better / special ingredients for such a high price and not feel like I'm paying a tax to take my wife out on Mother's Day. 

With that said, the service was fantastic and the food is good - just don't go here on a holiday or you're going to pay for the privilege.

I have had my eye on Olmsted for a while so I was super excited when I was able to snag a reservation!  We started off our meal with their ginger beer that was both refreshing and delicious.  For starters we had the wheatberry bread with honey butter as well as the crab rangoons.  The bread was nice and warm and the honey butter was the perfect pairing.  ** Note to my vegetarians, they will make a vegetarian version of the crab rangoons upon request!  These were also good and seem very popular but probably not my favorite part of the meal.  The rutabaga tagliatelle was definitely the showstopper, I didn't even know it was possibly to make something like this out of rutabaga but it was one of the best vegetarian dishes I have ever had.  It had amazing flavors and a texture I prefer to other types of vegetable "pastas" like zoodles or spaghetti squash or even actual pasta.  It really absorbed the flavoring of the seasoning and the cheeses well but and was all the more enjoyable as it was somewhat guilt-free haha!  For dessert we opted for the chocolate mousse and received complimentary frozen yogurt.  The mousse was nice with a cocoa-y flavor and the frozen yogurt was quite unique in both flavor and texture.  I would definitely recommend both.

The ambiance was nice and quiet, would be great for a datenight or small group gathering.  The service was also great and again I was happy at how willing they were to offer vegetarian variations on some of their offerings.

From the moment I was seated, I recognized the meticulous curation of every aspect at Olmsted. I was in awe of the thought and care put into treating diners with an experience rather than merely serving delicious food -- from the artistically laid out menu and napkins to the child-like simplistic plate-ware; (even the washroom is worth a visit!) If even these details were so scrupulously attended to, I could not wait to taste the thoughtful dishes the kitchen would stir up.

Popcorn Monkfish

A bite-size rendition of the classic fish and chips. As a lover of monkfish, this was a delightful appetizer to begin with; however, I do wish that there was more substance with each bite. The pieces were fairly miniature, and perhaps that contributed to the lack of fish in each bite. That being said, with a dip in the aioli sauce and a touch of lime, each piece was quite tasteful and crisp to the bite.

Sweet Potato & Uni Perogies with Sauerkraut & Sour Cream 

The addition of uni to traditional perogies was a clever touch. If sweet potatoes were not already soft enough, the uni exploded and coated my mouth with the same feeling I get when I pull a faux fur throw over myself. Aside from the uni, the taste of these perogies were good but not great. Having waited 40 minutes after the monkfish for this, I definitely expected a more impressive dish to compensate for the unpleasantly long service time. Nevertheless, it was a delicious velvety explosion of flavors.

Male Mullet Tartare with Cranberry Chimichurri, Lavash

The cranberry chimichurri was the subtle secret to success. Its fruity sweetness complemented the tartare with utter grace, without which would be rather average. With the tartare resembling a South American ceviche and the lavash originating from Armenia, this course was a cultural exhibition. Traveling half way around the world with a foot in each land was a rather uncomfortable stretch. Although the pairing of these cultural staples was not a success in my book, the distinct flavors from each separate entity were very enjoyable.

Rutabaga "Tagliatelle" with Burgundy Black Truffle, Brown Butter

As I was diving into the "pasta", I was puzzled as to why my "tagliatelle" was refreshingly crunchy before realizing that they were instead thin strips of root vegetables. Having been immersed in Alinea's gastronomical genius, I would expect nothing less from Chef and Co-Owner Greg Braxton, but to fool my senses. After a series of lackluster dishes, this plot twist certainly revived a spark of excitement in my heart. The heaviness of the truffle and butter did overcome the lighter veggie strips slightly, which may have also contributed to its unnecessary saltiness. In spite of that, this was still stood out as a favorite of the night.

Guinea Hen Roasted & Confit with Poached Quince & Caramelized Sunchoke 

The roasted hen was as soft as foam and the confit unravelled effortlessly in my mouth with its perfect stringiness. Hidden beneath the layers of hen confit were the poached quinces, a savior to the excessively salted confit. With a hint of sweetness, the quinces resurrected these wasted pieces of meat. I unfortunately could not even finish the confit because of how salty it was. This promising dish went to waste with its overly salted seasoning, what a pity.

TL;DR:
Price Range (per person): $50-60
After reading all the raving reviews and the remarkable experiences of the chefs/owners, I entered Olmsted with great excitement and high expectations. Instead, I was greeted with unreasonably salted dishes, odd fusions of food and ingredients, and unjustifiably long service times. Certainly, there were commendable aspects for each course, but the bad definitely outweighed that good that night. Despite its undeniably outstanding concept and presentation, our dinner service lacked substance. It would be a lie to say I wasn't disappointed; however, I'd like to give Olmsted the benefit of the doubt and claim that this visit as a very unlucky and unfortunate one. Upon my next visit to New York, I would certainly give this revered restaurant another shot at the hoop in hopes that they'll score. (3/5)

Insider's Note:
As per any praised restaurant in New York, seats are hard to come, and even more so at Olmsted with its endless recommendations. We made sure to make reservations a month before, but still could only land dinner at 9:15pm. If you want the freedom to choose your time and date, be sure to call more than a month prior to your planned visit.  

A blooming garden is hidden at the rear end of the restaurant, which I believe opens up for seating in the spring/summer season. Sipping on a cocktail with an appetizer in hand would be quite charming to have in a land where the dishes you consume are forged from.
Fun and delicious. A little bit fussy, but well thought out dishes and good service. Eating at the counter is a treat -- as you can watch them cook and plate such interest-looking dishes.
Cocktails, wine, food and service were all excellent and prices were very reasonable.  Best meal i've had in a long time.

Olmstead might just be Brooklyn's best restaurant... REALLY!!!   Why you ask?   Unique ambiance, excellent food and great service!!! Is there anything else you are looking for in a great restaurant???

If you want the full experience, head to Olmsted when the sun goes down, have drinks/appetizers in the back garden enjoying the twinkle lights, the night sky and watching the ingredients you are about to enjoy growing in raised beds and the greenhouse... Let's face it, the garden is a magical place!!!

Then, if you get a bit chilly at night, be sure you bring enough of your friends to book the private dining room... what an awesome place for a festive meal surrounded by the people you enjoy the most!!!   While many private dining rooms with high ceilings and large tables seem formal or cold... This on feels warm and intimate!!!   I LOVE THIS PLACE!!!! 

Now to the food... Everything (and I mean everything) my group ate at Olmsted got a unanimous thumbs up.   The meats were perfectly cooked, the vegetables and alternative (animal based) protein dishes served to the vegan members of our group were flavorful and, when it came to dessert, the chef knocked our socks off!   I WANT THEIR FROZEN YOGURT RECIPE AND I WANT IT NOW!!!!   There were 16 of us at dinner and we spent a good part of the last half hour trying to figure out the ingredients they used to make such a subtle, nuanced and deliciously refreshing dessert.   Siskel and Ebert agree... "Two Thumbs Up" for Olmsed from appetizers, to ambiance, to the main course, to dessert!!!!

Let me preface this review with saying I've been wanting to come here for over a year. I follow the place on Instagram and was SO excited to finally make it in. 

Pros: Very cool atmosphere, and the back garden seems like a perfect place to sip cocktails while you wait for your table. We didn't get to enjoy it because of rain, but I can imagine it on a nice day. 

Cons: So overpriced. This was the first time in NYC I truly felt scammed by a restaurant. Let me explain...

Upon arrival, our group of 4 was recommended to order the entire menu despite being told "none of the items are super small, but none are huge." Okay, so moderate sizes, right? Still 12 dishes for 4 people felt like a lot of they weren't small, but whatever - let's do it! We felt like big shots ordering the entire menu. 

The first item comes out - the lobster cracker dish. It's literally 4 (FOUR) glorified wonton crisps with a lobster flavoring for $14. And it was served on a bed of pebbles. Like, small rocks. I still can't get over it. The crackers were the kind of thing you could get a pound of in Chinatown for $1. I've never seen such a bold move by a restaurant.

It was followed by 4 pieces of partially deep-fried asparagus for $12. Nothing unique about it. Then 4 sweet pea pods wrapped in lemon for $10. Again, all very bold moves by Olmsted. 

Some dishes were definitely interesting and just fine, but definitely nothing wowed our group. Especially given how much we all wanted to love it. I'm usually a huge fan of small, shareable plates with interesting flavor combinations - this place was 100% up my alley. I'm no stranger to paying premiums for unique, interesting dishes. And while we enjoyed the beet salad and the bread with honey butter, I really don't remember the rest... and we were there only an hour ago. 

I am so disappointed to write this review. I had such high hopes. But one $400 dinner later, I can't recommend this to anyone unless price is truly irrelevant for you.

Overrated. $100 per person for food that's really nothing to get excited about. A man on the sidewalk in front of the deli next door literally shouted "white privilege!" at us as we were walking out. Was offended, but hard to disagree.

After we sat, waiter said we should "order entire menu" for our party of 4. So we did. First time ever. Dishes were a mostly a joke. There's much better in NYC.

This is farm to table with pizazz. The food is inventive and offers up some creative combinations. Not everything was tasty to my palette, but I was genuinely intrigued by the flavors. The ambiance is just right, and the service was efficient and kind. This is a must-stop restaurant in Brooklyn and seems to be best suited for two people.
Beautiful place with garden, good food and friendly staff. Love to come back. Bloody Mary is legit and the brunch is definitely a good time to come.

Can it be worth the hassle getting a reservation here? I always assumed the answer would be no--how good could it possibly be? It's that good! You should go!

The food is inventive and delicious. The menu changes with the seasons to keep it interesting. The drinks are excellent--and there's a strong non-alcoholic drinks selection, too. Great teas to go with your dessert. And wonderful, attentive service. All this in a low-key atmosphere that's the exact opposite of stuffy. 

I really don't know what else I could ask for. My new favorite NYC restaurant.

Decent brunch near the park. We stopped in on a Saturday with a reservation (recommended since the space is small and has a backyard that doesn't have real tables (more like benches). We sat at the bar.

We started with the duck liver mousse, which had a jelly layer that paired really well with the lightly toasted brioche. The beet salad was shaved and crispy, which is so different from the usual soft beet salad. It was a bit too much sour but fresh. We probably could've skipped the squash bread since it was slightly dry and too much carbs for us. 

Highlight was the duo (duck sausage and eggs), which paired well with the snap peas. The eggs were really tender but wish there was more sausages.

Let me be honest this place is good, but I mean for the hassle it is to get a reservation...meh. I also think they have some great stuff but not all of it is mind blowing. This is a spot that is good but I don't think is worth the wait (to get a Ressie), the price (some stuff is really OVERPRICED), the backyard is cool and the drinks are fine. Again in that area there are some other better spots you can walk right into and have a seat.
Amazing service, impeccable plating and divine food! Cannot rave enough about this place.

Olmsted is a popular restaurant in Brooklyn that is known for its farm to table cuisine and lovely backyard. We got the chance to come here on a Saturday for brunch, and had made a reservation. We'd specifically requested seating in their backyard, and were led there after we arrived. 
After our friend arrived, we ordered, and our food was served in a timely fashion. 
Two of our group who eat meat, shared a couple of dishes between them, while I opted to have my own vegetarian dish, the chickpea socca. There were only a few vegetarian dishes on the menu, so I had little choice. 
The chickpea socca was made from chickpea flour, and came with two perfectly fried eggs, avocado, and some vegetables. The presentation was something like what you would expect from a high end restaurant. The taste was fine, but nothing amazing or memorable. 
My friends who eat meat were happier than I was with their dishes, which included a bacon and egg roll, and the beet salad. 
Service was attentive, efficient and friendly. I would maybe come back for dinner, but based on what I had this time, not for brunch.

Been here for brunch and for dinner. A spot I will bring any visiting friend/family member...assuming I plan well enough for a reservation or we don't mind waiting for a table. Everything from the plates to the presentation to the taste is superb.

Truly lovely dinner here. Food might have been a 4, but the experience more than pushes it to a 5.

Their private dining room is stellar. Service is super attentive and you basically feel like you are eating in your own personal restaurant since even the entrance is separate from the rest of the restaurant. Highly recommend booking it if you ever have group dining needs.

We tried:

Fried asparagus - Light tempura with a delicious sauce.

Snap pea sushi - Omg I loved this. Raw fish draped over a snap pea with a slice of lemon on top, lovely contrasts of flavors and textures.

Duck liver mousse - This was revelatory for some but I was less blown away. It's very well executed duck liver mousse, but that can be found in other places as well.

Shaved beet salad - One of the less exciting dishes

Kale Crab Rangoon - Stuffed with crab meat and quite tasty.

Carrot Crepe - Iconic for a reason. Honestly found it heading a bit on the sweeter end but it was unique.

Nashville hot soft shell crab - Fine but it's just soft shell crab, nothing revelatory 

Heritage Pork - Wow this was excellent. The pork seemed a bit like chopped then reshaped like a singular piece but the fhppping is what brought out the flavor. I dunno what they're doing here but it's excellent.

Frozen Yogurt - Topped with a thick meringue it's interesting tho not necessarily my cup of tea

Old school chocolate mousse - Rich and creamy chocolate mousse topped with delicious creme fraiche.

My wife and I have been to Olmsted several times and always been impressed.  The kitchen has always been very accommodating for our vegetarian and vegan preferences, something that we truly appreciate!  Last night we had some great cocktails (negronis!), pea sushi and ridiculously tasty asparagus appetizers, followed by a delicious falafel, and an amazing spätzle.  Thank you once again!

this was an EXCEPTIONAL dining experience, worth the fact that i made
the RESERVATION 3 months in advance....THEY ARE POPULAR but
they are superior. Service, etc.  Absolutely fabulous and I can't wait
to go back (from L.A.).

Really not sure what the fuss is about. Came for brunch, the menu is VERY limited if you don't eat meat. The portions were small and I just was not blown away. Maybe dinner is what makes this place so popular. It's a
Cute space and the garden is gorgeous. The service was also really good and that's what the 3 stars are for. Good really was mediocre.

Was so glad I could finally visit Olmstead for brunch when I had family in town. We visited on a Friday and it was so lovely. We had all of the Instagram favorites: the egg rolls, the potato pancake and the liver mousse. I can't remember what cocktails we got but they were delicious! The restaurant itself is so fun; you can visit their garden with live chickens in the back. As instagram-baity the egg rolls were, I still talk about them! They were so delicious; I immediately wanted more! Will be back, hopefully sooner than later.

After coming here once for brunch and leaving without much of an impression, this dinner blew me away! We walked in around 5:30 when they open for dinner and sat at the bar. Our bartender was awesome!! So helpful when it came to picking dishes (we wanted to order everythingg) and called the some over to help us with a bottle of wine. He also made our starter cocktails super fast! 

The menu looked great for the season but we ended up going with duck patte, carrot crepe, spatzle, crab and kale rangoons, scallops, falafel and desert. 

The spatzle and crepe really stuck out. I'm still not sure how they made the spatzel but it was luxurious and silky smooth soft over perfectly chewy pasta and tons of cheese (how could you go wrong???). The carrot crepe is a signature dish which totally doesn't surprise me, I wouldn't immediately pair carrots and clams but they do it perfectly. 

We got a bottle of bubbly because I feel like it pairs best when there are flavors all over the place and the somm helped us pick something dry but not too thin in body. It was perfect. 

We got the frozen yogurt dessert and we couldn't stop raving about it. The whipped cream on top is like thick tangy sour cream and underneath is the creamy not too frosty ice cream. On a hot new york summer day it was truly unbeatable, we're already trying to replicate it at home. 

I will say we probably ordered too much food, but like I said, it was hard to pick from this line up. I do wish we had gotten the bread service, we had a little carb-based jealousy with the couple next to us!

Olmsted is creative and affordable, and I love a menu that continues to change!

Olmsted definitely lives up to the hype. I'm not gonna give a rundown of everything we ate because I don't feel like writing that much. Just know that almost everything we ate was exceptional. There were a couple misses (Kale Rangoon and Popcorn Fish), but both were still good. They just weren't as amazing as the rest of the meal. Service was warm and non-pretentious.
I expected much better food considering the reviews and buzz but they were expensive, small plates. The entrees were fine but forgettable. I won't ever come back.

FOOD 3.5
service 4

Went there on a Saturday afternoon. Made a reservation at 5:15pm, emailed the restaurant around 4:40pm to inform them that we will be late for 15mins. Got there at 5:30pm, we were told to wait in the garden area. The garden was really cute, you can order drinks and small bites while you are waiting. The cocktails are really good. But there are so many mosquitos in the garden, I got bit 5 times while waiting. They did provide bug spray, however, it's not very helpful.  The service is good, we sat at the bar and the bartender had been very helpful and friendly. The food is actually ok, we weren't blown away by any of the dishes. The ingredients are fresh and the presentation is good, however, the quality and taste of the food were just average to us. My bf left unsatisfied and we ended up going to Ichiran for our second dinner of that day lol. Overall, a cute restaurant in bk that worth checking out if you are nearby, but probably won't go back.

Total disappointment!!! We are from out of state and had read about Olmsted, its Michelin rating and the brilliant chef Greg Baxtrom. We considered ourselves lucky to have a reservation. We ordered three courses: snacks, then small plates, and larger plates. Snacks (3) and small plates (3) were all served together. We then waited 45 minutes for our last three dishes. Food was cold and bland. At no point did our server apologize for the time lags. We were made to feel that we we were lucky to be there!
Maybe they just had an off night, yet based on our experience we cannot recommend Olmsted and I don't believe we shall be back.

This place absolutely blew my mind. My boyfriend's brother bought him a giftcard to this restaurant, and we planned to surprise him with it on the night of. I made a reservation in advance, but the only time available was at the bar at 9:30 PM. I emailed the customer service team to see if we could have some better seating and an earlier dining time, and they were extremely helpful in seating us at the Chef's Counter and moving the reservation up 2 hours. I forgot to call ahead and ask if I could pre-order dessert for him as a surprise, so I quickly shot them another email in the uber to the restaurant with the order and asked that it be brought out after our meal, and they responded immediately and said yes! 

When we got there, we were seated right away, and looked over the menus. Our server was very patient explaining how the serving works (it's recommended to get multiple dishes, which are shared family style), what some of the menu items were, and even helped us plan around my dietary restrictions (I'm a vegetarian and allergic to nuts). 

We got the Roasted Shishitos & Bottarga, Summer Squash Sum Tum (without cashews), Garden Basil Spatzle, Einkorn Bread w/ Brown Butter, and Heirloom Tomato Schnitzel. We had a couple of cocktails when we arrived, and a beer each to close out the night. For dessert we got the Chocolate Mousse - they even put a candle in it for my boyfriend! It was a really lovely evening. I would highly recommend this place to anyone looking for a high quality dining experience. Make sure to reserve your table early as this place fills up!!
Amazing service and food. Walked in and got a table. The backyard garden looked great. Definitely recommend checking it out.

The food was very good here however the person who waited on us was super scattered and made the dinner feel quite anxious. Definitely not a relaxing way to spend a few hundred dollars. I'm guessing if we had a different server, the experience would've been more pleasant. Very cute place and a lovely garden (which unfortunately  closed before we could get there to enjoy our dessert.)

Olmsted is one of my favorite restaurants in Brooklyn! The dishes are delicious and interesting and, while on the smaller size, it always leaves me wanting to come back for more. One of my favorite things on the menu is actually the yogurt dessert. Really light and beautiful; a perfect way to end a meal. I also really appreciate the casual, but sophisticated decor of the place. The entire vibe is really unique, upscale but not stuffy or trying too hard.  The garden is absolutely beautiful and I'd recommend getting a cocktail out there before your meal.

Went there for the first time for brunch last weekend. Made a reservation for 6 people but last minute we added another person into our table. The servers were really nice about it, and were being very accommodating to our needs. My glass of water was never empty and was constantly filled up to the top! I love the interior decor as well as their backyard! 
As for the food, it completely blew my mind! Every dish was so unique in the flavor and presentation. Knowing the fact that they grew their greens in their backyard, this is basically a semi backyard farm to table, I love it even more! 7 of us we ordered about 8 dishes, and if we werent so full, we would have get to try their dessert too. oh well, next time! Because I will definitely visit Olmsted again! I highly recommend! :) Thank you for the great experience the whole time in Olmsted!

Was excited to eat at this semi hard to reserve restaurant. Brunch was ok, while the selections were unique/creative, i didn't fall over my chair. Restaurants looked was nice and crisp w an open kitchen concept. Where my review will go wrong is service. Waitress did fine up until we indicated to her there were live budancing in our food. (Notice the many plants throughout the restaurant) However the waitress had this "eww" look on her face (eww at me for pointing out something I need help correcting or the bug?). The shocker was no apologies comment/feedback from her (so I guess the eww was at a picky customer who don't like bugs in her food). She simply took the plate away and later came back w a new one. I thought this was a Michelin graded but that was an odd and I suppose rude experience....unless the bugs were part of the culinary experience.

What a farce! This is the most pretentious and overpriced restaurant I have ever frequented. Aside from minuscule portions of food, the way staff behaves more like used car salesman, figuratively strong arming patrons into ordering more food than they could sensibly afford. The pitch is that if you don't order lots of shareables, you will wait A LONG TIME for your food...and we did. My advice, stay away!

I came here for dinner after my coworkers and friends suggested it. The service was great and the concept of having a backyard for dessert and drinks was nice. 

The food was good, but struggled with the price-for-value component. Portions were rather small for the cost of the dish. I ordered the watermelon sushi, kale crab Rangoon, heirloom tomato schnitzel, chicken cordon bleu. Perhaps where Olmsted rang superior was their preparation of sauces, especially the sauces for the dry rubbed scallops (rustic charred corn with slight tartness from blueberries) and chicken dish (a rich green sauce with flavors reminiscent of peas). I appreciate the chef's effort incorporating a culturally diverse set of ingredients to the menu.

I would only return here for drinks or dessert in the backyard, but I question paying $20 for s'mores made with Hershey's chocolate :P. If Olmsted is going for the nostalgia factor, I don't quite recall paying $20 for Hershey's.

My expectation was sky high the moment I walked into Olmsted.  With James Beard award for the best new restaurant and raving reviews on Eater. I expect the best, and Olmsted does not disappoint.  I liked the vibe, the coziness, the back patio with string lights a bathtub koi pond, all the details of the decor really make the restaurant pop and be as inviting as it can be.  Food was amazing - The fried crab rangoon was a stand out, along with the clam carrot crepe and the grilled pork belly were my favorites.  We ordered a burgundy red ($100) that was pretty good value and paired well with the food.  

Highly recommend

We often dine at Olmsted because we love the food.  Last night we had the most amazing server, Miriam.  She was amazingly helpful in guiding us through the menu and checked back periodically throughout the meal.  I am not sure we have ever had such a great server anywhere. Thank you Olmsted for the food, and making a great decision to hire such a stand out person.

After hearing all the raves and having difficulty getting a reservation, I was excited to try this buzzy place in the 'hood. The first half of the evening was delicious and unusual, though the portions were small, salty, and not very easy to share, as was recommended. We much enjoyed shisitos with bottarga, lobster chips with hot veg dip, watermelon slices wrapped in fluke, and grilled tuna with basil leaves. The only miss was the scallops, served on two plates, one with a petite skewer of shellfish, the other with accompanying dollops of corn kernels and sugary blueberry sauce, which tasted as confusing as it sounds. Each item delivered to our table was accompanied by fresh place settings, somewhat annoying, since the servers ceremoniously removed essentially clean plates and cutlery and replaced them every few minutes. Perhaps the washing of so many dishes and utensils contributed to the unnecessarily high cost of the meal.

Things got worse when we were asked to retire to the garden for dessert. We tried to carry our beverages with us, but were sternly told to leave them behind by a new server, who assured us replacements awaited outside. They didn't. The outdoors set up was awkward. We were seated on hard benches without backs across a narrow path from the little platform where our dessert and coffee were set. As a result, it was a long reach to get to our dessert, while servers and other patrons kept walking the path between us and the platform, interrupting our conversation and our enjoyment of the sweets. Towering Jerusalem artichoke plants teetered menacingly over our shoulders. Our displeasure must have been noticable because the outdoor servers tried conspicuously to ignore us as they passed to and fro between us and our food. The chocolate mousse was tasty and the portion large, which kept us from leaving hungry. But it was served in two heavy bowls, one for the mousse and one for the vanilla creme topping, which were hard to juggle while reaching across the busy path. And make-it-yourself s'mores for $20? Please!

Short cut; lovely place, bright, & friendly staff, with expensive, unremarkably tasting food but real hi end presentation. 

They recommend ordering 4 - 5 plates for 2. We did. Even though I try not eat things I dont love (why waste the calories) my nephew is 19 with the appetite and metabolism of a line backer(read eats ALOT of anything) so I was sure we would order more. We did not. It was just too much mediocre food. We had the Duck Pate - sweet and fluffy a very weird texture for pate, I did not like it. My nephew liked but didn't finish it. The Waffle - came with a scoop of ice cream, and some very tasty fruit across the top. When served they pour the syrup immediately over,  not enough I found myself hunting for it and suddenly could not get the attention of anyone to bring me a little more. We were at the bar. He demolished this! The Duck Eggs with Bangers - meh. Didn't finish. He didnt like the eggs, I thought they were over cooked and missing salt. There was a homemade loaf which was really more like a muffin that I thought was good. He was unimpressed. The drinks both non & alcoholic were very small and took a ridiculous amount of time to get considering they were mostly premade ( and we were at the bar!).
Staff: The staff was bright & friendly but drinks and plates came out without regard.  We waited, while a couple whom sat & ordered well after us got an Egg Dish we had ordered as well. This happened several times but it may be because we never finished anything.  Brunch for my nephew and I with tip came to $120. Almost everything was just lackluster in taste but lovely eye candy. Maybe this is what English food taste like. (No offense to English Food )

Food was excellent and the service overall was great. I would particularly like to thank Derek for going above and beyond. We visited on the evening of Saturday 10/5. He was working on the back patio and was not our designated server (she was excellent too). We brought our two year old with us to dinner and when she started to get antsy, he saved the day twice. First with a flower and some fish food when we took a walk out back. A second time later in dinner when he made crayons and a sheet to color on magically appear when she was starting to get upset. Thoughtful, supportive staff throughout the whole place.

Really good. Although nothing I ate blew me away, so that's why it was 4 stars instead of 5. We enjoyed 4 dishes, kale crab ragoon, some lamb appetizer, and scallops and duck for dinner. Everything was very good, although the lamb appetizer was just ok. I also enjoyed a really good whiskey drink with black walnut, I think it may have been called the Lavender. The service was also fairly poor, which was weird because it seemed like a lot of staff around, but I ended up not trying a second drink because no one ever came by, which was odd. The lady pouring the wine in particular seemed to be joking around a lot, which seemed very unprofessional. Not sure why this place has a month long wait for reservations, it's good but not a month long wait good.

This is not your random night out. It's expensive and I swear anytime a place even has the illusion of "Michelin star" being echoed around it, the size of the dishes shrink more and more. I'm not one who needs to pay $20+ for maple truffle smoke essence and one slice of mushroom on a plate. I am exaggerating, but I k ow I was in for it when the server greeted us and said "everything is meant to be shared, I would suggest each of you pick 3 or so things you like". Mind you, each plate runs from $12-24! And if you have a cocktail, add another $15 per. The food was.. good. Will I come back? Probably not. And how dare you charge $20 for my beloved s'mores. If you wanna be fancy for one night, go, get ready to pay a lot, and maybe get a slice of pizza after.

Olmsted is my favorite restaurant in all of New York City. And if you even just look at my review count, you can see I eat out a lot in New York City. 

This spot in Brooklyn is absolute magic. While you wait for your table, you can sit in the cozy back patio where they have blankets to bundle in if it's cold. 

The reason I like this place is because every single item is incredible. There may be some single dishes I like better at other places, but for a complete meal where every dish made me go WOW, this is it. 

The lobster dip thing is a great little app, and the carrot crepe is absolutely to die for. Clams, carrot crepe, and citrus make it for a rare and incredibly flavorful combo. The duck is also delicious. I've been a few times and really everything is good. 

I've unfortunately never made it in time for s'mores here, which you can cook in the back. I think you have to order it by like 8:30 or something to do it, and I'm always still on dinner then. But, the lavender yogurt is outstanding and a wonderful dessert. 

Oh, also, they have cutie little chickens in the back! Olmsted is an absolute MUST.

The best farm-to-table dining experience in Brooklyn. Truly delicious, innovative dishes served in a comfortable, inviting dining room by warm, welcoming, knowledgeable and efficient staff. The standard of cooking is very high and very consistent. Great every time.

Excellent dinner spot!!! We had the squash rings (delicious), trumpet mushrooms (YUM), summer squash som tum (very unique), rutabaga tagliatelle (sooo good!!!) and the duck (also very tasty). Only issue I had with the duck is it was very hard to cut through the fat, so maybe a sharper knife would have been useful. The frozen yogurt was insane !!!! Definitely order that. Such a wonderful place, I highly recommend it.

The food was good but didn't wow me. Underscore "good", not remarkable. While a lovely spot for a Brooklyn meal (cozy atmosphere, bright light, friendly staff), there's too many other options for an interesting, creative, farm to table meal in the area for this to be a top contender.

I really wanted to like Olmsted, but the whole experience fell flat for me. My friends and I were visiting NYC for a weekend and made a brunch reservation months in advance anticipating a great meal. It's hard not to be excited after reading so many favorable reviews. The restaurant space is pretty amazing with tons of charm and a beautiful outdoor patio and garden. However, the food and service left more to be desired. 

We ordered six dishes from their brunch menu, including the potato latke, the grilled breakfast burger, duck duo, coddled eggs, and waffle a la mode. The latke was definitely tasty, but aside from that, the other dishes were underwhelming. The coddled eggs were particularly disappointing and had an off-putting flavor that I couldn't quite figure out. 

Service was also a bit disappointing. We had to wave down waiters a few times to refill our water glasses and for a set of missing utensils. It also took about 15 minutes just to get the check, which was a bit frustrating given our group's tight schedule. Maybe dinner is a much better experience but brunch was not great for me.

Perfect experience every time! Very creative, thoughtful, and delicious food. Welcoming and warm atmosphere. Attentive and friendly service. So yes if you are wondering - go for brunch! Go for dinner! They even have a magical garden in the back where you can admire all the botany and sparkly lights from any of the various cozy seating nooks and from where you can dine or just have drinks/dessert.

Small place, good ambiance, our go to place when in Brooklyn. The menu is small, delicious and interesting. Cocktails are well prepared and I really like the wine list. Patio out back is a good place to have a drink while waiting for your table. Go, relax and enjoy

The service was fantastic, we loved our waiter.  We had 6 dishes in the dining room, all of them were beatiful.  But - the flavor was very subdued in every dish, nothing wowed us.  We had dessert smores in the backyard, and that was lovely, the backyard area is spacious and cute.  I'd go back to try it again next time they change the menu.
One of the better meals I've had recently, the egg rolls and breakfast burger are a must.

Enh. I had eaten dinner here before and remembered it being good. I recently received an email about a post-Thanksgiving pre-fixe brunch they were offering this weekend. It was expensive, $75/person, but I thought it would be a nice final meal with visiting family and made a reservation. 
We arrived about 10 min before our reservation but they turned us away at the door because they hadn't opened yet and told us to wait outside. It was just over 30 degrees out.
When we came back they sat us right by the front window despite the rest of the restaurant being empty. We mentioned that it was cold up there, but they said they were going to turn on the heat but it never warmed up.
Included were four courses - a small loaf of bread to start, then egg/cheese/bacon (or no bacon for veg) eggrolls and a salad, then what they called Shukshuka but really was green beans in a cast iron with a poached egg, then a very sweet waffle. 
You had to share things (bc family style) but they offered no serving pieces, you had to keep using your own silverware and serve yourselves onto your tiny plates.
I asked if they could do a bloody mary without worcestershire, nope (not so uncommon that it's in a pre-made mix but some places will still make you a drink from scratch). 
I know poached eggs are usually runny but the ones on our "Shakshuka" were actually raw. We said something and the waiter took it back, then everyone in the kitchen huddled together and stared at us. They brought us another one with overcooked eggs. 
At the end of the meal, we asked for Decaf, which they didn't have and no other hot drink was offered as an option until we asked about Decaf tea.
The food was very mediocre, not as innovative/unique as I remembered, and the service was really flat. At one point they did come to wipe the table, but only cleaned about a third of what had fallen off the bread tray or from us serving ourselves.
Just overall a pretty disappointing ripoff, especially considering it was more $$$ than an amazing dinner with two drinks each, 2 appetizers, 2 entrees, and a shared glass of wine and dessert at a great restaurant in W'burg earlier in the week.

OMG we had the most mediocre post-thanksgiving day brunch here. $75 for a pre-fixe family style menu. That's $150 for a 5-inch piece of cornbread (to share), a small radicchio salad (to share), 1 small cast iron pan with runny eggs and string beans, 2 fried egg rolls, and a large waffle for dessert that was probably the most filling item, except for $150 we did not expect to be left most filled by the waffle (we were still hungry at the end of the meal even after the waffle). The meal was edible but a complete rip off. I lost my taste for it shortly after I realized we were being ripped off just as the tiny egg rolls arrived. I wanted to try what they had to offer but felt forced to eat what it seemed they felt like making that morning. Seems like this place takes themselves way too seriously if they think what they served this past Friday was worthy of such a high tab!

If you could have brunch in a pristine forest where you dig up custom made wood and pottery utensils and have fresh ingredients and perfectly crafted dishes and still see a hint of creative flair in the presentation of the food ... why wouldn't you?

SO disappointing after hearing such great things about this place.

Food was meh.  We were surrounded by a swarm of fruit flies coming from the plants above us inside the restaurant.  Wait staff efficient but almost arrogant about how great the food was (it really wasn't).  For small plates, Freeks Mill and The Farm On Adderley both outshines this place by far.  Would NOT go there again.  A total waste of money.

I had been wanting to dine at Olmsted for two years and was so excited when I finally made the reservation. Sadly, my guests and I left disappointed, underwhelmed and hungry. The ambiance and service are nice. The creativity and concept are there. However, the execution, food, and flavor are completely underwhelming. I truly wanted to love each dish and when disappointed with the first, brushed it off and said the next will be better. I found myself at the end of the meal with no silver lining, a lingering appetite, and a $200 bill. We shared seven dishes for three people. The lobster starter was a centimeter of liquid and two centimeters of foam in a small cup with airy, crispy chips. The lobster flavor was indiscriminate. The squash were good enough but really only five slices of delicata squash. The beef tartare completely lacked flavor and textures did not come together well. The pierogis were good but not memorable, and just as good as any fried dumpling. The carrot crepe was probably the most disappointing. It was delicate and pretentious- almost insulting to call it a crepe. Again, we are open to creativity and invention but the flavor must be there and it just wasn't. We actually are light eaters, and did not go in expecting hearty steaks. We did expect flavor and being fed well though. After five small (very small) beginning plates, I still had hope for the two entrees. The scallops were inconsistently cooked- two soft without searing and three burnt/blackened (a burnt flavor not a delicious scallop sear). The rutabaga tagliatelle was okay but again needed much more flavor! I really wanted something to wow me, or at least hit the mark!
