I wanted to feel good about spending $200 and sadly couldn't justify it. I want to note that the service was good, ambiance nice, and cocktails great. However, I just can't understand how Olmsted is so highly recommended and rated for the food. Maybe it is because of our Instagram era and the slight whimsy and gimmick of it all, but even that isn't pushed forward enough at Olmsted to make this dinner memorable. Although still hungry and craving a win from Olmsted, we lost hope by the end to opt for dessert and left to go get dessert elsewhere. Ah well.

I've been wanting to go here since they opened and after having my plans thwarted multiple times, we finally made it for brunch. If we lived nearby, we'd always be here. I wasn't a huge fan of the gravlax, but did love that they could do almost everything gluten free. The GF squash bread was amazing, especially with the butter and jam, served hot. My friends loved the donuts. The Vietnamese pizza was also a hit. The mushrooms were outstanding. The kathi roll was interesting, but we were stuffed by the time we got it. And I don't know that I'd order it again. I'll definitely be back to try dinner.

We celebrated two birthdays among the six of us at this attractive "hole in the wall".  There are only seats for 50, and one table for more than four.  There is a limited, but unique menu since much of their food is grown and farmed out in back.  I live two blocks from this place and wanted to find out why we had to book one month in advance for a Saturday 5:30 pm reservation.  We went and found out:

Most are outstanding small plates with a few larger entrees.  

Here is the entire menu except for the three deserts

SNACKS
Chicken Fried Trumpet Mushrooms
Beer Battered Delicata Squash Rings
Lobster "Thermidor"
Duck Liver Mousse

PLATES
Sweet Potato & Uni Pierogies Sauerkraut, Sour Cream
Radicchio Wedge SaladBlue Cheese Dressing, Bacon Bits
Beef Tartare Roasted Heirloom Pumpkin, Nutmeg Hollandaise
Carrot Crepe Little Neck Clams, Sunflower

LARGER PLATES
Rutabaga "Tagliatelle"Burgundy Black Truffle, Brown Butter 
Grilled ScallopsWinter Slaw, Spicy Peanuts, XO Sauce
Duck Breast & Leg MortadellaHakurei Turnips, Lentils
Heritage PorkReading Raclette, Broccoli Rabe, Mustard Jus

Among the six of us, we ended up with dining on each of the above items except for the Duck Liver Mousse and the Beef Tartare.  Snacks and plates are meant to be shared.

 Don't go there in a rush.  Dining here is an experience.  Between the courses and drinks we were here almost three hours.  Food came out at a good pace despite their warning of a small kitchen.  As busy as they were, we were never rushed.  Our waiter Alex was very attentive and carefully answered all questions.

We now know why this place is so popular.  Definite thumbs up!

After a 2 hour wait, we (party of 3) were seated and essentially ordered the entire menu which left us sattisfied but definitely not full. Each plate served family style and meant for sharing  (3-4  plates pp was recommended to us, hence why we ordered everything) felt like it was trying really really really hard to be creative and ultimately came up short every time. The salad was bitter, the"pork" just a honey baked ham topped with a green veggie medley and the duck dry. There is so much hype surrounding this place (and we even spotted a celebrity at the table behind us) but ultimately i don't think it lives up to its MICHELIN recognition. I'll come back for a drink in the summer to enjoy the adorable backyard but beyond that I'll pass. I have been excited to try this place given all its attention but at least for me it didn't do it. 
Other comments: hostess was less than welcoming and bar only seats a party of 2 max. Also definitely make a reservation. Not great for groups, nor for kids.

Cute place that I've been wanting to try for a long time and we finally made it over for a brunch during a very snowy day. The service was fine and the restaurant has a spacious garden in the back that was extra cute cause of the snow fall. There were some yummy dishes from the many that we ordered, my favorite being the house gravlax for the starter and Vietnamese pizza from the main. The yogurt was underwhelming and potato latke was super burnt on the outside. Carrot Kati roll was good and the waffles were yummy but the server poured too much syrup on it even though it came on the side. I would love to try their dinner one day.

This place is perfect. There were an abundance of vegetarian options. The rutabaga ribbons with truffles, radicchio wedge and chicken fried mushrooms were some of the best things I've ever eaten. The frozen yogurt was a perfect end to the meal.

I'll get straight to it - this is my favorite restaurant in NYC. The food is always creative and delicious, the drinks are excellent, the service is great. You get all the benefits of a bougie dinner without feeling stuffy or awkwardly fancy.

Really wanted to love it. New to the neighborhood and spontaneously dropped in late on a weeknight. Lovely space, music not too loud, attentive service. Ordered the heritage pork which seemed salty and turns out it was brined, which was unexpected. A few measly pieces of broccoli rabe as accompaniment, left hungry. Underwhelmed by the food; will try again for brunch.

Dined during the second seating (2pm) of Saturday brunch to celebrate my husband's birthday. It was the first time we brought our 2-month old infant out for a semi-spencey ($$$) meal. I was originally nervous about how we would be received, since some of the trendy spots tend to turn their noses up at babies & families dining out during busy periods. But every aspect of the experience was made sweeter by the entire staff. 

Service was exceptional! Each touch-point was flawless. From the hostess who seated us helping to put our stroller away...to the runners, servers and the manager checking in on us, to ensure that our meal and drink selections were to our liking. 

Everyone seemed to understand that being out with a small baby is a large enough feat, and genuinely wanted us to enjoy every bit of our experience.

Thank you Olmsted. We'll be back!

Eh. After having Olmsted on my NYC dinner list for months, I finally had the chance to go for a weeknight dinner with a friend. Admittedly I came in with high expectations given reviews from others, but while the food was unique and tasty, the experience didn't merit the hype that this place has garnered over the years.

We walked in through a confusing curtain to claim our reservation and were seated at the bar immediately, giving us a perfect view of all of the action in the kitchen. We ordered drinks and split a bunch of dishes and ate them all as they came out, with the total for 2 drinks, 3 starters, 2 mains and 1 dessert coming out to around $80pp, which is a bit steep.

Food:
(4/5) Squash rings - Spiced to perfection but the squash flavor didn't come through, and ended up a little too oily for my taste

(4/5) Carrot crepe - highly recommended but not super memorable to me, was a bit too liquidy for my taste and wasn't really much of a "crepe" at all. The carrot flavor was still very present though.

(5/5) Beet salad - super unique texture and the presentation was lovely! Looks like an explosion in a bowl. Enjoyed the crunchiness of the sweet beets combined with the saltiness of the cheese

(3/5) Tagliatelle - definitely the most puzzling dish of the night; upon first bite I thought it tasted more like cabbage than pasta, and the butter was overwhelming to the point of dripping all over my plate

(3.5/5) Pork belly - Well cooked but portioned a bit too small and nothing special, tasted like most other pork belly I've had.

(5/5) Dessert donuts - Delicious end to the meal with ice cream that complemented the hot donuts very well. 

Drinks:
Lavender (3/5) - Not too different from a regular Manhattan. 

Rosemary (5/5) - A must-get cocktail! Loved the flavors of mezcal and the black salt that was set around the rim. A great addition to the meal.

Overall I'd still recommend checking it out, but there are definitely better restaurants for the price.

Wonderful cocktails and outstanding food! The service we had seated at the bar was excellent. I can't remember the name of our server now--she works primarily on the weekends--but she kind of looks like Anne Hathaway and made a lovely old fashioned for me! We will return to try more of their menu

Items we ordered:

-Soba cocktail - excellent

-Chicken fried trumpet mushroom - excellent

-Squash rings - good

-Carrot crepe little neck clams - interesting concept, excellent clams

-Black truffle and brown butter rutabaga "tagliatelle" - Amazinggg flavor and perfectly seasoned! Hope they will recreate this with pasta tagliatelle in the future!!!! Chewy Al dente pasta with that sauce would be divine.

-Smoked pork tenderloin - excellent

-LI duck with fried morning glory salad - the flavors are definitely good, but a bit salty and heavy on the lemongrass / fish sauce. The dish is great but you have to really enjoy strong Thai flavors. This was my least favorite.

Overall the food + service were excellent!

Customer service and quality of food- my top two determining factors when rating a restaurant.

I came here for the Valentine's Day prefix dinner with my partner for $125 PER PERSON (not including drinks, gratuity or tax).

The customer service was AMAZING. Honestly, above and beyond. They also gave us two complimentary bottles of sparkling water.

Now, for the food.
$250 for JUST a tasting menu was a little on the steep side- but I understand.

The tasting menu included:
-Oysters (delicious, but 4 small oysters)
-Lobster Thermidor (very small)
-Kale and crab Rangoon (amazing)
-Shaved beet salad (amazing)
-Mushroom stroganoff (amazing)
-Rye bread with honey butter (amazing)
-Scallops (cooked PERFECTLY. Debatably the best scallops I've had to date)
-I had the Long Island Duck with a side of something (the side I had was to DIE for. The duck was bland, unseasoned and not memorable. Kind of disappointing)
-My parter had the rutabega tagliatelle (wasn't good AT ALL but E for effort)
-for dessert, the raspberry jam and milk ice cream sundae cream puff with caramelized white chocolate (OMG! To die for)

I left full and delighted. The food exceeded my expectations.

I'd be back.

A beautiful space with great service. Brunch menu is ok. Nothing particularly captured us on the page, but we settled on the duck liver mousse (phenomenal), the potato latke (lackluster), and the burger (ok, too much sauce and didn't come out at the temperature we requested). We had the drip coffee (watered down and a bit sour), fresh squeezed OJ (yum yum), and the carrot OJ mimosa (ok). Overall, not what I expected considering how much I've heard about this place.

Olmsted is one of my favorite restaurants in Brooklyn! I have been here for brunch and dinner. Both meals were fantastic. This time for brunch, my friend and I ordered the duck liver mousse, BEC egg rolls, duck duo, potato latke, and the donuts for dessert. We loved everything but would have gone without the egg rolls. Our server was extremely nice and took the egg rolls off of our check. We weren't expecting that when she asked what we thought of them. She suggested that we get them initially so I guess she felt bad that we didn't like it.

I came here for an early dinner with my mom prior to a concert at Barclays. I made the reservation a month in advance and was able to get seats at the bar which were great! We ordered the fried delicata squash rings, the rye bread loaf, the king crab rangoons, beet salad, rutabaga pasta and the heritage pork which ended up being the perfect amount of food for two hungry diners.

As the dishes arrived, one was truly better than the next. The beet salad was a nice fresh & crunch break from the heavier (fried & carb) items. I was actually blown away by the rutabaga and could not believe I was eating a vegetable. My favorite was the king crab and kale rangoons which were just so perfectly stuffed and came steaming hot!

I will definitely be back here but just note that you really do need a reservation! Also theres a very sweet garden in the back where you can get drinks and bites and smores!

Olmsted is the MVP of restaurants in New York. Chef Baxtrom, who trained under two of the most highly regarded names in the business, serves up some of the most flavorful, creative food I've ever enjoyed, regardless of price point. But his ability to do this without having a single item on the menu above 24 dollars is simply remarkable. Furthermore, the lack of high priced options and pretentiousness makes Olmsted extremely comfortable for a relaxed meal any day of the week. Three of their dishes from my most recent experience at Olmsted stand out: delicious squash rings served on an actual tree - of sorts; extremely basic crab rangoon, with a very simply but equisite spin, served humbly, and for fun in a Chinese take-out container no less; and the most delicious duck dish - served two ways, both incredible - that I've ever encountered in my life. Beyond this, the service is superb, stacked with serious foodies who will happily offer their honest opinions. The drink menu is outstanding, with simply labeled cocktails disguising brilliant subtlety. And the atmosphere is as good as it gets, feeling like you're eating in the chef's garden; and that's before you go out into the actual back garden of the restaurant, where you can roast smores, keeping warm under blankets on a cold winter's night. Olmsted is simply amazing, and easily one of my 3 favorite restaurants in the world.

Olmsted has been on my hit list for the longest while yet, but its far-flung location and oft-fully booked status made it hard for me to come here. Yet I finally did, and boy, was it worth the wait! 

The menu is tight and concise, but just about everything I had was top notch. That is my favorite kind of menu. Because I came in the winter, a lot of root vegetables were featured and celebrated. I don't think I have had vegetables so transformed yet held so true to its essence. Someone who hates vegetables would probably be a convert after an Olmsted meal.

My favorite dish was probably the rutabaga tagliatelle - ribbons of rutabaga were shaved and tossed in a browned butter cream sauce. The same amount of pasta probably would have felt too heavy, but because it was rutabaga, it was very more-ish. The rutabaga felt like a slightly crunchy yet al dente pasta - it worked pefectly against the savory sauce. 

Likewise with the shaved beet salad - again, that ribbony yet crunchy texture juxtaposed very well with toasted hazelnuts and crumbly blue cheese.

The carrot crepe with mussels seems to be a menu staple. It was tasty, but reminded me very much of the carrots and clam dish at Crown Shy. It's hard to say who copied who. The carrot crepe here was slightly unwieldy, but I certainly soaked up every last bit of that flavorful sauce with the rye sourdough.

Oh, the rye sourdough. Warm, fluffy, full of the toasty earthy and slightly spicy/herbal notes that accompany rye - it was very delicious and worth the extra $6 it cost.

Lastly, I got the duck two ways - there was duck lard tossed among deep fried spinach, and duck breast. The duck breast was cooked to medium-rare perfection. The duck lard crispies was tasty, but the entire dish felt a bit too salty and I wish I had saved my bread to balance out this dish.

The meal was rounded off with a complimentary apple cider jelly candy - it tasted like fall in a gelatin (or agar!) cube.

I'm looking forward to coming to Olmsted in the spring/summer and see how else they might revere vegetables!

We visited Olmsted some weeks back. The overall experience was very uneven. The execution of the food really didn't rise above 3.5 stars for me, the creativity was also underwhelming considering the chefs resume. The service and overall vibe was great, elevating the experience.
On to the individual dishes, the first thing we got was lobster "thermidor" which is like those prawn crackers with a cheesy dip. It was pretty good, but the ratio was off. A lot more crackers were needed to finish the dip.
Chicken fried trumpet mushroom. This one was a miss. The batter was not fried enough, dense and not at all crisp. 
Duck liver mousse. Good, as most liver mousse are. Not much one can mess up and they didn't.
Carrot Crepe. This is a really interesting dish. There's one bite I had that was just the right ratio of everything that is simply amazing. But I didn't manage to replicate it again for the rest of the course. The beautiful presentation may have made it difficult to appreciate.
Beef tartare. I have increasingly starting to favor lean meat as tartare, this was too fatty and too traditional for me. But that's personal preference.
Rutabaga "tagliatelle". Another miss for me. Under-seasoned and more butter than necessary, this could be great but the execution let it down.
Heritage pork. This was an amazing dish, everything was on point, from seasoning to texture. 
Duck breast and leg mortadella. Another great dish, the mortadella was just about the best duck based dish I had in quite some time, perfect in every way.
Frozen yogurt with lavender honey. Amazing dessert, but a little less honey would be better as it is too sweet for us in the current form.
Chocolate mousse. Great dessert as well, though this one needed more creme fraiche.
Overall still a very positive experience, the missteps seems to have been due to an off night. I'll definitely be back again.

Olmsted is a hidden gem tucked away in Brooklyn. The food here is excellent. 

The garden outside is great for a cocktail or desert, yet the seating is not ideal for more than two people, as it lines the perimeter of the garden with fixed mini tables.

Seconding another reviewer -- Olmsted's current "camp-themed" menu is awful and incredibly disappointing. Having dined here a year ago, it was difficult to believe this was even the same restaurant. The fried chicken was dry and flavorless. The crab claws were disgusting; clearly frozen for an extended period of time. I understand that this is a very difficult time for restaurants, and by no means do I want to detract from the need to support their business. That said, I would highly recommend avoiding Olmsted's outdoor dining option at all costs and supporting them instead through their trading post.

I have been wanting to dine at Olmsted for quite awhile and was lucky enough to snag a reservation a couple weeks ago.The food, atmosphere and service were fantastic! As a former hospitality worker, I've also been extremely impressed with how involved Olmsted has been with helping out the community and navigating different avenues to keep their employees hired during the pandemic. Olmsted is a great restaurant, with caring owners and I would highly recommend dining there to anyone.

I really wanted to love this place but it disappointed. Hopefully if I come back again, the menu and experience would be different post-COVID. 

First, I know they are trying their best with outdoor seating but the umbrellas did not do anything in the hot and humid weather. It was difficult to be comfortable and be with your company with the sun blocking everything. It also would have been nice to be have a choice in being able to reserve the back garden. The bathroom was great and so was the little market. In general, the staff was really friendly and took covid precautions to heart. 

Main Takeaway of the food and drinks was that it was underwhelming on all fronts. Some of the portions were too small for the price, and the flavor was a little off for everything. I know the menu is different than normal so maybe I came on an off day. 

For 4 people, we ordered:
-Vesper Martini (Gordon's Gin, Vodka, Kina, Lillet Blanc) - $12
-Ginger Fizz (White Rum, Domaine de Canton, Honey, Lemon, Soda) - $12
-Honey Suckle (Barr Hill Gin, Salers, Cocchi Americano, Kina) - $14
*The drinks overall were good but nothing too special. The presentation was what made it stick out.

-Red Little Gem Lettuce ($9): to be honest, it was too small and boring to be so expensive. It was glorified lettuce in a bowl with ranch on the side. 
-all the summer salad ($14): again the portion was really small for the price. The flavor as better here and a little refreshing. I loved the presentation and colors.
-tonkatsu spareribs (full rack -$30): I liked the smokiness and the meat came right off the bones but it was wayyy too salty. We couldn't even eat half.
-stone crab claw boil ($28): my favorite dish of the whole meal. The flavor was old bay seasoning, and everything was cooked well. It was a little difficult to get the crab meat out.
-wagyu beef corn dog ($16):  the corn bread was great. I would recommend getting that just as a side. The sauces on it were also great. You can't tell that the frank is wagyu beef though.

We were so excited about our meal at Olmstead and we were so very disappointed with the food.  We pretty much ordered everything on the menu and everything was so incredibly over seasoned.  The little gem salad is awkwardly presented and difficult to share.  The fried chicken is all batter and dry.  The crab boils had way to much old bay seasoning.  I love old bay, but couldn't even taste the crab it was so seasoned.  The Tonkatsu ribs were so salty, I could not detect any tonkatsu flavor... just salt. I couldn't even down one.

The BLT was good, it was deconstructed and the tomatoes were quite fresh.  The service was very good and the slushies were amazing.  Perhaps I would return for drinks, but definitely not for food.

Super cute concept right now for summer called "summer camp." Arrived at Olmsted on a Saturday evening and was early for our 5:00pm reservation so headed into the trading post to look around. Saw others stop by to pick up their loaf of sourdough, some fresh produce and berries and just seemed like a popular place for locals to pick up great ingredients for home. I got a jar of apricot jam and a chocolate chip cookie! The cookie was $6 and Jam was $12 which is definitely pricey but I think that's what you should expect from things in the area and everything seemed very homemade or from farm to table sort of thing. Cookie was very good and have yet to try the jam! 

We checked in at the front with a "counselor" and was brought back through the trading post to the garden. It seems it was split into two with one side full of tables and the other is their classic bench garden for walk-ins. We got seated at a super cute little table and I'm glad we made a reservation because it sure would be hard to eat on a bench. The only issue I had with sitting out in the garden was MOSQUITOS! I'm very prone to bites and had a dozen by the time I left. For others who relate, you can definitely book a seat out front on the sidewalk seating!

Our waiter was very friendly and we got started with some drinks. The menu can be accessed by the QR code on every table. I got the honeysuckle which was a gin drink. Very good, and subtle I loved it. Boyfriend got the husk which was a whiskey drink. It was super citrusy which I love and very refreshing. 

As for food, we went with the 5 piece fried chicken, 1/2 rack tonkatsu ribs and the wagyu corn dog. We also chose the truffle honey butter to go with the chicken. Our food arrived quickly and the fried chicken was hands down our favorite. Super juicy, crispy, and the truffle honey butter really was a great choice. The chicken came with some of their whole kirby bread and butter pickles. WOW I don't even like pickles like that but this was amazing so good and paired so well with the chicken! The wagyu beef corn dog was honestly my least favorite item. Could've gone with a salad instead of it. It was a lot of meat so that was good but as I expected, I couldn't really tell the quality difference with the wagyu. To us, it seemed very very normal. The 1/2 rack ribs was larger than we thought and honestly very delicious! Tonkatsu tasted like a sweeter version of bbq so ribs were sweet and smoky. We enjoyed it. 

Overall, good experience (minus the mosquitos; do wish they would place some outdoor fans to create airflow to shoo away the mosquitos or have bug lamps that prevent them for the customers dining outside. This would make outdoor dining 100x better. I saw some other customers slap mosquitos away too). Food was good and definitely pairs well with their drinks. I love the concept of their trading post and they sell the truffle honey butter so that's a plus! Wish they sold the pickles because I would buy a whole jar. It's definitely a bit pricey but we were glad we gave this place a try after seeing their video on YouTube and their generosity during the worst of COVID. I hope to come back and try their other dishes especially new ones that may come up during seasonal rotation!

Don't go! Food was mediocre at best. New menu very disappointing. Make a fresh salad at home go to a dozen other places in the neighborhood. This place has become a joke. NYTimes gave if a bad review with good reason. So disappointing and expensive!!!

I recently went to Olmsted with some friends for dinner in their backyard. They modified their menu because of COVID to feature a bunch of new options and to reflect a backyard bbq picnic vibe. I was nervous to eat here since I am vegan, but was pleasantly surprised that they had many options they could make/modify for me. They even had veganise to accompany the build your own BLT dish. I highly recommend you check Olmsted out for some delicious food and great drinks!

We had such an amazing time here. The outdoor dining in the garden is so romantic. Even in the pouring rain. We shared the summer salad, the steak skewers, the fried chicken. You can't go wrong with anything you order here and I look forward to coming back when they have their full menu. The wait staff is superb and gracious. The little store in front is adorable. Can't wait to come back. I can't thank you guys enough for the plastic bags to put over my white shoes in the torrential downpour! We had a blast xoxo!

Phew! Shout out to Frederick Law who would be honored to have this restaurant named after him. I have been wanting to go to Olmsted for a while and I finally got a reservation....on March 18, 2020. So due to COVID, I couldn't go but finally made it. I was nervous that the food was going to be expensive and not filling but I was WRONG!

Everything was delicious. The coleslaw was like blanched cabbage served cold with a delicious sauce (sorry to the amazing chefs for this probably horrible description), the salad was made with carrots and ricotta and CARROT BUTTER (????) and finally, the corn dog was delicious. It had a very crispy, very thin batter and I am team ketchup AND mustard so this did not disappoint. I can't get over how unique and delicious every single item on the menu was. I cannot wait to go back!

Also shout out to Ben who was a great server and was happy to answer our questions about the menu. 

As an FYI - the food comes out as it's ready, so if that isn't your thing, you might want to ask for the food to come out at the same time. Thankfully the three of us all got multiple items so we were pleasantly snacking away the entire time.

Olmsted has a lovely seasonal menu that incorporates interesting, fresh ingredients on a rotating basis. The food on the fall menu was phenomenal - from lighter fare like the fall salad, to more substantial dishes like the duck kofta and the smoked spare ribs. All of the food we tried had great flavors!

Bonus points for having a hot toddy available as the weather starts to get chilly in the evenings!
Worth the price! Yes, the reviews are true. DELIIIIIIICIOUS!! Staff is polite and efficient. Looking forward to going back here again!

The new fall menu is incredible. I thought I'd be disappointed without my favorite go-to dishes, but I was so wrong. The squash rings, duck kofta and spare ribs are amazing. Drinks were incredible as always.. we got the spiced pear and the pumpkin spice mai tai. 

Don't forget to check out the trading post after you eat! Get the duck liver mousse and some fresh bread to go.

I wouldn't be writing this review if the Olmsted staff had responded to my email concerning Covid-related hygiene and safety feedback, but given their lack of response, it is important for patrons to be aware.  Here is the feedback that I sent them, which sums up my experience.

"The food was absolutely delicious and the service was warm and inviting.  We had a lovely time in your garden setting.  

Given the impeccable "front office" experience, I was a bit surprised to get a glimpse into your kitchen, however.  Our table in the garden was right by the kitchen window.  When we were getting ready to leave, I looked in and saw that the two chefs working at the time were conversing while their masks were on their chins and one chef was eating off of the plate while he was preparing it.  Given the pandemic and all of the precautions that your restaurant has outlined on your site, I didn't think this was something that was in line with your standards and it made me feel very uncomfortable for having dined there.  

I do hope that this will be addressed through appropriate training, as I would like to enjoy the great food at Olmsted again."

I came with my friend who just delivered her son 4 weeks ago (in a mask during a pandemic). I was coming from Manhattan with my husband and 9 month old son and had to drop them off so I could park the car. They wouldn't seat my friend despite them asking and explaining the situation multiple times (my friend physically was in pain and would have felt more comfortable seated). Honestly, I thought their behavior was absolutely disgusting.

This restaurant is my go-to for a special meal. I always have to ask (or secretively Google) what the items on the menu are, but I have yet to be disappointed with the flavors and presentation. I highly recommend.

Had their Thanksgiving prefix last night at the outdoor back area, decor was beautiful but even though it was relatively warm for the season we still found it chilly, the closed section of the back area does not have any heaters on it so dining here when it gets colder is definitely out of the question. Service was fine, food was generally good (but to be honest my favorite course was the bread and butter), wine pairings were underwhelming but cocktails were good for the price. Lavender yogurt dessert was exceptional. They lose one star for sneaking in a Covid fee that they didn't tell us about in advance even though they had plenty of opportunities to (multiple confirmation e-mails, etc). I'm all for contributing and encouraging restaurants to stay in business, but adding a 10% charge at the last minute felt very shady. The meal was expensive enough, if you want to raise prices just raise prices.
Really delicious but one of the servers was a little snooty and was trying to rush us out which was uncomfortable. Otherwise the food is wonderful!

I had been wanting to try Olmsted as this place has received a lot of positive press. My overall score is 3.5, but I rounded down to 3 stars due to the 10% Covid charge, charging $8 for bread when not telling us about the additional charge, and the small portion sizes. The squash rings, bacon & brussel sprout pierogies, bread & butter and the smoked duck breast were the highlights of the thanksgiving pre-fix. Our meal was very pricey for the small amount of food that we received (over $200 per person). I'm glad that I tried this place, but it's not worth the hype.

Came for dinner in late November and sat in the garden out back, which was so neat! It was mostly open but also heated, so it wasn't too cold. My boyfriend and I ordered: 

+ Lavender bourbon cocktail
+ Spiced pear cocktail
+ Rye bread cocktail 
+ Pumpkin mai Tai - best cocktail I tried 
+ Hot Apple Pie a la Mode cocktail 
+ Delicata squash rings - best dish we ate
+ Kale & Crab Rangoons 
+ Fall Spiced Smoked Spare Ribs
+ Duck kofta
+ Fro-yo with whipped lavender honey 
+ Apple cider beignets - best dessert imo

Overall it was an amazing experience, so I'm adding a star!

I'm inclined to think I went to Olmsted during the worst time possible -- grabbed dinner in 20° weather in their partially covered backyard patio with minimal heating -- I've heard such, such great things about this place but I think the cold affected the whole experience.

Between two, for food: we ordered the Balmy Baked Bread w/ Maison Yaki's Green Yuzukōsho Butter, the Boiling Red Miso Chawanmushi, the Sizzling Grilled Scallop, Duck Duchesse, the Sweltering Julia Child's Beef Bourguignon and for drinks: we ordered a Spiced Pear and a Hot Toddy. All the foods were delicious but the duck and beef bourguignon dishes were underwhelming and I wouldn't order it again; the drinks did its job and kept us warm and slightly buzzed.

I really hate to be leaving a mediocre review during a pandemic but it just doesn't live up to its (former) hype. Would definitely love to give the place another try during the warmer months though!

Food was absolutely delicious and service was great. 

I loved the piping hot acorn squash soup - probably my favorite dish of the night. The only snag was that it was more gently warm than piping hot 

The fondue was incredibly tasty. For entrees we had the rutabaga pasta and Julia child's beef bourignone which just can't be beat

This spot has been on my list since moving to the area in July, but we haven't been able to secure a garden reservation until now. It was worth the wait 100p! I am one of those annoyingly picky eaters, always have been I am sorry, but every single thing on this menu blew me away. You get to build your own "perfect bite" for everything, which I greatly appreciate. Here's what we got:

Acorn Squash Soup -- this gem surprised me, we decided to get after hearing the table next to us rave about it and can confirm: it is delicious. It comes in a perfectly cooked squash shell and the coconut bubbles give it a slight Thai taste, the tiny pears are like an explosion in your mouth
Grilled Scallops -- don't even think about it, just order this immediately. Comes on a salt block where they continue to sexily sizzle and you can make your own radicchio wrap with slaw and XO sauce WOW I am drooling just thinking about it
Duck Duchesse -- this was a lot like shepherds pie but with duck (duh) and yummy smashed potatoes on top. Lots of flavor and very hearty for winter time

We also got the spiked hot chocolate, which comes with a camper canteen and you assemble yourself ('twas delicious, not too sweet and alcohol was perfectly balanced), then two hot cocktails: the sweet potato pie (Also not too sweet but otherwise as expected for something called sweet potato pie) and spiced pear (nice and light, a better version of apple cider).

Overall takeaway: go here. 

@Yelp, just confirming you can't leave 6 stars?

3.5 stars. I really liked the pickled yuzu butter and fresh bread - for me that was the highlight of the meal.

Acorn squash soup (sadly not pictured) was very creatively and delicately presented. I enjoyed scooping out the tender to squash to accompany the coconuty soup.

I thought the fondue was meh - a little bit one note, and the fries were not well thought out as a vehicle for dipping, as they were far too soft. I really would recommend serving with some type of bread-based items for dipping.

Overall good, bur pricey for the experience.

I really wanted to like this place, I had heard so much about it. The place looks really nice and service is great but the food was really not good. The Tempura were way too oily, the Mac and cheese was over cooked and unflavorful, the scallops were barely edible. the only good thing was the fondue which was literally just a cheese put in the oven... Even the fries seemed to be frozen fries. We paid over 200$ for two with two cocktails and I'm so disappointed in the experience. the products really don't taste fresh either.

Amazing dining! Acorn squash soup was excellent. Tempura broccoli rabe was good and crispy and perfectly fried. Tagliatelle was a fun surprise as we didn't realize it wasn't actual pasta but a root vegetable. I really enjoyed the sauce.  Scallops very good but sauce was a bit too spicy. Chocolate mousse was impressive. The Rosemary cocktail was great but the Rye bread was not for me but may be more enjoyable to whisky lovers. The outdoor backyard space was so quaint and comfortable to be in and the staff were incredibly helpful. A bit pricey but worth it!

Great meal! Great service! Incredible taste! Came here on a Wednesday for a late dinner at 9:30pm. I was blown away by the flavor combinations and wish I could've eaten more. Needless to say, I'll be back soon! 5star!

After the Covid lecture about how one must wear a mask except while eating, our party of 5 perused the menu. We had a couple of questions about some of the selections. The server told us that they usually recommend that with a party our size we order one of "everything" on the menu so each of us could get a couple of bites. While the lunch menu wasn't huge, that would cost approx. $250 not including drinks. We were told that each dish would be served as soon as it was prepared which would have been fine except for the very very long delay for 2 of the entrees. I'm not complaining about the food...it was memorable, creative, and delicious, but I felt the experience was a bit snooty and pretentious. Maybe a better place to take a date with whom you want to impress!

We just had a beautiful, delicious and decadent birthday dinner at olmstead! The food was beautifully presented and each dish looked like a piece of art. The backyard was gorgeous with lush greens and twinkly lights. We ate the crab Rangoon, som tum salad, spaetzle and carrot and scallop crepe. The carrot crepe was especially memorable with a luscious and sweet sauce. For dessert, don't miss the lavender honey frozen yogurt!

Staff was great so I am going to make the beginning point here that this is not really a negative review at all for the service.

Don't eat here.  

Lobster toasts are rice crackers with a seafood taste.

Liver mousse was half strawberry puree.

Fried asparagus was five pieces of battered asparagus. 

Radish salad was tart and weak.

Fried crab was small.  Thirty bucks.

I looked forward to this meal.  I wanted to like it.  I wanted to find the good thing to order.

Don't eat here.  I won't be back.

Wish I saw the review below because I have the same thoughts. 

Service was great - no complaints here, our server was so nice and very prompt. 

Food was pretty mediocre but overpriced. 

We ordered the fried asparagus which you only get 4 of not even 5. 

$20 for duck liver moussee with this weird whipped strawberry on top.

Crab rangoon was so mediocre. Felt weird about the chinese take out container and chopsticks it came in. 

The chef has some weird obsession with whipped purée foam on the food which was very not enjoyable and reminded me of soap. This was on both duck dishes. 

The duck confit was the best but again the ramp foam....

All of the above + 2 cocktails + 1 wine for $180. We were still hungry at the end.

We had an incredible meal at Olmsted tonight with wonderful service. Emma guided us through the menu expertly for both drinks and food, and everything we got (almost everything on the menu) was inventive and delicious. The music is great and the atmosphere overall was awesome. The s'mores outside in the garden was the cherry on top of a lovely dining experience!

Don't get it. Whole experience was so random and hodgepodge. Thought it was Farm to table? It's more like seafood dragged through the garden, weird. Service was pretentious from the hostess to the server.  Doesn't deserve the hype. Thank goodness for the taco food truck parked curbside in front of the restaurant.

I stopped in for some wine and a plate. I wasn't a fan of the wine that I had. I believe it was the la ginestra sant. It was way too tangy for me. 

I paired it with the Nashville's fried soft shell crab. Super creative dish. Perfectly crispy and the crab was tender and juicy. I found the fun to be a bit too nutty. I tasted some strong spices that over powered the crab. Nevertheless, it was a very creative dish and something I'd like to see on more menus.

Totally overpriced. Service was good but food was just "meh". Wagyu hotdog? I don't understand the point of it. Tasted like a regular corn dog to me. All of the dishes we got were nothing special and seemed quite pricey for what they were.

It's been 4 1/2 years since we came for dinner. This time we got to dine in the back garden (it's closed last time due to rain). The cocktails (lavender, rosemary and rhubarb) set us in the mood. Knowing that the portions tended to be small, we ordered all the snacks and plates (except the liver mousse eclairs) on the menu including double orders of corn bread and Crab Rangoon for six of us. The delicious corn bread with honey truffle butter was a crowd pleaser. The crab Rangoon served in a Chinese takeout container was tasty. We barely got a morsel of dainty carrot crepe and minuscule clams. Tiny samples of the other snacks/plates including yellow wax beans, spaetzle, squash som tum, and lobster crackers that came in quick succession, found nothing spectacular. Then there was a long interlude before the mains arrived  Of the entrees the roasted duck confit was superb: tender, juicy and flavorful. The scallops tasted very fresh. The tomato schnitzel would have been great if the crust/tomato could be crispier. The froyo dessert and shortcake were satisfactory. Our dinner spanned 2 1/2 hours. Good thing we came armed with bug repellent that made us impervious to becoming insect feast on this summer night. Pippa our server provided excellent service.

OMG they increased the prices 40-80% for most dishes. This is ridiculous. 16 dollars for bread??? Used to be $9. Kale and crab rangoon was $13 now $18. None of the plates 2 years ago even got close to hitting 30 dollars they were all 20-25. The spatzle dishes used to 15 now its 20. Carrot crepe was 13 now its 20. The frozen yogurt used to be 9 dollars now its 13. Covid inflation is real and very present in this restaurant because they choose to raise the prices to compensate but that's not great for the community. The community has been dedicated to going to to your restaurant and now you are robbing them. I'm glad I went here a lot when prices were reasonable. I won't be coming back ever until prices go back to what they were.
July 4 Sunday Brunch experience was perfect. Everything was delicious, great service, reasonably priced compared to other places. The burger is a must

Overall a really lovely meal and atmosphere. We loved the fried veggie and einkorn bread The duck pastrami was also really good, but I forgot to get a picture. The spatzle also good. The tomato schnitzel was okay, I wish it was crunchier but I think the wet tomato was working against the crunchy. Cocktails were also great. The fro-yo dessert is really original but it is A LOT of honey, you have to like honey.

Came for breakfast today. There was no wait however we were limited to the bar. Interior is beautiful and Trendy, beautiful garden in the back. Staff was pleasant and welcoming. We tried The matcha cocktail which was good but sweeter than expected. For entrees the burger was delicious juicy as it was half sausage and half beef patty topped with onions , cheese and This incredible sauce.  The eggs crab Benedict was okay , and interesting twist on traditional way as it's served.

I'm reviewing the 620 Loft and Garden rooftop event that Olmsted was hosting. I'm not sure how the restaurant itself is, so this was a separate event on its own. 

I made reservations for this event on Resy and was super excited for it. The seating area and arrangements were beautiful. We were welcomed with a non-alcoholic daiquiri (one of my favorite things of the night) and were seated promptly. This pre-fixe menu was listed on Resy as well which helped. 

When the food arrived, it looked great, however, it fell short on the taste. Our favorites were honestly the potato salad and the tomato heirloom salad (whatever was in this dressing was like crack). The star of the course, the short rib, fell short of our expectations. While it was tender, the overall taste of it wasn't anything spectacular. The dessert itself was just ok as well. There were seeds in there that kept getting stuck in our teeth so that got a bit annoying lol.

On top of that, the service was so odd. We clearly weren't done finishing our food, and we were asked multiple times if they can remove our plates for us. Towards the end, my friend still had some ribs to finish while a gentleman walked over and asked if he was done, and proceeded to wait there until my friend was done eating. On top of that, when we were done, we waited maybe 20+ minutes for someone to bring us our check. 

We paid $200+ for this, and I'm afraid to say it was definitely not worth it. Maybe in the future, I'll try the actual restaurant.

I thought the cocktails - which were phenomenal - were better than the food. It was a very vegetable-forward summery menu, and I enjoyed the som tum, carrot crepe and tomato schnitzel. I remember the scallop dish from my last visit here more than two years ago; it's their signature and interesting with the sweet and savory combination of flavors. The s'mores which you put together yourself in the beautiful back garden is a gimmick but cute, if you're into that sort of thing. 

1. Carrot Crepe (Clams, Sunflower, Carrot Butter)
2. Heirloom Tomato Schnitzel (Pistachio Pesto, Piperade, Olive Oil Jam)
3. Tempura Fried Dashi Poached New Potatoes (XO Sauce)
4. Duck Liver Mousse (Late Harvest Strawberries, Jicama, Alex's Toast)
5. Spelt Bread (Truffle Honey Butter, Warm Ricotta with Garden Chive Oil)
6. Summer Squash Som Tum (Heirloom Thai Chili, Shisho, Cashew and Shrimp Crumble)
7. Pasilla Rubbed Scallops (Corn Pudding, Blueberries, Chanterelles)
8. S'mores (House Marshmallow, Ginger Snaps, Hershey's Bar)
9. Peach (Single Barrel Ragtime Rye, Amaro Meletti, Bitters, Absinthe Rinse)
10. Baby Flower Watermelon (Clairin, Aquavit, Amontillado, Lemongrass, Yuzu) - Not Pictured

Had dinner at Olmsted on Friday evening. The restaurant is testing limits of creativity with its menu, however I couldn't help but feel that the concepts and the flavors were not aligned, sacrificing quality for style.

Quality: Olmsted is a Brooklyn restaurant that has garnered a strong reputation. They keep a small menu that rotates regularly, and we visited during the start of the fall season. While there was no doubt that the dishes use very fresh ingredients and attempt to elevate traditional items, I left feeling there was not much about my meal I loved. I started the evening with the Rosemary Cocktail, based in mezcal with a herbal and spicy flavor, it was a hit with me. For dishes, first out were the Beer Battered Squash Rings, which were just okay. They come out hanging on a tree, and while I liked the mix of seasoning on them, I just felt it landed closer to onion rings than the donuts they aimed for. Next was the Duck Liver Mousse, which I liked though it was a little heavy on jam. Then was their signature Kale & Crab Rangoons, which I simply did not enjoy. I think the name conjures a certain flavor, and this was quite the opposite. I would classify the dish as closer to fried ravioli. The one thing I think they did get right from take-out Chinese crab rangoons is the minimal amount of crab flavor. Our mains were both decent, but neither I would need again. The Rutabaga Tagliatelle added an interesting textural element to a traditional pasta dish, but not one I would crave. While the Roasted & Confit Duck was a fun way to showcase two styles of duck, with the confit style much more flavorful. There were highlights to the meal, but my true takeaway was too much inconsistency for a menu with so few items.
Quantity: Dishes are all medium sized and arranged to share. 
Value: $15-$16 for their Cocktails. $15 for the Beer Battered Squash Rings. $16 for the Duck Liver Mousse. $18 for the Kale & Crab Rangoon. $30 for the Rutabaga Tagliatelle. $36 for the Roasted & Confit Duck.
Ambiance: Olmsted is located in the Prospect Heights area of Brooklyn. The street in front of the restaurant was shut down, so they had plenty of seating located outside. Inside, the space is long and narrow, with a bar that stretches about half the restaurant, until it hits the kitchen, with a row of tables parallel. Lots of plants hung from the wall, adding a touch of greenery to an otherwise simple space. They also have an outdoor garden patio, which looked lovely from my quick peek. The space gets pretty loud when busy, so I could not tell if music was playing in the background.
Crowd: Reservations are required at least a week out for this hot spot. I was only able to get bar seating on a Friday night.
Service: They were one of the more stringent locations for COVID I have visited recently, still doing contact tracing. We sat at the bar and the two guys behind the counter were great acting as servers for us and drink makers for the rest of the restaurant.
Parking: With construction and closed streets, the only parking would be several blocks away.

I was really looking forward to trying Olmsted for months but left feeling a little underwhelmed. The squash onion rings were great but I really wish there were more of them.. 4 small rings for $15 felt a bit ridiculous. The banana squash bread and the root vegetable som tum were blah. We also got the crab and kale rangoon, which kind of just tasted like spinach and artichoke dip.. no crab in them. The lobster spatzle and the roasted and confit duck were delicious and definitely the standouts. The arctic char was also pretty good. Overall, there were a couple good dishes but most of them fell flat.

Great accommodations and a well organized restaurant. We ended up at the bar for a hour because without reservations, that's all you going to get. It's plenty of time for a quick drink and a few dishes. 

A quality and well made cocktails is definitely hard to fine. Olmsted bartender knows their drinks and crafts some of the best drinks in the area. We tried the honeysuckle and spiced pear on the menu. Apparently these are seasonal drinks and can't wait for their fall creation. 

I love the exterior and interior decor. It's small inside but they still feel spacious with the way things are. I haven't get a chance to see the backyard and maybe next time with a reservation. 

I am honestly not a fan of the food. It's too creative for me.

Came here on a Friday night & managed to negotiate a bar seat for an hour for drinks and some apps. I think this spot serves fantastic and inventive cocktails & would love to keep coming back to sample their seasonal rotation. My partner had a white Negroni with a gin made from Montpelier VT. Really appreciate how the bartenders know their gin story & origin (apparently it's a distillery founded by a distiller and bee farmer) and they honored that origin in the cocktail they featured (with honey).

The food presentation was great but don't think I'm so sold on them. I had a rutabaga tagliatelle and while the concept was great the flavor infusion was a bit lacking. The fried squash was also delish but perhaps under seasoned?

Went to Olmsted tonight for my 5 year wedding anniversary. Sadly, despite the amazing reviews, it was a disappointment. There is no soul at Olmsted. It didn't seem like any passion went into preparing the food and the service was like a conveyor belt, having 3-4 different servers.

It is suggested you order 3-4 dishes to share. We ordered 5. The food was lacking, at best, with little flavor. And we left still hungry. I'm not sure what the goals are for Olmsted. It was a very cold dining experience-- definitely not romantic. There are loads of better options for a special occasion.

A beautiful little "farm" feel in the middle of Prospect Heights! Really, one of those "only in Brooklyn" restaurants where you feel completely taken out of the city. Reservations here are pretty hard to come by, and I recommend looking for reservations at least 2 weeks in advance. We enjoyed sitting in the back patio area, and it seems that they can still accommodate walk ins but without real tables. The soft shell crab here was so good (although cost a pretty penny), as were the asparagus fries. Our gin cocktail was good and did not taste strong. Overall, great experience, and definitely somewhere to try at least once, but I don't think I'll be back again since it was just a little too expensive for the amount of food - and the area has great options for less as well.

Our first time here, and its our new favorite. Everything was wonderful. The food, and ambiance was all so comforting. The main room seemed a bit loud, so if you'd like a more intimate setting the garden is the way to go. We will be back to try all the new season menus.

I was very excited to try this place. I am a fan of farm to table type restaurants. Had every dish except 3 (skipped the bread, duck liver mousse and swapped the artic char for the special arctic char). The dishes were very well presented but none of which were delicious. The special arctic char was probably the best dish but it was mostly just great fish with acid. After every dish I thought, maybe the better dishes are coming - nope. 

The restaurant is cute and very organized. Oh and my friends mocktail was f'ing amazing - Sage and Molasses syrup with Ginger beer, I'd only come back for that, sorry chefs.

This place has inventive food, good service and a nice atmosphere. 

Server very helpful in identifying types of allergens in each dish. She also recommended the right amount of food for the 4 of us to order. 

All the dishes were either delicious and creative or, at worst, solid. Many served in artful ways. 
Fresh plates and utensils brought midway through. Appreciated 

Bathroom grade: A+. When I want to stay in the bathroom, when I return to the table and talk about the good bathroom -- it deserves this grade. So I'm waiting for the bathroom-- a single-serve gender neutral-- and the server says if I don't want to wait there is another one, and gives me directions. I'm winding through a series of doors and then----- there's a magical hallway, like a woodland passage. And behind an unassuming door, a bathroom with magical Victorian wallpaper, Apothoke candle and terry towels. I visited the other bathroom before the end of the night. Though it didn't have a magical passageway, the decor was woodland- magical in its own way.

Dinner at Olmstead was delicious, the flavors were fun and interesting, and the cocktail menu is well done. But the real highlight was our server, Emma, who made the night special with her great recommendations and cool ease. Not sure the food is worth all the hype of the place, but it was solid. Emma is definitely worth the hype. Thank you for a lovely dinner!

So to start: as of yesterday, Olmsted has started only offering a Pre-Fixe dinner. It was their first night, which is prone to some issues they may need to work through (i.e. very very slow food prep...we were there for nearly 3 hours...). That being said, I can't wait to come back and experience a regular menu.

The four starters were all quite delicious. The burrata dip for the bread was refreshing. The duck ham wrapped fritters were absolutely delicious. The oyster mushroom tempura also stood out. 

Both mains were solid, too. The thai-inspired soup was a nice flavorful departure.

The chocolate cake was a bit too dry, but came out quickly which was nice.

The drinks are great, too. The cocktail menu isn't massive, so we had basically tried everything between the 3 of us over the three hour meal.
Superb gourmet dishes! Superb service! I love this place and the food !! Greatest birthday place my sister could have chosen!

Just so-so. We had the pre fixe with the wine pairing. The timing was all over the place, we were there for 2.5 hours. The wine would get poured for the next course and we'd wait another 20 min for the food that was supposed to go with it. Didn't have water on the table for half the meal. The food was good but it left us thinking "what can we have for a snack when we get home?"

Finall take my foodie pilgrim to Olmsted for pre-VDay celebration! Didn't disappoint! Creative cooking meets fresh locally sourced ingredients. 

Olmsted recently switched to tasting menu only . Great, less work for me ;P Starting off with the popcorn monkfish bites with lime leaf - light, savory and perfect to go with the paired bubby.

Duck ham air-baguette (say what!?) was a pleasant surprise - a cross between bread stick and duck ham crostini. I would consider remaking this at my next house cocktail party.  

And  the rubataga soup, a off-the-beaten-path veggie choice , is akin the savory, creami-licious version of pea soup that demonstrated a potato leek soup like consistency and umami from miso. 

My favorite was the agedashi scallops - practically an adaptation of tamagotofu and fishcake but more delicate. And it jiggled! 

The special add-on ribeye with paper-thin scallop potatoes was beautiful in presentation and execution.

Service and wine pairing was on point; the tasting menu is well worth every penny. Will def come back soon!

The tasting menu was a bit of a disappointment.  I would have easily considered it a fun, surprising dinner at HALF the cost.  But for $90 a person, it just felt brutally slimmed down for the sake of covid savings.  Understood, but I left feeling cheated. 

None of those fun little quirky plates like, rangoon served in a Chinese container are included.   You start with some thoughtful nibbles, a shot of delicious soup, a couple of monkfish fritters.  Its a great start, but these are all tiny tastes.  And then it kind of falls of the rails.

Next comes a mini loaf of fresh bread.  Everyone loves fresh bread, but make no mistake, this is meant to fill you up.  You will leave hungry if you dont engage with this bread.   You must eat all the bread, enjoy the foamy dip like its a legit course because it is.

The next  is a scallop dish, totally tasty.  Because its a tiny fancy dish, you'll take small bites and search for the little flavors from the various ingredients.  Great but small.  Live in this dish because its the best you'll get for the night.

And the big dissapointment for me, was the crescendo.  Mushroom risotto, with vegetable in place of the rice.  Its a nice dish, but not one that sticks to the ribs, as they say, and just not that special.   Its vegetarian, and just... light.  TLDR: Its a shame to say, don't come hungry to this meal. 
A nice dessert follows.

My wife and I went here over the weekend to check out the tasting menu and I was super, super impressed. I had been a few times over the years and always enjoyed the food but was never quite as in love with this place as the entire neighborhood seems to be. That being said, this past visit really changed my perspective and I kind of hope they stick to a tasting menu format indefinitely! First of all, as far as tasting menus go, $89 is very reasonable. All told with a few cocktails, 2 tasting menus, tax and tip we came in under $300. Now the food:

- Duck ham baguette - tasty, nothing mind blowing but a great starter
- Completely blanking on the name of a particular soup they served, i think it was a rutabaga soup, so light, creamy, warm and satisfying. Just really deep flavors. 
- monkfish popcorn - little monkfish nuggets - nothing extraordinary but super addictive and a great starter 
- bread course with an aerated ricotta - omg, really indescribable. best bread course i've had anywhere in years, wish there was more of it. 
- agedashi scallop - never had a scallop with the texture of this particular one before, that being said, forget the scallop, which was great, my favorite thing about this dish was the broth which was so complex, tangy, slightly sweet, sour, just a complete flavor bomb
- salsify "risotto" - think of a root vegetable based risotto where every bite is completely unique, and the rootiness of it all somehow doesn't get in the way of the melt in your mouth flavors. really good.
- rainbow carrot cake - like one of those oat bars you can get at any grocery store but exponentially tastier? very carroty and not overly sweet. a really nuanced dessert that i could've had 20 of. 

Strongly recommend for a special night out!

This is a really cute place for dinner. There is a garden seating that is outdoors but heated and semi-indoor. 

Beef tartare was much more seasoned and chewy than others I've had elsewhere. Still good just different. The pork collar was ok - was told would be crispy and there was indeed a slight crisp but maybe had my expectations built up for it because I expected it to be crispier.

Probably the curry spatzle was our favorite dish. Really reminiscent of the spatzle I've had in Munich. Soft but chewable, and the curry flavor was light.

The frozen yogurt is really good. I prefer that over the chocolate mousse. Would also not recommend having both of them at the same time since the yogurt is much sweeter than the mousse so it takes away from the flavor/overpowers. 

Overall would give the food 4 stars, but service was a little slow (we ordered everything aside from dessert from the beginning and each dish took a while to come, as well as the check) and I don't think I would come back too often since the food is a bit pricey for what you get, which dropped my rating to 3. I would give this place a shot if you haven't been here before and judge for yourself though! Worth trying!

We did a prefix menu with wine pairings. It was outstanding. The staff was so knowledgeable and helpful. I have many allergies and they worked around all of them. Definitely need a reservation. The outdoor back patio seating was really nice. The inside looked a bit tight when it was full. It's pricey but worth it for a celebratory dinner!

I went to Olmsted last night to celebrate my husbands birthday and had a pleasant experience.

We sat in a little shack in the garden. There was also outdoor garden area with heating lamps if you are waiting for tables & wants to have a drink. Food here was casual fine dining which were light and flavorful. Overall food tasted relatively healthy and I also find staffs at the restaurant friendly. I thought price was good ($89 for 4 course menu) and was satisfied with the amount of the food but my husband who is a big eater wasn't full after the dinner and had another small meal at home. One thing I liked about their menu is that they also provided non alcoholic pairings with pre-fixed menu which I appreciate as a light drinker. They also had some really cool looking cocktails.

Even though we visited on Wednesday night this place was packed and I think Olmsted is a great casual but nice place to have a dinner with friends.
Loved the food on the pre fixe menu! Very innovative. The ambience and staff were also very friendly. Definitely a great date night spot!

We went for a last minute late night reservation. Everything was nice and lovely. Flavors were muted and subtle. Enjoyed the starchy risotto and the scallop agadashi. Wine pairing is pleasant, and they were kind enough to substitute dishes to accommodate my dining companion's restrictions. The only downside was the duck ham breadstick in the amuse bouches... the bread was somewhat stale, maybe perhaps our reservation was for so late.

We had very high expectation given head chef's past experience but came out with mild disappointment. There are a few hits and misses in the menu. We got white asparagus sushi, bread service, lobster cracker, Gazpacho soup, carrot crepe and duck breast. We also ordered three cocktails. 

The carrot crepe is bomb! It's delicious with well balanced of savory, sweet and umami. We really enjoyed it!

The rest is a bit mediocre, especially the zaatar duck breast. The spice is too strong and duck is too salty. We waited a while (about 1.5 hours) for our main entree but was very disappointed. 

The cocktails were not great either. Rosemary cocktail is lack of herb flavor. Other ones are a bit too sweet.

Came here on a date night with my boyfriend last night with some high expectations and left somewhat disappointed. There were some definite hits and misses. 

What We Got:
Orange Wine - Not like a typical orange wine, but good. 

Duck Liver Mousse - Definitely an acquired taste. Really rich and not enough crackers. 
Fried Pickles - The pickles got lost in the batter and sauce. 
Bread Service - Both bread and marmalade were delicious.
Kale & Crab Rangoon - Biggest disappointment of the night for me. Crab was completely lost and while making it lighter with ricotta is a great idea it missed on the creaminess that makes this dish normally so good.
Carrot Crepe -  Great flavor and texture. Would 100% get again. 
Tagliatelle - Our favorite dish of the night. It was made with a vegetable (can't recall) that made this normally heavy dish feel a lot lighter.

By far the desserts were the best part of the night. We were a little bummed that neither the churros nor smore's were available *but* we split the froyo and strawberry rhubarb shortcake and were so happy. 

Service:
Our server was both helpful and informative. They take your entire order at once so the one big downside to the service was that it felt like dishes came out really quickly for us before we had to make space for another. 

Overall this is a place I'd likely come back to for dessert and wine. While some other items are great, it feels like too expensive of a spot with not enough of a guarantee.

A solid farm to table option with cute outdoor space - the best tasting or value farm to table I've been to in nyc? No.

Food - 4/5 - in general, we had a great meal. The duck liver mousse was a classic, heavy but decadent and lovely and they were generous with extra crostini. The rutabaga tagliatelle - it means the noodles are made of rutabaga!! We were surprised, definitely better than any other vegetable based noodle I've ever had - but overall the dish was pretty bland. The broccolini was a must have! Fennel cocktail was light, refreshing and lovely. Skip the asparagus som tum. The desserts weren't tempting....

Service - 5/5 - truly went above and beyond. I tried to get an extra seat on a rainy night, and the host tried everything truly - sadly unsuccessful, but I really appreciate the effort. They forgot our duck liver mousse, but when we reminded us, they gave it to us on the house - really classy and appreciated!!

Ambiance - 5/5 - love the light and greenery indoors. The outdoor seating was warm and gorgeous, very much evoked the farm to table atmosphere. Not too crowded or loud. And a gorgeous, clean, great smelling bathroom!!!
Excellent meal, very innovative dishes and delicious cocktails. We sat at the bar looking into the kitchen. It was fun to see how everything was put together z

This hip prospect heights eatery has been getting great notices for years. Much of it truly deserved. The location is small and hosts a nice bar which you can eat at and watch the cooks work. Limited table seating is tight and reservations are highly recommended. The drink menu is great and the wine selection is lovely. The menu is seasonal and changes every so often. It's limited but it's focus is great. I was actually amazed the chefs are able to make this menu in such a small kitchen. The lobster crackers are a must. The som was nice as well. Crudo is tasty and light. I did find the pork dish over cooked but tasty. Staff is friendly and attentive. And the back garden is a must!

I live in the area and have been meaning to come to this restaurant. It is usually fully booked and if you're trying to do a walk in on a weekend , forgettahboutit!  I was ecstatic when I got an early reservation and had the pleasure to try the farm to table food provided. 

We ordered the duck liver mousse, the fried asparagus, the scallops, and roast duck. For our drink we both got the fennel! Which was also very good, light and herby, perfect for an early dinner.
The duck liver mousse was light and surprising. It was sweet and paired well with the baguette and spring onion. The fried asparagus was one of my absolute favorites! It was perfectly seasoned and the side sauce of lemon aioli, I couldn't put my finger on, but it paired well with the salt from the asparagus. 
Between these two plates they wiped our table to get ready for the entree , which was a nice touch! 
Then they served us the scallops with polenta and 
Za'atar Duck. 

The scallops were cooked perfectly and seasoned well, with a little heat kick I loved. The polenta was great and creamy and should be eaten with the scallops . 
Last but certainly not least we had the Smoked Duck. This dish stole the show. This was single-handedly the best duck I've ever had. It was so tender and paired with a semi sweet sauce underneath it was just golden. It came sliced and also shredded, and a side of something I thought was like a roti. I could've eaten 10 of those ducks, I am not kidding. 

Anyway, an amazing experience with amazing food. I would've given 5 stars, but I would suggest an addition of a screen door to keep any (of the very few) flies out of the restaurant. 

My favorite: Za'atar Smoked Duck Breast 
Her Favorite: Duck Mousse ("I've never had mousse like that!!")

First off, cocktails. Love when the cocktails are just as good as the food - I'd come here for the drinks alone. I tried the fennel & honeysuckle and really enjoyed both. The honeysuckle was gin forward without being overwhelming. Also had a sip of the "cucumber" cocktail and that was (so!) refreshing. 

As for food, some reviews mention a prix fixe but this wasn't on the menu when we came in on a Sunday during early dinner. 

Our party of two had the duck liver mousse, tempura asparagus, lobster cracker, some kind of ceviche, duck breast, and a froyo w/ lavender honey. Everything delectable, everything plated prettily.  Plates are on the small end so we could've done one more dish, but we left feeling content and not stuffed. 

Only miss was that there were random lulls, e.g., two apps arrived before our drinks; there was a period of random 15 mins from our third dish to the fourth; another lag of 15 mins from the fourth dish to the fifth; someone dropped off the lobster cracker without a suggestion as to be mindful that the lobster foam would dissipate (we were too busy finishing off the mousse) - but none of these shortcomings were attributable to our waitress, who was hospitable & helpful in ordering. 

Looking forward to coming back to try other menu items v soon (restaurant seems to change menus according to what's in season). 

Tip - we made a resy for inside & dined indoors but the pros / repeat patrons appear to opt for the outdoor garden area which seems to be the right move; they have a beautiful outdoor setup.

We were a little hesitant to dine here because it's not an inexpensive meal, but boy was it worth it! My only regret was not making the reservation further in advance. They were fully booked outside so our only option was indoors. The have a beautiful outdoor space in the back for dinner, and there is also a wonderful area for drinks and snacks outside. TIP: If you have to book indoors, arrive early to grab a drink outside (in the back patio) prior to your meal.

We ordered the following for three people which was the perfect amount of food:
Tempura Fried Asparagus: crispy and delicious
Zucchini Som Tom: if you like papaya salad, order it!
Fluke Crudo: small bites with big flavor
Kale & Crab Rangoon: unique, crunchy, and sorta healthy because of the kale
Carrot Crepe: delicate, light, and feels/tastes like summer 
Za'atar Smoked Duck Breast: cooked and seasoned to perfection
Old School Chocolate Mousse Vanilla Creme Fraiche: creamy, rich, and just the right sweetness

TIP: If you are going here to celebrate something (we went for my friend's birthday), mention that in the reservation. They brought out a special dessert with a candle, and I didn't even have to remind them. Nice touch Olmsted!

The service was impeccable.
One of the most creative and delightful meals of all time! Great service and atmosphere, loved the garden space. Don't wait to get here!!

Had dinner here for the first time after hearing good things. The staff was courteous and knowledgeable and the service was seamless. The food was a delicious sensory experience. Come here with an open mind and enjoy the ride.

I came here to celebrate my sister's birthday last night, and she chose this restaurant because she had heard that it's a great restaurant, and after my experience, I realized that this is definitely true. Olmsted is a farm-to-table tapas restaurant and there were plenty of good options on the menu. We had a hard time deciding what we wanted because everything sounded really good, so we just ended up ordering everything. The food was great, and I loved everything but we got full really fast because everything on the menu was so good. 

After we had finished our meal, we were escorted to the garden area of the restaurant for dessert we ordered the froyo and the chocolate/corn dish and they were good. I originally thought the chocolate and corn combination would be too weird but it was pretty good. I have to say that the froyo was AMAZING! It was a lavender-flavored froyo with a honey-flavored marshmallow fluff topping. I am SO happy that I can eat dairy now because this was an amazing experience. 

The restaurant is also very accommodating towards dietary restrictions, which made it easy for my gluten intolerance and my dad's intolerance to certain spices. 

The restaurant was also really beautiful, and I recommend going to the bathroom with the long hallway because it feels like you're stepping into another world. It's so beautifully decorated. The garden is also really nice because there is a lot of space and they grow their own herbs. I also notice that they have three quails for some reason. I don't know why they had them there, but they were so cute! If you're thinking about coming here PLEASE, DO! I promise you will love it.

I was really looking forward to my visit to Olmsted, but we were very disappointed. Ee were seated where the air conditioner was dripping next to me. I was unhappy with the Ramp cocktail. I am a big fan of Gin Gibsons, and this drink just had way too much vinegar. I could not drink it and sent it back. We thought that Watermelon Sushi was terrible, all you tasted was bonito flakes. It was a waste of good fish. We liked the carrot crepe. The crab rangoons were under seasoned, and it was just poor presentation that the dumplings did not fit in the bowl for the sauce. We got the smoked duck - which was way to smokey - the duck was tender, and that was good - but you tasted only smoke. It was a waste of a good piece of duck. The scallops were prepared well, BUT - that corn/blueberry sauce was not good. We also had to wait 20 minutes for the scallops. I think the server did not put the order in until we checked in with her. I appreciated not being charged for the Ramp cocktail. Overall it was a big disappointment! I would not recommend Olmsted and I doubt I will be interested in trying it out again.

Food was amazing 

I ordered:
Quinoa crusted Duck 
Carrot crepe 
Kale and crab wontons 

Although the duck was crusted, it was still morsel melt in mouth good; very soft and paired well with the berry and greens dip served with it. I had a glass of  Tempranillo that paired well with the dish. 

The carrot crepe was not what I expected but in a good way. It was savory but a small dish.

If by yourself, ordering an appetizer and one main dish will definitely fill your needs. When learned most plates were small I ordered more but ended up having leftovers.
Incredible meal. The carrot crepe was a standout. The watermelon cocktail was also excellent. Pricey but worth it.

Went to Olmsted recently and wish I could give it a split review: 5 stars for food and 2 stars for the experience. The food was spectacular and original and delicious, plated gorgeously. Service was a tad slow, but my entire party raved about everything we got: pork collar, smoked duck breast, watermelon sushi, tempura beans, fortex beans, crab rangoon, carrot crepe...just...WOW. Clever cocktails and superb wines added to the great experience.

Here are the negatives: the service was aggressive and controlling. NO, WE DO NOT WANT TO SHARE OUR FOOD. We had to argue with the wait staff about that, and we should not have had to do that. I get that sharing is a thing, but it will never be with me and my friends. Once we said that we were not sharing, the wait staff should have kept their thoughts to themselves, "Some people order the entire menu." Ok, but some of us had dietary restrictions and the wait staff kept forcing the issue about how the kitchen could modify. We had all selected what we wanted and the wait staff's behavior was way over the top and frankly annoying.

Also, we were sitting in the garden and we saw the lovely birds in cages and the garden beds and...rats. Many, many rats. I was pretty sure they weren't getting inside but...sure, the restaurant composts and grows food and those activities attract rats but seeing them did not enhance our dining experience. If you eat inside you won't see them but in the garden, well, just don't look out there.

The food is beautiful and delicious.  We ordered one of everything. The service, however, was lacking. Our server was lovely and then he disappeared.  He was replaced by a grumpy, sour woman.  it's unfortunate the front of house let down the kitchen.  We will not be returnin.

We LOVED our dinner at Olmsted. The hosts were so accommodating to us after we showed up 30 minutes late to our reservation by accident. They still sat us very quickly and were very understanding of the mishap on our end. 

It is "tapas" style so everything on the menu is meant to be shared. It is definitely pricey but everything we tried was so tasty. The cocktails were delicious and service was phenomenal. Would definitely come back!

This was our second time at dining here, and it was an extremely disappointing experience. Olmsted goes out of their way to mention that they can accommodate specific food allergies and dietary restrictions - I happen to have a severe allergy to nuts and seeds. This was explicitly mentioned in notes in our Resy reservation, but we also told the person who sat us at our table and our server multiple times. We decided to add another dish to our order at the end of our meal - we were concerned specifically about the spices used in this dish because it usually contains sesame seeds, so we were very careful to mention this to our server. She told us she did not think the spice contained seeds and came back to tell us we were good to go after checking with the kitchen. We must have mentioned my allergy more than 5 times throughout the course of the meal and in ordering this specific dish.
