When the order came out, it had visible seeds on top - we were so sure that these could not be sesame seeds (maybe they were tomato seeds or pepper seeds which I am not allergic to?) because we had talked about it so much - I almost took a bite because we had been told explicitly that this food would be safe, but we decided to doublecheck and ask one more time. Our server went back to ask the kitchen and confirmed they were seeds - if I had eaten them, I would have ended up in the hospital (or potentially worse). While they apologized, my follow-up discussion with the restaurant included inaccurate information and did not make me feel comfortable that they understood the gravity of this situation. I would warn anyone with dietary restrictions to avoid going here.

Additionally, there were two MASSIVE rats (I have lived in Brooklyn for a very long time and these were two of the biggest rats I have ever seen - probably each at least a foot long) running around in the area where guests were dining in the garden.

Sad to say, I will never be returning.

Been here a few more times since the original post and everything has been consistently good. I've enjoyed sitting at the bar counter as the bartenders have always been super helpful in choosing wine that pairs nicely with each dish. Also, just look at how perfect these wontons are! So crispy on the outside, silky smooth on the inside and just explode with flavor
Really cute new farm-to-table new American. Food was great. Outdoor dining area is really nice. I even ordered a beet drink! Unclear if it's alluding to Olmstead, prospect park's landscape architect!

We had our small family wedding dinner in Olmsted's private dining room, as well as a 30-min cocktail service in their garden beforehand. 

The food, drinks and service couldn't be beat. Our party of 17 (including two kids) was beautifully taken care of, and every dish we had built on the last for a lovely, totally satisfying meal. Unbeknownst to us, one of our guests had a food allergy they communicated to the staff at the last moment, and they pivoted on the spot for his needs.

The private dining room didn't look like too much when we originally checked it out, but for our dinner and by candlelight it was charming, feeling both homey and special occasion. The garden was also lovely to enjoy a drink or two before we went inside for dinner.

I'm giving 4 of 5 stars (I'd do 4.5 if I could) because while the final experience was all that we hoped it would be, some of the the communication/planning ahead of time was spotty and frustrating. In the end it all worked out, and stressors get magnified in a big way when you're wedding planning, so if you're planning a birthday party or other celebration, you might not find it as troublesome.

In the end I would certainly recommend Olmsted for a private dining experience. Get the smoked duck if they have it as a menu option!

This place is extremely average for the price. I was with a group of 4 and the waitress actually recommended we order the entire menu because of the portions if we were hungry or 9 dishes if we weren't that hungry! Seriously!? We started off ordering cocktails and my mezcal cocktail was good, but nothing special. We first had the duck mousse that was actually pretty decent and the crudo was decent as well, but not memorable. The brussel sprouts were basically a bowl of burnt brussel sprouts leaves with truffle shavings on top, very boring. The roasted butternut squash was a joke for $30. This was probably the worst dish I have every ordered for over $30, EVER. I could honestly make a better butternut squash dish at home. The scallops were another joke. Two tiny scallops on sticks with some lettuce with for $34?! Everything is so outrageously overpriced it is comical how people would even come here when there are so many better options in the neighborhood for that type of money. Save your money and go somewhere better.

Food was amazing, ambiance was amazing and service was wonderful. You pick 2 appetizers, 2 small plates, and 2 main plates. Then they time each plate to come out after you are finishing the last, and they did a heck of a job! Smocked duck and Pork collar were fricken amazing. You should 100% plan this in your next trip out.

After wanting to try here for a while, we finally went for dinner last night. Excellent food, wine, and service. The three of us ordered 5 dishes and 2 desserts and it was the perfect amount - the waitress was spot on when she suggested 5-7 dishes for us. She also gave a great wine recommendation that was a very good price. All the food was tasty but the duck was by far our favourite. In fact it was probably one of the best duck dishes I've ever had and I regularly order duck when I'm out. Just perfectly cooked and such good flavour. 

We got: crudo, brussle sprouts, speatzle, pork, duck, chocolate and corn, and the zeppole. Also had a bottle of bubbly and some port. 

Will definitely go back when the weather is nicer and try out the back yard.

Very nice ambiance, seated promptly when we arrived a little early for our reservation. Very attentive service.

Everything was really good:

Cocktails: 4/5. My friend felt so-so on the first one he received, but then was able to freely swap it out with the one I got because he liked it a lot more.

Beer battered squash rings: 5/5. Presented on a cool, albeit a little cumbersome, tree.

Mahi-mahi crudo: 5/5. Fresh, simple, garnished tastefully with a delicious sauce.

Crab and carrot curry: 5/5. Our favorite! Tasted Thai-inspired.

Scallop lettuce wraps: 4.5/5. Reminded me of vietnamese wraps, but with pickled vegetables.

Roasted maitake: 4/5. Something about it tasted a little yogurty/sour, and unfortunately I don't like that. Also seemed to need a bit more of umami.

Grilled honey nut squash: 4/5. I don't remember this too much other than that it didn't really wow me... Although, the squash Rangoon, that was memorable in a great way.

Grilled pork collar: 4.5/5. Nice.

Service: 5/5!

Rounded down to a 4 for some of the above dishes and the price. Would come back here again, but not frequently as it's pricey.

Really really good food. They had a lot of squash on the menu the night we ate there:  battered delicata rings for an appetizer, the bread had squash in it, and there was a honeynut squash entree. Skipped the bread but the other two were excellent, as was the the duck liver mousse and the short ribs. Where they were less than perfect was service. We waited 3 minutes inside for someone to greet and seat us, with no acknowledgment from the bartender or any of the wait staff who saw us standing here, not even an eyebrow raise or nod or "we'll be with you shortly". Our server was very nice but extremely soft spoken (the restaurant is NOT QUIET) so we had to have her repeat things again and again. And the dietary restriction thing got a little...forced. Both of us have some - not allergies, more like strong preferences - and we told the server we could figure it out. She kept questioning us - are you vegetarian? Pescatarian? We said no, and no allergies so nothing for the kitchen to worry about, but we can work it out when we look at the menu. "But are you pescatarian?" Back off, we got it.

This is a grift. The food is atrocious. It's made for pretentious hipsters who  are impressed by semi prepared Georgian food. 

16.00 for 4 butternut squash rings, poorly spiced. 
18.00 or so for crudo that is cut too thickly, improperly spiced. It's as though it's an amateur chef, trying to find his footing. 

The Main of scallops were barely cooked, the salad was the worst thing you probably ever put into your mouth. 
They kitchen doesn't really cook anything. 

The dessert is audacious. They will spoon froyo and call it innovative. Sad. 

Atrocious food. Impersonal service, chef table felt uncomfortable. Save your money, if you want a tough time, but with better food, try any Georgian fare

We went to Olmsted 2 years ago and were surprised by the tiny portions and high prices. It was during the pandemic and we thought it might just be a blip.

No... it's not a blip. Long story short, Olmsted is an egregiously expensive restaurant with apathetic employees in a gorgeous space serving delicious food. 

We went last night, excited and nervous to try it again. As soon as we sat down, the service was fine, but lacked much personality or familiarity - standoffish. The food is amazing but the portions are surprisingly small, even for folks who are used to fine dining portions. 12 dollars for a small cinnamon roll style bread (BUT DELICIOUS)! Natural wine (tasted like grape juice) was 100 a bottle. The heated garden is gorgeous and was very sweet.

What an experience! Went here to celebrate my husband's 72nd birthday and a belated 30th birthday for our son-in-law.  They have a tasting menu that they accommodated for my fish allergy and son's shellfish allergy.  Our daughter and myself added the wine pairing and the guys shared a stout.  The menu changes with the seasons so we'll definitely have to return. We added the bread and short ribs with black garlic to the dinner. The appetizer had crab/kale Rangoon and a vegan choice with spinach. We tasted fried duck rilette, and artic char, pickled delicata squash and so much more. We finished the meal with vanilla orange ice cream with freeze dried cranberries.  One of the most amazing food experiences I've ever had.

The food and atmosphere reeked of pretentiousness. Exorbitantly expensive for meager portions of food. I paid $88 dollars (with tip) for a thimble sized cup of soup, 1 crab rangoon, and 1 small duck deep fried stick plus the main meal of ribs...no sorry one rib wiht sauce). Not a repeat. Not even a matter of inflation. I'm just appalled.

My boyfriend and I came here for our anniversary dinner. We were blown away by everything we ordered. It was creative, delicious, and presented in a way that was truly special. The scallops appetizer and the s'mores dessert was a huge highlight. We also thought it was so sweet they brought us another dessert to celebrate our anniversary. We'll definitely be coming back.

The ambience is nice but this place is definitely not worth it. The appetizers were great...but then the entrees came out and hour+ later while we're paying these outrageous prices. Service was meh 

By the way the bar has a shit ala carte menu that has no options and is way overpriced. I saw the person next to me get the same dish way quicker...? Don't come here 
 
Go to Otis

The food is delicious. It is truly farm-to-table. The front of house staff is also delightful. They have a somm who is really helpful and you should absolutely utilize his help to guide you through their beverage program... it's an often under-utilized service that can truly make or break your experience! The kitchen was extremely careful and accommodating with dietary restrictions which is really nice... they came up with thoughtful alternatives for my vegetarian sister-in-law and my mother who couldn't have gluten or dairy and their dishes weren't just an afterthought (they were delicious!). 

It is pricey, but for the location and quality, it is understandable. My only frustration is with management. We have been to the restaurant a few times and also had a large party in the private dining room. It's a gorgeous space and was a lovely dinner. Unfortunately, management is not organized. They were not easy to communicate with before the event and made some silly mistakes during the event. Thankfully, the waitstaff and kitchen saved the day. While the management compensated for their mistakes after the fact (which again is why I would still recommend the restaurant for dining), I really hope that they consider making some changes to how they manage their beautiful private dining room. If you decide to utilize their private dining space, make sure you cross your t's and dot your i's.

One word to describe this place "mediocre". A mediocre fine dine place, with mediocre cocktails. 
None of the dishe was super tasty or interesting. The service was actually below average, they took our menu cards too soon, the server was not very interested to discuss any food/drink on the menu either.The sequence and menu was also a little off, and I left the place a little hungry as well. 
I can see why this restaurant has lost its Michelin star.

Frederick Olmsted is a name with a big reputation, and this restaurant honors lives up to the man and his accomplishments. Servers are personable but non-intrusive, bartenders are as much perfectionists as their counterparts in the kitchen, and the food is an explosion of delight. We enjoyed expertly curated cocktails, house-made breads with complementary spreads, brilliantly executed meat lovers and vegetarian dishes, and seasonal desserts we were keen to share for extra depth, our experience was memorable. A city with so many options is great for foodies and tough on restaurants, but Olmsted earns its repeat customers.

Food is tasty, atmosphere is good. 

Portions are too small :(

Overall would go more than once because first two reasons but also would eat something later hahah
Great dinner with a crowd of eaters- everything was delicious and servers helpful with  wine suggestions and my gluten needs. Place has a fun vibe.

I went here a few years ago and had an ok meal but loved the garden in the back and the atmosphere. Went back recently to find out it was only an 8 course tasting menu. It was too late to cancel the reservation without being charged so we gave it a try. I was left very hungry after about 8 bites of food and $250 later. The garden in the back is also gone now. I will not be returning.

Having lived in NYC for over 20 years, my first meal at Olmsted was long overdue. And it was, without a doubt, one of my top ten meals in the city. Each course was a testament to culinary excellence.

Three dishes in particular left an unforgettable impression:

- **Cow Tongue Appetizer:** It's a rare skill to transform cow tongue into something as soft, buttery, and bursting with flavor as this. So delightful that even my 7-year-old was enamored.

- **bread service** the bread we received was nothing short of extraordinary. It had this alluring sweet, buttery garlic touch.

- **King Crab Over Rice with Pea Mint Foam:** the best crab dish I've ever had. The richness of the crab harmonized perfectly with the freshness of the minty peas.

We concluded the meal with s'mores, accompanied by actual coals to toast them to perfection. The combination of crisp graham crackers, decadent dark chocolate, and gooey marshmallows was a delightful ending.

Special shout-out to our waiter, Chris, who was warm, attentive, and exceptionally knowledgeable in guiding us through our dining experience.

All the food and drinks at this restaurant are delicious. The chef can accommodate dietary restrictions, even on a pre-fixe menu. The ambiance is nice, the garden is beautiful. The food is very expensive, and one might expect to receive larger portions. However, even after dining on the pre-fixe menu for date night, I left feeling full and pretty satisfied.

The service and staff are extremely friendly and so personable. They were very knowledgeable about the food and the drinks! I got the mezcal drink and it was yummy!  Given the course size for the tasting menu, my friend and I opted Al carte and go the beef tongue and the mini crepes. Both appetizers weren't impressive so I didn't take photos and the crepes were mushy. The two entrees were the duck breast with complimentary heart and glizzard and the king crab dish. Both were good dishes but not wow! The backyard is definitely a sight to behold like a garden!  I can definitely say this is a one and done place.

I came for a friend's birthday and expected a tasting menu and got literally 6 bites of food instead.

None of these bites were impressive and did not leave me wanting more. Honestly, it felt like a total scam.

The only thing that tasted remotely edible was the duck and even that dish only had two small slices of duck breast. 

I'm not certain if these issues were as a result of the the package my buddy ordered or if this place is a serious grift. Overall, huge disappointment. I would never come back nor recommend this place to anyone. 

My prediction is this place won't be around in a year.

We just celebrated a group birthday dinner for my husband and had an amazing time and highly recommend Olmstead for all your birthday dinner needs! I worked with Corbin prior to the event to make sure everything went seamless day of and he was amazing. He made sure that everything was exactly the way we wanted it to be. Right before the dinner started we had some unexpected guest turnaround and Finn was super helpful at adjusting our table setup to be exactly how we like it. The food was amazing as Olmsted always is and the garden in the back was beautiful! Thank you to everyone there for dealing with our big party :)

Dined here for my anniversary and was absolutely blown away! We each had the tasting menu and it could not have been more well thought out and delicious. The ambiance was also unique, we were seated in front of a quail coop, which my girlfriend thought was the cutest thing ever. We were also moved to a more relaxed environment for s'mores after an already incredible version of peaches and cream. Service from Finn was excellent, and Matthew came in clutch with great scotch recommendations.

We were underwhelmed by both the quality of the food and the overall experience. At one point, we waited ~45 minutes between dishes, with the tasting menu taking over 3 hours. For the prices that Olmstead charges, we expected better across the board.
Excellent service and great patio very romantic. We went there for my birthday. I have several food allergies and they were very accommodating. It was very special.

Have eaten there three times between 2021 and a month or so ago, and each time the food has been delicious and inventive. And I love the setting--cozy and personal, with great service. They recently changed up the seating process, so now you are greeted in a kind of anteroom with a little aperitif before they bring you in. Fun and unique, and it is unexpectedly nice to have a special "way station" to enjoy between street and restaurant.
Excellent food, and service. Love the Parring testing menu. A must local hotspot not to miss.

Minus 5 stars

     Thanksgiving dinner 23/11/2023. First of all our party of six were seated at a small round table designed for 4 people. The dinning room was a large hard shell tent suitable for warm weather events. The outside temperature was a chilly 45 deg F. The detached structure had two doors one for food service and the other for patrons which were frequently opened  letting in volumes of cold air. It was heated with overhead radient heaters in the peaked top with ceiling fans above to force air down to the floor. At some point the fans were turned off greatly reducing heated efficiency.  Typical cycling time was 3-4 minutes heat followd by 12 minutes of rapid cool down. We had a wonderful winter camping experience.
     The dinner consisted of several courses of so-so appetizers. One interestingly named, was called an "air baguette". This was a 2&1/2" hollow pastry shell with some kind of flavoring on top. Eventually there were 2 kinds of sliced turkey roll, cranberry sauce, potatoe croqets, ice cold green beans, and an interesting/tasty mushroom stuffing. The desert was a small bowl of 4 tablespoons of (presumably) pumkin pie filling, melted vanilla ice cream and some of crumbly chocolate? waffers. All this a mere $145 per person. Unfortunately Yelp does not have the neagtive 5 stars this meal deserves.  On the positive side the wait staff sevice was good.

Let me cut to the chase! The pre-fixe dinner was a major disappointment considering this restaurant boasts the affirmation of Michelin!
Let's start with food. Except for the two starters, the food was quite underwhelming. The presentation and plating was enticing, but there was no soul and spirit in taste. What I mean is it did not light up my taste buds. As an avid international traveler who also into food in a big way I frequently dine in both Michelin Starred restos as well as in hikes in the wall. I am not quite sure how Michelin decided to recommend this. 
Now the service. Hit and miss is the best way to describe it. With each course the server delivered this rather robotic description of the course. Frankly, it was at turbo speed and half the time couldn't even comprehend what was being said. Very perfunctory!
Ambiance! Average. 
I wish the patrons bonne chance but my likelihood of returning is slim to none!

We arrived about 10 minutes early for our 8pm reservation. Maybe the Hostess felt she needed to accommodate us early, but there was no table for 2 available, or so it would seem. She took us to the kitchen bar. Clearly an area reserved for walk-ins, we surmised, as it was filled with piled-up clean plates. We immediately requested to be moved, at which point Hostess stated the restaurant was full. Full? We have a reservation, we replied. So she quickly pivoted to a table in the rear of the dining room, with a superb view of the bathroom. Moreover, the table abutted the entrance to the patio dining area. which with the door constantly opening, was quite drafty, requiring a space heater for comfort. It was apparent that we were not going to have the 8 pm table that did open up, so we 'gave up' and decided to commence the meal. What we observed during the evening was laughable, but sad. The hostess attempted to 'sell' those same seats 3 times with no luck (I think one couple actually left). The table in the middle of the dining room opened up about 8:10 (we would've waited), but I digress. 
Now to the dinner...
Our server for the evening was Scott. A very gracious and attentive server who 'rescued' the evening. The dinner was paced appropriately and the food was underwhelming to excellent. We ordered the Rangoons (average), Lobster Cracker (underwhelming), the Cheesburger (good) and Duck Pastrami (excellent!). 
A good wine (suggested by our server Scott) enhanced the experience, but the issue with our table almost sunk the evening for us. At the price point of this establishment, much was expected and a bit more understanding from the Hostess, would've gone a long way. Again, thank you Scott and Happy New Year!

Great cocktails, excellent menu, perfect for dates and fancy nights out but worth it.   Get the veggies.   This is a good rule in general but in particular here.   

Glad to have this spot so near me.

It took over a half hour to order a drink from our table. horrible service. in the time it took to get one drink to our table we made a reservation at another place down the street that was so much better. was looking forward to a nice meal and relaxing night and got none of that here...night started off better when we left! really disappointed with this place.
Great food combined with a lovely ambience is always a win! I don't frequent reservation based places often, but I can't wait to go back here.

We had a reservation for 4 at 8:30pm on a Saturday evening. Despite our prompt arrival time, we waited an hour to finally be seated. When we did get to our table, our server was never explicitly introduced to us. The person we thought was on our table (they'd taken our drink orders on the patio) was not, and it took another 15 minutes for us to get water from the person who was our server. The experience  just declined from there. They asked if we'd like still or sparkling water. I requested tap, as often restaurants in the area offer "still" and will bring bottled. The server's condescending response about still being the same as tap was irritating. The pacing for everything was just off - time it took for us to place orders for appetizers, for additional drinks, for dinner. I spoke to the manager about how long it was taking for us to get appetizers, and he assured us "the magic starts now." But it did not. We had a couple more incidents where we felt condescended to by our server, and ultimately we didn't leave until nearly 11:30pm. At the end there was no acknowledgement about our wait, the lack of improvement of service, or anything. 

The food was tasty. We enjoyed the scallop crudo immensely as well as the crab and kale rangoon. The duck liver bahn mi didn't stand out to us. The grilled pork entree was very good, if not particularly filling. The cheeseburger and duck fat fries as also a highlight. 

Despite the quality of the food, it's unlikely we'll return to Olmsted. Being kept waiting despite our reservation, the lack of concern by management, and the experience with our server just didn't inspire warm feelings.

This place is really really nice but something always feels not quite up to the hype. That being said, the food is innovative and the menu changes every 3 months. The aesthetic and vibe is cool earthy modern. Wouldn't go out of my way, but would go again if someone wanted to!

Ambiance was nice, cool plants and chill lighting but the food - super tiny and not good. 

Restaurant notes that they can accommodate allergies - I wrote my allergy (gluten) in the resy reservation and emailed them since they don't pick up the phone to confirm. No response. I arrived for my reservation and they offered me a menu with crossed out items and handwritten substitutions. I ordered the gf "cranberry" bread - no cranberries were in this bread and it was as hard as a rock. Ordered the broccolini tempura - it was 3 tiny pieces in unsalted starch with not much flavor. Ordered the potato gnocchi - it was a joke - it was cubed potatoes in a white soup... no effort whatsoever to make gnocchi. And the portions overall were tiny. We ordered most of the menu. Left hungry! The only part that was good was the dessert the froyo with the whipped honey. Would not come back for this "accommodated" meal.

dinner on a Saturday night: food was mediocre. the water server was great and otherwise the service was terrible; confused (bringing wrong dishes) and incredibly slow -- waiting 20 minutes for cocktails alone. Tables are squeezed so tight as to be claustrophobic. will not return

Olmsted had been on my list since I first read about it in Condé Nast Traveler so I was excited for my first venture into Brooklyn as I usually spend time in Manhattan. I was well on my way until I got on the wrong train and realized to my dismay that I was going to be 45 minutes late! I tried calling the restaurant but was directed to email them which further stressed me out because I assumed I would have to make alternate plans. 
As soon as I entered, I apologized profusely to Michaela and she calmed me down immediately be explaining that even seasoned New Yorkers sometimes get on the wrong train. She did everything she could and secured me a seat at the bar. I was so grateful! As soon as I sat down, Mark, the bartender laughed and joked with me about my experience and soon after I was greeted by my waiter Greg, who was fantastic and by the end of the night, I was just in awe of the hospitality of the entire staff. 
The ambiance was warm and inviting and the curated playlist with artists ranging from Amy Winehouse to Corrine Bailey Rae and Outkast, created an invigorating and lively atmosphere.
For drinks, I started with The Fennel which was really good, but the showstopper was Greg's creation which will soon be featured, "The Cucumber". It was fire and aesthetically pleasing!
I like that you have an option for either the a la carte menu or the tasting menu and I chose the tasting menu and added on the pumpkin kouign-amann. The dishes were all delicious except I was not too crazy about the rutabaga tagliatelle.
Olmsted is truly a neighborhood gem and not to be overlooked.
Nice place, with ok service and pretentious food that sounds interesting but doesn't actually taste good.

In a world where excessive tipping culture is holding us all hostage and making us furious, I was happy to leave 30% for my server. 

Just eat that they tell you to. They know what they're talking about. 

I'm still dreaming of their magical bread, foamy gnocchi, and stiff cherry cocktails.

Such an incredible experience, everything was wonderful. Each dish was so unique and delicious, especially the scallop crudo, and sitting at the chefs counter you get a behind the scenes view that's to die for. The staff (especially our server Kayleigh!) was all lovely, the meal beautiful, and we hope to be back soon!
Had a lovely time at Olmsted! All of the dishes were delicious - especially the scallop crudo! Kayleigh helped us and provided wonderful service. Definitely a must try if you're in Brooklyn!

I think it's a 3.5/5, New American that's a bit of a hit or miss situation. Carrot crepe and the squid ceviche are delicious. Thick-cut bacon cheese burger is well executed, but the key ingredient, beef patty, doesn't taste like high quality beef. I thought the pasta dish was real pasta with some decorative root vegetables, my bad, but the richness of cheese and truffle went wasted on those ribbon shaped rutabaga imo. Grilled monk fish was small in portion and the sauce was weird. Falafel w/ whipped honey was decent, even for someone who doesn't like falafel. I wish we had some bread to dip the remaining whipped honey with. Chocolate tart and banh mi were unmemorable. Wine list looks meh. We didn't order any of the cocktails although judging by the menu, some options look very clever and interesting. Service staff were kind and friendly, so four star.

Sat at the Chef's table for the Tasting Menu at Olmsted. An amazing meal while watching three talented chefs feed a whole restaurant on a busy Saturday night. The menu was 89 dollars and quite a good value for the quality of food and service. Small bites included, Tempura Broccolini with the most amazing sauce, Falafel with "whipped honey" and a liver pate take on a bahn mi sandwich. Don't miss the monk fish or the rutabaga tagliatelle! 
Service and atmosphere was great!

Middest meal of my life. We got the crab rangoon, leg of lamb, potato gnocchi, and monk fish. The only thing good here was the monk fish...

Crab rangoon was like so average. Nothing popped out from it, it was just painfully average. 

Potato gnocchi wasn't bad, a bit salty though

Leg of lamb was so gamey and tough, worst thing I had here. 

Service was great and ambiance was great but im not eating ambiance so this is mid af. I assume mid usually means 3 but i felt like it was also expensive and not that impressive so whatever
Banh Mi, monkfish, carrot crepe and lamb are to die for! One of our favorite neighborhood spots for dinner. But make a reservation.

Started out strong with small plates-watermelon sushi and falafel with whipped honey both dishes were confident, and expertly rendered. But as the service continued the quality of the dishes began to wane, the gnocchi was over cooked and the sauce was more of a thin parmesan broth. The flavor was there, but the textures were too mushaad and runny. The entrees were sadly just flat. The tomato schnitzel was too thick and under seasoned, had it been prepared as a fried green tomato is in the South it would sing with the accompanying condiments of chow chow and olive oil jam. The scallops had more interest with the corn and blueberry gastrique components, but it was far from perfect, and what was called corn pudding was really a sauce. Overall it was a pretty uneven service. It's a cool looking spot with phenomenal outdoor spaced in a great neighborhood, if they could tighten the service it could be a top tier experience. But it isn't. 

Oh i almost forgot to mention the froyo with whipped lavender honey, it was exactly the kind of dessert you want at the end of a meal. An unexpected delight. Light, refreshing and an excellent palate cleanse. The two courses that worked both had this whipped honey in them. It started strong and finished strong but the middle was just flabby and unexciting. Perhaps they will make some adjustments and improve the dining experience for future customers, but sadly it won't be me. NYC is too big and has many many great restaurants to try so there is absolutely no reason for me to return to a spot that didn't nail every course. Since smaller plates seem to be where they succeed perhaps they should consider a degustation menu.

The food at Olmsted is still basically good and the service is excellent. But Good God people, if you're going to sell me a $30 burger, don't offer me ketchup and tell me you don't have any mustard. It's 2024. Get a jar of Grey Poupon or something and keep it in your pantry. It'll last for years.
amazing drinks and amazing service! the cocktails are so good and the vibes are great. would highly recommend  sitting in the garden area as well.

The food was full of flavor that my taste thoroughly enjoyed. The watermelon sushi had quite the mix of flavors. The service was mixed we booked the dining room but was sat in the garden room. The vibe was great for dinner

Came here for my birthday on a Thursday night. Sat outside in the back and it was still comfortable out there in 62 degree weather. My personal favorite was the burger w/ the duck fat fries, and the carrot crepe. My boyfriend loved the kale & crab rangoon and the scallops (the sauce that came with the scallops was very spicy!) 
Overall, this was an excellent experience, and half of the reason I will be coming back is the wait staff alone. Our server Sofi made the night that much better! They were nice, helpful with suggestions, and so easy to talk to I wanted to pull up a chair and just have them join us. There was also a kind server with longer hair that has only been working there for 7 months (I wish I remembered their name!) They were very knowledgable about the menu and the restaurant as a whole! 
I had really wanted to try the s'mores dessert, but thought $22 was a steep price, until it all came out. The marshmallows and graham crackers were homemade, and being able to sit and roast a marshmallow in Brooklyn ... so unique and such a fun idea! Will definitely come back!
Slowest and most inattentive service I've received. Food was ok, certainly not worth the experience as a whole.

Comparing this unfortunate eatery to like-priced places and it receives my first and hopefully last single star review.  I spent over 600$ on a three person preset menu for Thanksgiving yesterday, including four drinks, two of which were lukewarm coffees.
My main concern was the poorly constructed meal, which seemed to scream "there was a glut of cheap salt at our supplier this week!" as every bit that could have salt included wayyy too much of what happens to be my favorite seasoning USUALLY.  My guests and I were also rather confused by all courses being shared, rather than individually portioned or served.  For example, the dessert came on a single plate alongside 3 spoons...smh!  Even the main course, salted salty saltlick-like turkey, was only slices on a singular plate for the three of us to politely share.
A less important callout is the inattentive, slowww service...add an apparent unwillingness to remove finished dishes to a presumed dearth of clean plates and, if it hadn't been a holiday, I would have left an offensively small tip.  
To make the trifecta of failure complete, the ambiance included a light timer system that went dim every 20 or so minutes and a 5 song soundtrack, which was repeated a few times in the 2 or so hours we were slogging through salt and slop and sloppiness.

Besides these three pillars of a restaurant not being well executed, I might recommend this spot for the foolishly brave and bored and spendthrifty crowd that needs to raise their blood pressure...

Food was outstanding.  Excellent and attentive staff.  Good wine list.  The meal was practically perfect.  Enjoyed the carrot crepe, kale crab Rangoon and rutabaga tagliatelle.  Rutabaga pasta -- a new experience!
Had a lovely time with friends. A bit pricey, but great for a special time/occasion. The food was very well done/presented.

We made reservations on the enclosed patio which was so gorgeous and very warm despite it being February. Our waiter David was probably the best server I had ever had. His timing was impeccable, he gave incredible suggestions and great banter- we were laughing with him all night. This is the kind of place you want to stay a couple of hours at.... AMAZING food that changes with the season (my favorite was the hamachi crisp and the duck pastrami). I had the blood orange cocktail which was absolutely delicious. Everything about our experience was incredible and exceeded our expectations. The kitchen even brought us multiple "gifts," free little dishes that only added to the experience. If you go, and you should, ask for David!!!! He's the best
